### `PO/Assumptions/ConsistencyLemmas.lean` — Pointwise consistency for `POVar`

Generalises the two pointwise consistency specialisations of `LATE.lean`
(`DofZ_eq_factualD_on_zEvent`, `factualY_eq_YofD_factualD`) to arbitrary
`POVar` pairs on distinct nodes.  Each lemma discharges the `Consistency.factual`
clause by reducing it to a singleton-regime agreement check.

| Declaration | Signature | Description | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POSystem.factualAgrees_empty` | `∀ ω, P.FactualAgrees Regime.empty ω` | Trivial base case: every `ω` factually agrees with the empty regime (target is `∅`) | **Proved** |
| `POSystem.factualAgrees_sqcup` | `{r₁ r₂ : Regime}`, `h : r₁.Disjoint r₂`, `P.FactualAgrees r₁ ω` → `P.FactualAgrees r₂ ω` → `P.FactualAgrees (r₁.sqcup r₂ h) ω` | Combinator: `FactualAgrees` for a disjoint union reduces componentwise. Lets theorem files assemble multi-target consistency hypotheses from per-variable pieces without hand-rolling a `Finset.mem_union` case split | **Proved** |
| `POVar.factualAgrees_single` | `(a : POVar P α) (x : α)`, `a.factual ω = x` → `P.FactualAgrees (Regime.single a.v (a.equiv.symm x)) ω` | Combinator: turns a factual equality `a.factual ω = x` into `FactualAgrees` for the singleton regime `{a.v ← a.equiv.symm x}`. Base case for building compound `FactualAgrees` via `factualAgrees_sqcup` | **Proved** |
| `POVar.cf_eq_factual_on_event` | `hC : P.Consistency`, `a w : POVar`, `a.v ≠ w.v`, `ω ∈ w.event y` → `a.cfUnder w y ω = a.factual ω` | Consistency of `a` under `{w ← y}`: on the event `{w = y}`, the `w`-intervened counterfactual of `a` equals the factual | **Proved** |
| `POVar.factual_eq_cfUnder_self_selected` | `hC : P.Consistency`, `a w : POVar`, `a.v ≠ w.v`, `∀ ω` → `a.factual ω = a.cfUnder w (w.factual ω) ω` | Pointwise: the factual equals the counterfactual under `{w ← factual w(ω)}` — the identity used to rewrite factual outcomes in terms of cf outcomes on the natural treatment choice | **Proved** |
| `POVar.factual_mul_indicator_eq_cfUnder_mul_indicator` | `hC : P.Consistency`, `a : POVar P ℝ`, `w : POVar P β`, `a.v ≠ w.v` → `(fun ω ↦ a.factual ω * 1_{w=y} ω) = (fun ω ↦ a.cfUnder w y ω * 1_{w=y} ω)` | Integrated form of consistency: multiplying by the indicator `1_{w=y}` lets factual and cf values be freely interchanged; workhorse of backdoor-style Step-1 rewrites | **Proved** |
| `POVar.factual_mul_indicator_eq_cfUnder_mul_indicator_fn` | `hC`, `y : POVar P ℝ`, `w : POVar P β`, `[MeasurableSingletonClass β]`, `y.v ≠ w.v` → `(fun ω ↦ y.factual ω * w.indicator x ω) = (fun ω ↦ y.cfUnder w x ω * w.indicator x ω)` | Pointwise-function variant matching the new `POVar.indicator` shape; one-line reduction to the `Set.indicator` form above. Used by backdoor/Manski/frontdoor/DTR Step-1 rewrites | **Proved** |
| `POVar.cf_eq_factual_of_factualAgrees` | `hC : P.Consistency`, `a : POVar P α`, `r : Regime`, `a.v ∉ r.target`, `P.FactualAgrees r ω` → `a.cf r ω = a.factual ω` | **Multi-target** consistency: pointwise, `a`'s counterfactual under any regime `r` (not naming `a.v`) coincides with its factual at every `ω` that factually agrees with `r`. Generalises `cf_eq_factual_on_event` from singleton to arbitrary regimes | **Proved** |
| `POVar.factual_mul_indicator_eq_cf_mul_indicator` | `hC : P.Consistency`, `a : POVar P ℝ`, `r : Regime`, `a.v ∉ r.target`, `E : Set P.Ω`, `(∀ ω ∈ E, P.FactualAgrees r ω)` → `(fun ω ↦ a.factual ω * 1_E ω) = (fun ω ↦ a.cf r ω * 1_E ω)` | **Multi-target** integrated consistency: on any event `E` of full factual agreement with `r`, the factual outcome and the multi-target counterfactual outcome are interchangeable inside `a · 1_E`. Generalises `factual_mul_indicator_eq_cfUnder_mul_indicator` to arbitrary regimes; consumed directly by `cdtr_backdoor` Step 1 | **Proved** |
| `POVar.eventCondExp_cfUnder_eq_factual_on_event` | `hC : P.Consistency`, `y : POVar P ℝ`, `a : POVar P β`, `y.v ≠ a.v` → `eventCondExp μ (a.event a₀) (y.cfUnder a a₀) = eventCondExp μ (a.event a₀) y.factual` | Consistency-on-event for `eventCondExp`: on the stratum `{a = a₀}`, the `{a ← a₀}`-counterfactual and the factual have the same event-level conditional mean. Shared rewrite in `Manski/{MTR,MTS}` and (via the `Fintype` total law below) the integrated MIV bounds; lives in `EventCondExp.lean` alongside the other `eventCondExp` tooling | **Proved** |

### `PO/Conditioning/Bundle.lean` — Bundle-conditioned conditional expectation

Lifts the single-`POVar` conditioning machinery in `CondExpTooling.lean` to a
`POCFBundle`, i.e. conditioning on the *joint* cf-value map of a tuple of
regimed variables.  The conditioning σ-algebra `B.sigma` is
`MeasurableSpace.comap B.jointValue inferInstance`.  Used by the multi-stage
DTR / sequential-backdoor identification arguments (`PO/ID/Exact/DTR/`)
where the conditioning σ-algebra is generated by a *bundle* of covariates rather
than a single one; mirrors all the lemmas of `POVar.condExpGiven` /
`POVar.condExpRatio` at the bundle level.

| `POCFBundle.integrable_condExpGiven` | `Integrable (B.condExpGiven g μ) μ` | `condExpGiven g` is integrable | **Proved** |
| `POCFBundle.condExpGiven_tower_of_le` | `m ≤ B.sigma → [SigmaFinite (μ.trim _)] → μ[B.condExpGiven g μ \| m] =ᵐ[μ] μ[g \| m]` | Tower property against an arbitrary smaller sub-σ-algebra `m ≤ B.sigma`; bundle analogue of `POVar.condExpGiven_tower_of_le` | **Proved** |

### `PO/Conditioning/EventCondExp.lean` — Event-level conditional expectation and drop-of-conditioning

Thin wrapper around `∫_A g ∂μ / (μ A).toReal` paired with a **drop-of-conditioning**
lemma: when the event-defining variable is `IndepCF` of a bundle `B`,
conditioning on a `value = x` event has no effect on `∫ h ∘ B.jointValue`.
Both multiplied and quotient forms are provided.

Lifts the single-period `EventCondExp` workhorse to the bundle-conditional setting (`P.CondIndepCFBundle a B C`) used by the Dynamic LATE bridges.  Per-stage workhorse: under bundle-conditional independence + consistency-on-event, the bundle conditional expectation of `factualF · 1_{a=x}` factors into the conditional expectation of `h ∘ B.jointValue` times the conditional expectation of `1_{a=x}`.

quantile. Gives meaning to "the `τ`-quantile of `Y(d)`"; input to the QTE
(`PO/ID/Exact/QTE/QuantileEffect.lean`). Builds on `Stat/Quantile/Quantile.lean`.

| `POVar.cfCDF a r μ` | `StieltjesFunction ℝ` | Distributional potential outcome `F_{a(r)} = cdf (a.cfLaw r μ)`. | **Defined** |

## 9. `SCM/ID/Identifiable.lean` — Identifiability

Namespace: `Causalean.SCM.ID`.

### Identifiability definitions

Identifiability is phrased in terms of **measure-theoretic observational
equivalence** against the SCM observational kernel: `obsEquiv M₁ M₂` is
`HEq` of `Causalean.SCM.obsKernel M₁` and `Causalean.SCM.obsKernel M₂` (the `HEq`
is necessary because `obsKernel` has dependent domain/codomain via
`FixedValues M` and `ObservedValues M`).

| Definition | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `CausalQuery` | `SCM N Ω → α` | Functional of a gSCM (ATE, LATE, interventional law, etc.) |
| `obsEquiv` | `SCM N Ω → SCM N Ω → Prop` | `HEq (SCM.obsKernel M₁) (SCM.obsKernel M₂)` |
| `Identifiable` | `SWIGGraph N → CausalQuery N Ω α → Prop` | Same SWIG graph (`M.toSWIGGraph = G`, pinning observed/latent/fixed + edges) + `obsEquiv` ⟹ same query value. Faithful to `def:scm-identifiability` (model class shares a SWIG graph, not merely a DAG) |
| `NonIdentifiable` | `SWIGGraph N → CausalQuery N Ω α → Prop` | Negation of `Identifiable` |
| `IdentifiableUnder` | `SWIGGraph N → Af → As → CausalQuery N Ω α → Prop` | Identifiable given functional (`Af`) and structural (`As`) assumption predicates over `SCM N Ω`, within the model class sharing SWIG graph `G` |

### Theorems

| Theorem | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `nonIdentifiable_iff` | Non-identifiability iff there exist two models with the same SWIG graph and `obsEquiv` but different query values | Equivalence characterization of non-identifiability |
| `identifiable_eq_identifiableUnder_true` | Identifiability without assumptions is the special case `Af = As = fun _ => True` | Links unconditional identifiability to `IdentifiableUnder` with trivial assumptions |
| `identifiableUnder_mono` | Stronger assumptions `(Af₂, As₂)` that imply `(Af₁, As₁)` preserve identifiability | Monotonicity: identifiability under weaker assumptions follows from identifiability under stronger ones |

## 9a. `SCM/ID/Overlap.lean` — Rule 2 / backdoor overlap predicate

The kernel-level absolute-continuity overlap predicate consumed by the
kernel-native do-calculus Rule 2 and the backdoor / frontdoor identification
theorems.  (The quantitative small-value/weak-overlap rate analysis — polynomial
lower-tail inverse moments — is developed separately under `Stat/PolynomialTail/`.)

| Definition | Signature | Description | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Rule2JointOverlap M' Z hZ_obs hZ_fixed W hZrW s'` | `Prop` | **Canonical Rule 2 overlap.** Absolute continuity `((M'.fixSet Z).obsKernel s').map π_{Zr∪W} ≪ (M'.obsKernel ∘ fixSetProj s').map π_{Zr∪W}` — a kernel-level AC predicate with no pointwise singleton positivity requirement. Holds trivially in the discrete case; holds in the continuous case whenever the SCM's structural functions are measurable and latents match. Hypothesis of `obsCondKernel_fixSet_eq_ae_witness` (canonical posterior witness-kernel Rule 2) and through it of `do_rule2_kernel` and backdoor / frontdoor identification. | Complete |

Reference: Basic Concepts.tex, Definition 2.12 (Overlap assumption).

---

## 9b. Structural Assumption Ownership

Causalean no longer carries a standalone IV/DID/RDD/proxy assumption catalogue.
Structural assumptions are owned by the theorem module that consumes them
(`PO/ID/Exact/*`, `PO/ID/Partial/*`, or downstream CausalSmith artifacts), while
`SCM/ID/Identifiable.lean` still provides generic `Prop`-valued assumption slots
for abstract identifiability statements.

---

## 9c. `SCM/ID/GraphicalThms/` — Graphical Identification Theorems

Formalizes Basic Concepts.tex §4.1.  Several live files:

* `InducedSubgraph.lean` — graph-only utilities (ancestral closure,
  proper-descendant / non-descendant sets in `G_R`).
* `CComponentFactor.lean` — c-factor definition (`qFactor`),
  c-component parent helpers, and the per-node chain-rule factorization
  theorem `M.obsKernel s = M.qFactorProduct s` (Tian full-history
  convention).
* `QFactorIdentity.lean` — Tian's Q-factor identity (Prop 2.19),
  intervention-target simplification (`fact4`), and the district-id
  corollary.  The Q-factor identity is currently formalized as the
  real marginal fixing identity obtained from Rule 3 and
  `induce_marginal_compat`; the final conditional-`qFactor` reindexing
  remains future work.

The old kernel-era files (`Fixable.lean`, `FixingStep.lean`,
`CFactor.lean`) are **archived** under
`archive/SCM/ID/GraphicalThms/`.  The Shpitser–Pearl c-component
recursion (the chosen design path for the Session-5 ID algorithm) does
not consume the fixing-step machinery, so it is no longer in the build.

### `CComponentFactor.lean` — c-component factorization (Tian, 2002)

Formalizes `thm:scm-c-factor` (Basic Concepts.tex:662–672) against
`obsKernel`.  The Pa⁺ semantics is the standard Tian (2002) convention:
*topological predecessors*, i.e. observed nodes preceding `v` in a fixed
topological order — not the direct-parent set.

| Definition / Statement | Description |
|---|---|
| `SWIGGraph.observedPredecessors v` | `Pa⁺_G(v) := {w ∈ G.observed | topoOrder w < topoOrder v}` |
| `SWIGGraph.qFactorParents C` | `(⋃_{v ∈ C} Pa⁺_G(v)) \ C` — conditioning set of `Q[C]` |
| `observedPredecessors_subset_observed` / `qFactorParents_subset_observed` | sanity lemmas (proven) |
| `SCM.qFactor M C hC s` | Tian's c-component factor `Q[C]` as a slice of `obsCondKernel M C (qFactorParents C)` at `s` (via `Kernel.comap`); requires `StandardBorelSpace`, `Nonempty`, `IsFiniteMeasure`, `CountableOrCountablyGenerated` instances |
| `SCM.c_component_factorization` | `M.obsKernel s = M.qFactorProduct s`; per-node chain-rule factorization over observed nodes, now sorry-free via `obsKernel_eq_qFactorProduct`; c-component grouping is deferred to a later theorem |

conditional q-factor equality (a.e. under the induced parent marginal), the
marginal fixing identity is retained as a proved helper, and fact4 is an

### `Density/ReferenceMeasure.lean` — dominated-model density foundation

Namespace `Causalean.SCM`. Foundation for the **density-assisted** c-component
factorization: Tian's assembly `P(v) = ∏_C Q[C]` is a commutative regrouping of
scalar density factors with no kernel-composition analogue, so the
`doKernelY` identification (obligation 2) is routed through the joint density.
Unifies discrete (counting reference) and continuous (Lebesgue reference) models.

| Definition / Theorem | Signature / Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ReferenceMeasures Ω` | structure: `μ : ∀ v, Measure (swigΩ Ω v)` + per-node `SigmaFinite` | A σ-finite reference measure per SWIG-node value space (counting for discrete, Lebesgue for continuous) |
| `ReferenceFaithful ref` | `∀ v x, ref.μ v {x} ≠ 0` | Full-support condition for finite references; counting reference measures satisfy it |
| `jointRef ref I` | `Measure (ValuesOn I (swigΩ Ω))` | Finite product `Measure.pi` of the per-node references over a node set `I` |
| `DominatedObs M ref` | `∀ s, M.obsKernel s ≪ jointRef ref M.observed` | The gSCM's observational law is absolutely continuous w.r.t. the joint reference (admits a density) |
| `obsDensity M ref s` | `ValuesOn M.observed (swigΩ Ω) → ℝ≥0∞` | Joint observational density `(obsKernel s).rnDeriv (jointRef …)` |
| `withDensity_obsDensity_eq` | `DominatedObs M ref → (jointRef …).withDensity (obsDensity …) = obsKernel s` | Density determines the law (Proved) |

### `Density/FiniteReference.lean` — finite discrete reference infrastructure

Namespace `Causalean.SCM`. Instances and helpers for the finite/discrete density
path: when every base-node value space is finite and has measurable singletons,
the SWIG value spaces and finite product references inherit the corresponding
finite/measurable structure needed by the finite-reference RN chain rule.

|---|---|---|
| `instFintypeSwigΩ` / `instMeasurableSingletonClassSwigΩ` | `[∀ n, Fintype (Ω n)]` / `[∀ n, MeasurableSingletonClass (Ω n)]` ⟹ the same instances for `swigΩ Ω sn` | Transfers finite and singleton-measurable structure from base nodes to random/fixed SWIG nodes |
| `isFiniteMeasure_of_finite_measurableSingleton` | a σ-finite measure on a finite measurable-singleton type is finite | Generic finite-space measure helper, proved by covering the space with finitely many measurable singletons |
| `instIsFiniteMeasure_refMu` / `instIsFiniteMeasure_jointRef` | finite node spaces ⟹ `IsFiniteMeasure (ref.μ v)` and `IsFiniteMeasure (jointRef ref I)` | Supplies the finite fibre and finite product-reference instances used by discrete density proofs |
| `jointRef_singleton_ne_zero` / `absolutelyContinuous_jointRef_of_faithful` | `ReferenceFaithful ref` ⟹ every product singleton has nonzero `jointRef` mass, hence every measure on the finite coordinate product is `≪ jointRef ref I` | Full-support infrastructure used to prove do-law ancestral marginal domination |
| `aemeasurable_fiber_rnDeriv_of_finite` | any raw fibre RN selector `(κ p.1).rnDeriv ρ p.2` is a.e.-measurable on a finite measurable-singleton product | Discharges the explicit product a.e.-measurability hypothesis of the finite-reference composition-product RN lemma |

Namespace `Causalean.SCM`. The reference-splitting foundation for the density chain
rule: `Measure.pi` over a disjoint union of coordinates factors as a product.

| Definition / Theorem | Signature / Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `unionSumEquiv hDisj` | `({a // a ∈ A} ⊕ {b // b ∈ B}) ≃ {i // i ∈ A ∪ B}` | Index equivalence for disjoint `A`, `B` |
| `measurePreserving_valuesUnionEquiv` | `MeasurePreserving (valuesUnionEquiv hDisj) (Measure.pi μ_{A∪B}) ((Measure.pi μ_A).prod (Measure.pi μ_B))` | **`Measure.pi` over a disjoint union = the product measure.** Fully proved, axiom-clean; routes the project's union equiv through Mathlib `sumPiEquivProdPi` + `piCongrLeft` |

### `Density/ChainRuleDensity.lean` — observational chain-rule density

Namespace `Causalean.SCM`. Density analogue of the proven kernel chain rule:
the observational density is reduced to the scalar product of the
Radon--Nikodym derivatives of the one-node conditional kernels
`obsStepCondKernel`, evaluated along the observed topological order.

| Definition / Theorem | Signature / Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `obsStepCondDensity M ref s i` | `ValuesOn M.observed (swigΩ Ω) → ℝ≥0∞` | One observed-coordinate conditional density: the RN derivative of `obsStepCondKernel i.isLt` against the node reference measure, evaluated at the prefix and coordinate read from a full observed assignment |
| `qFactorDensityProduct M ref s` | `ValuesOn M.observed (swigΩ Ω) → ℝ≥0∞` | Product over `Fin M.observed.card` of the per-node conditional density factors in observed topological order |
| `qFactorProduct_rnDeriv_eq_qFactorDensityProduct` | with finite measurable-singleton node spaces, `DominatedObs M ref → (M.qFactorProduct s).rnDeriv (jointRef ref M.observed) =ᵐ … qFactorDensityProduct …` | Analytic RN-derivative chain rule. **The `DominatedObs` hypothesis is essential** — false without it (singular part ⟹ vanishing rnDeriv vs nonzero conditional-density product). Fully proved in the finite-reference setting |
| `obsChainKernel_rnDeriv_eq_prefixDensityProduct` | with finite measurable-singleton node spaces, general-`k` prefix induction: `(obsChainKernel k s).rnDeriv (jointRef prefix k) =ᵐ prefixDensityProduct k` | **Proved.** Base on `ValuesOn ∅`; successor peels `extendObsPrefix` via `MeasurableEmbedding.rnDeriv_map`, splits via `jointRef_extendObsPrefix`, derives joint product domination from base and fibre domination, and uses finite-space measurability for the raw fibre derivative |

| `obsChainKernel_absolutelyContinuous_jointRef_prefix` | `M.obsChainKernel k hk s ≪ jointRef ref (M.prefixNodes k)` | **Proved (no Mathlib gap).** Chain = prefix marginal of the dominated `obsKernel`; the reference marginal is a scalar multiple of the prefix reference via the disjoint-union split (`measurePreserving_valuesUnionEquiv`) + `Measure.map_fst_prod` |
| `rnDeriv_compProd_prod_sigmaFinite` | `(μ ⊗ₘ κ).rnDeriv (ν.prod ρ) =ᵐ fun p => f p.1 * (κ p.1).rnDeriv ρ p.2`, for finite `μ`/`ρ`/`κ`, σ-finite `ν`, `μ ≪ ν`, **joint domination** `μ ⊗ₘ κ ≪ ν.prod ρ`, product a.e.-measurability of the raw fibre derivative, and `μ.rnDeriv ν =ᵐ f` | Finite-reference composition-product RN identity in `Causalean/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/RnDerivCompProdSigmaFinite.lean`. Finiteness of `ρ` makes `Kernel.const _ ρ` a finite kernel, so Mathlib extracts μ-a.e. fibre domination from joint domination. The raw `Measure.rnDeriv` fibre representative still carries an explicit product-measurability hypothesis; Mathlib's measurable representative is `Kernel.rnDeriv κ (Kernel.const _ ρ)` |
| `map_pi_valuesEquivOfEq`, `jointRef_prefix_card_map`, `singletonValues_map_ref_eq_jointRef`, `jointRef_extendObsPrefix`, `rnDeriv_compProd_same_left`, `absolutelyContinuous_of_map_measurableEmbedding`, `qFactorProduct_rnDeriv_eq_obsChainKernel_card_pullback_of_jointRef`, `obsChainKernel_card_rnDeriv_pullback_eq_qFactorDensityProduct_of_prefix` | reference reindex / singleton split / per-step `extendObsPrefix` reference split / embedding-pullback of `≪` / `rnDeriv_map` peels / a.e. transport | The transport + reference-split sub-lemmas of the chain rule — **all proved, axiom-clean** |
| `obsDensity_eq_qFactorDensityProduct` | with finite measurable-singleton node spaces, `M.obsDensity ref s =ᵐ[jointRef ref M.observed] M.qFactorDensityProduct ref s` | Dominated observational density factors as the product of one-node conditional densities; D1 is now sorry-free in the finite-reference setting |

### `Density/CComponentDensity.lean` — c-component regrouping of the density

Namespace `Causalean.SCM`. The commutative regrouping with **no kernel analogue**:
the scalar density product is collected by c-component. (Composed kernels can't
be permuted to gather a non-contiguous c-component's factors; scalar densities
can.)

| Definition / Theorem | Signature / Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `cComponentDensityFactor M ref s C` | `ValuesOn M.observed (swigΩ Ω) → ℝ≥0∞` | Product of the one-node conditional density factors over the observed indices whose node lies in c-component `C` (density analogue of Tian's `Q[C]`) |
| `qFactorDensityProduct_eq_prod_cComponentFactor` | `M.qFactorDensityProduct ref s x = ∏ C ∈ cComponentSet, cComponentDensityFactor … C x` | The chain-rule density product regroups as a product over c-components. **Fully proved, axiom-clean** (pure `Finset.prod_fiberwise` regrouping; the kernel-impossible step) |

## 10b. `SCM/Examples/BackDoor.lean` — Backdoor Adjustment Example

Demonstrates the backdoor criterion DAG:

```
    Z
   ↙ ↘
  D → Y
```

Observed: D (treatment), Y (outcome), Z (observed confounder). Latent roots U₁, U₂, U₃ added to satisfy `unobs_are_roots`.

**What it tests:**

| Module | Tests |
|---|---|
| `Graph/DAG.lean` | `parents`, `isRoot`, `isAncestor` (irreflexivity via `isAncestor_topoOrder_lt`) |
| `Graph/DSep.lean` | `dSep` for the observational graph; no d-separation by {Z} (direct edge D → Y remains open) |
| `Graph/SWIG.lean` | `SWIGGraph` construction with three latent roots; `swig_random_root_of_root` for each |
| `Graph/SWIGSplitMono.lean` | Backdoor condition (ii): `splitMonoDAG {bdD}` d-separates Y from D given Z, verified by `native_decide` on the computable `splitMonoDAG` |
| `Graph/CComponents.lean` | Each observed node is its own singleton C-component (no confounding) |
| `SCM/Model/EdgeType.lean` | `allNonparametric` edge type assignment |

The file now additionally demonstrates the full `bdSWIG.backdoorCriterion` on this concrete 3-node DAG.  Condition (i) (no `z ∈ Z` is a descendant of any `random D ∈ X`) is discharged by `native_decide` + `simp`.  Condition (ii) is routed through `splitMonoDAG` (since `splitMono` itself is `noncomputable`) and also closed by `native_decide`.  No full SCM is built — only the graphical criterion is exercised.

## 10c. `SCM/Examples/ContinuousBackdoor.lean` — Linear-Gaussian backdoor (continuous treatment)

Validation of the posterior witness-kernel backdoor pipeline: a 3-node SCM with continuous value spaces (`ℝ`) on every observed node, exercising `backdoor_completeness_ae` end-to-end on a treatment variable that is *not* discrete.

DAG: `Z → X`, `Z → Y`, `X → Y` (so `Z` is a backdoor-admissible confounder for the effect of `X` on `Y`).  All three observed nodes have value space `ℝ` (via `CBΩ : Fin 3 → Type := fun _ => ℝ`).  The latent set is empty, so the SCM is fully deterministic — the kernel-native pipeline does not need probabilistic latents to demonstrate the continuous-treatment regime; what matters is the continuity of the value spaces.

The example uses a *computable* SWIGGraph (`cbSWIGGraph`) so the backdoor criterion can be discharged via `native_decide` even though the parent `SCM` is `noncomputable` (carries `Measure`s).  `continuousBackdoorSCM.toSWIGGraph := cbSWIGGraph` definitionally.

| Declaration | Description |
|---|---|
| `CBNode`, `CBΩ` | Node set `Fin 3` (`Zidx = 0`, `Xidx = 1`, `Yidx = 2`) with continuous value spaces `ℝ` |
| `cbEdgeBool`, `cbEdge`, `cbDAG` | Edge relation (`Bool`-lifted for `decide`-friendly `Decidable`) and underlying DAG |
| `cbSWIGGraph` | Computable SWIGGraph (empty latents, `observed = {Z, X, Y}` as `.random` nodes), used for graphical criterion proofs |
| `continuousBackdoorSCM` | The full SCM: extends `cbSWIGGraph`, constant-`0` structural functions, empty `latentDist`.  Marked `noncomputable` only because of the `Measure` API in the SCM structure |
| `cb_Xrand_obs`, `cb_Xfixed` | Witnesses that `random X` is observed and `fixed X` is not in `fixed`; supplied to `backdoor_completeness_ae`'s subset-hypotheses |
| `cb_backdoor_criterion` | Discharges `cbSWIGGraph.backdoorCriterion {X} _ _ {Y} {Z}`.  Condition (i) (`Z` not descendant of `X`) by `native_decide`; condition (ii) (d-separation in splitMono) by `native_decide` on the computable `splitMonoDAG` |

**What this validates.**  Continuous value spaces (`ℝ`) flow through the kernel-native pipeline (`obsKernel`, `obsCondKernel`, `Rule2JointOverlap`, `backdoor_completeness_ae`), and `SWIGGraph.backdoorCriterion` discharges by `native_decide` on the continuous SCM.  This example is sorry-free.

## 9d. `SCM/ID/Adjustment.lean` — Adjustment Functionals

Graph-level adjustment functionals that turn an SCM's observational
kernel into a post-intervention `Y`-marginal kernel under the backdoor
or frontdoor criterion.  The split into a *single-SCM completeness*
lemma plus a *cross-SCM congruence* lemma factors the cross-SCM HEq
plumbing out of the do-calculus assembly in `SCM/ID/Backdoor.lean` /
`PO/ID/Exact/Frontdoor.lean`.

| Definition / Statement | Description |
|---|---|
| `SCM.backdoorAdjustment M X hX_obs hX_fixed Y Z hY hZ` | Kernel `Kernel (M.fixSet X).FixedValues (ValuesOn Y _)` implementing `∫_z P(Y \| X, Z=z) dP(z)` as a kernel-native `((zMarginalPost ⊗ₖ M.obsCondKernel Y (X.image .random ∪ Z)).comap ...).map Prod.snd` chain.  The conditional's `(X.image .random ∪ Z)`-argument is assembled via `M.fillZrW X hX_obs hX_fixed Z s_post z`, which fills the `X.image .random` slice from `s_post` (reindexed from `X.image .fixed` through `zFixedAsRandom`) and pairs it with the outer `Z`-value `z` — routing through `fillZrW` (rather than an inline `valuesUnionMk ∘ zFixedAsRandom ∘ valuesProjection`) removes a reindexing-bridge gap in the downstream backdoor completeness proof.  Signature carries `[StandardBorelSpace (ValuesOn Y (swigΩ Ω))]`, `[Nonempty (ValuesOn Y (swigΩ Ω))]`, `[∀ s : M.FixedValues, IsFiniteMeasure (M.obsKernel s)]`, and a `CountableOrCountablyGenerated` instance for the conditional kernel |
| `SCM.frontdoorAdjustment M X hX_obs hX_fixed Y Z hY hZ` | **Proved** (sorry-free).  Kernel `Kernel (M.fixSet X).FixedValues (ValuesOn Y _)` implementing the frontdoor integral as a chain of `⊗ₖ` legs: outer X-marginal `(M.obsKernel.map projXr).comap fixSetProj`, middle `M.obsCondKernel Z (X.image .random)` (Rule 2 leg, `P(Z|X)`), inner `M.obsCondKernel Y (X.image .random ∪ Z)` (Rule 2 leg on inner `do(Z)`, with `X` as adjustment set).  The three kernels compose to `((xMarginal ⊗ₖ zCondX) ⊗ₖ yCondXZ).map Prod.snd`.  Signature requires `[StandardBorelSpace (ValuesOn Y _)]`, `[StandardBorelSpace (ValuesOn Z _)]`, `[Nonempty (ValuesOn Y _)]`, `[Nonempty (ValuesOn Z _)]`, `[StandardBorelSpace (ValuesOn (X.image .random) _)]`, `[StandardBorelSpace (ValuesOn (X.image .random ∪ Z) _)]`, `[∀ s, IsFiniteMeasure (M.obsKernel s)]`, and two `CountableOrCountablyGenerated` instances for the conditional kernels |
| `SCM.backdoorAdjustment_invariant` | **Proved** (sorry closed).  HEq cross-SCM invariance: two SCMs sharing `toSWIGGraph` and `obsKernel` produce the same `backdoorAdjustment` kernel.  Proof destructs both SCMs via `obtain`, `cases h_swig` unifies the SWIGGraph fields definitionally, then `apply heq_of_eq` reduces HEq to Eq. `eq_of_heq _h_obs` strips the obsKernel HEq; `unfold SCM.backdoorAdjustment` + nested `congr 1` peels off `.map Prod.snd` and `⊗ₖ`, leaving the `zMarginalPost` branch (closed by `rw [h_ok]`) and the `condPost` branch (closed by unfolding `obsCondKernel`/`obsCondPairKernel` and `rw [h_ok]`). Does not require `heq_obsCondKernel` — `cases h_swig` already aligns the kernel arguments |
| `SCM.frontdoorAdjustment_invariant` | **Proved** (sorry-free).  Same shape as `backdoorAdjustment_invariant`.  After destructure + `cases h_swig`, `unfold SCM.frontdoorAdjustment` exposes the `⊗ₖ` chain; unfolding `obsCondKernel`/`obsCondPairKernel` exposes the `condKernel`-of-`obsKernel.map`-joint pattern; `simp_rw [h_ok]` rewrites every `obsKernel` mention to the M₂-side, then `rfl` closes the remaining proof-irrelevance noise on `fixSetProj` (only SWIGGraph fields are used in `fixSetProj`; all unified after `cases h_swig`) |

---

## 9e. `SCM/ID/BackdoorCriterion.lean` — Backdoor criterion + Rule-3 leg

The graphical backdoor criterion (Basic Concepts.tex:636–645, Pearl 2009
Theorem 3.3.2) and the single regime-independent do-calculus leg the backdoor
identification proof consumes.  The identification *theorems* live in
`SCM/ID/Backdoor.lean` (§9e').

**Design note on condition (ii).**  `Graph/Mutilation.lean` is not yet
implemented, so the lower-bar mutilation `G_{X̲}` is encoded via
`SWIGGraph.splitMono X hX_obs hX_fix`: splitting `X` reroutes outgoing
edges of `random D` (for `D ∈ X`) to root nodes `fixed D`, which is
exactly the effect of lower-bar mutilation for d-separation purposes.

| Declaration | Description | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `SWIGGraph.backdoorCriterion G X hX_obs hX_fix Y Z` | Two-condition criterion: (i) no `z ∈ Z` is a descendant of any `random D` with `D ∈ X` in `G`; (ii) `Z ∪ X.image .fixed` d-separates `Y` from `X.image .random` in `G.splitMono X hX_obs hX_fix` (encodes `G_{X̲}` d-sep; fixed_X conditioning is vacuous in splitMono but carried to match `do_rule2`'s shape) | Defined; type-checks without sorry |
| `SCM.backdoor_rule3_Z_marginal` | **Rule-3 leg**: under criterion (i), `((M.fixSet X).obsKernel s_post).map proj_Z = (M.obsKernel (fixSetProj s_post)).map proj_Z`. Applies `do_rule3` with `Y_param := ∅`, `W_param := Z` and bridges `hNoDesc` via `fixSet_isAncestor_fixed_forward`. Consumed by `backdoor_completeness_ae`. | **Proved** |

## 9e'. `SCM/ID/Backdoor.lean` — Backdoor Identification (continuous, a.e.)

The sound **continuous-treatment** backdoor results, stated a.e. in the
treatment value (so they never read `obsCondKernel`/`backdoorAdjustment` on a
`{X = x}` null slice).  Built on the posterior witness-kernel Rule 2
(`condDistrib_fixSet_cross_SCM_bridge`).  Headline theorems
`backdoor_completeness_ae` and `backdoor_identifiable_ae`.

| Declaration | Description | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `SCM.treatmentMarginal M X hXr s0` | The observational treatment marginal `νX = (M.obsKernel s0).map π_{X.random}` — the supported measure the a.e. statements are anchored at | Defined |
| `SCM.BackdoorPositivityAE M X Z … s0` | Product positivity / overlap `Prop`: `νX ⊗ μZ ≪ μ_{X.rand ∪ Z}` (the standard continuous-treatment positivity; vacuous-free, covers both atomic and non-atomic regimes) | Defined |
| `SCM.doKernelY M X … Y hY s0` | Post-intervention `Y`-marginal as a kernel in the treatment value `t`: `t ↦ ((M.fixSet X).obsKernel (extend s0 t)).map π_Y`. Type `Kernel (ValuesOn (X.image .random)) (ValuesOn Y)` — independent of `M`'s fixed values | Defined |
| `SCM.adjustmentKernelY M X … Y Z hY hZ s0` | Backdoor-adjustment `Y`-marginal as a kernel in the treatment value: `(M.backdoorAdjustment …).comap (fixSetExtend s0)` | Defined |
| `SCM.backdoor_completeness_ae_compProd M X … s0 hOverlap hPositivity` | `νX ⊗ₘ doKernelY = νX ⊗ₘ adjustmentKernelY` at base `s0`, under backdoor criterion + joint overlap + `BackdoorPositivityAE`. The compProd (joint) primary form — well-posed for continuous treatment (never reads `obsCondKernel` on a null slice) | **Proved** (sorry-free) |
| `SCM.backdoor_completeness_ae M X … s0 hOverlap hPositivity` | **Continuous backdoor completeness (a.e.).** For `νX`-a.e. treatment value `t`, `doKernelY … t = adjustmentKernelY … t`. Derived from the compProd form via `Kernel.ae_eq_of_compProd_eq`. **Headline.** | **Proved** (sorry-free) |
| `SCM.backdoor_identifiable_ae M₁ M₂ h_swig X Y Z … h_obs h_s0` | **Continuous backdoor identifiability (a.e., cross-SCM).** Two SCMs sharing the SWIG graph (`h_swig`) and observational kernel (`h_obs : HEq …`) with aligned base points (`h_s0 : HEq s0₁ s0₂`) produce `doKernelY M₁ s0₁ =ᵐ[treatmentMarginal M₁ s0₁] doKernelY M₂ s0₂`. A plain `=ᵐ` (not HEq) since `doKernelY` is `M`-fixed-value-independent. Proof: `backdoor_completeness_ae` on each side + cross-SCM `adjustmentKernelY` invariance (`backdoorAdjustment_invariant` after destructure + `cases h_swig`/`h_s0`). **Headline.** | **Proved** (sorry-free) |

abstraction layer introduced in `PO/`: counterfactual maps are built
as `POVar` (`zVar`, `dVar`, `yVar`), single-node interventions as

`cfTuple` / `measurable_cfTuple` / `indepFun_factualZ_cfTuple` /
`integral_zEvent_of_cfTuple` scaffolding in favour of direct
`POCFBundle.jointValue` usage.

## 9f'. `PO/ID/Exact/HeckmanRoy/{Setup,Wald}.lean` — Heckman–Vytlacil IV / Generalized Roy Selection Model (PO framework)

Formalises the Heckman–Vytlacil IV / generalized Roy selection model from `Basic Concepts.tex` (def:po-iv-heckman-roy-system, def:po-iv-heckman-roy-assumptions, def:po-iv-heckman-roy-late, prop:po-iv-heckman-roy-wald, rem:po-iv-heckman-roy-lean). Generalises `LATE.lean` to:

* an arbitrary measurable instrument value space `α` (with `MeasurableSingletonClass`), instead of `Bool` — same parametrization pattern as `Manski/Setup.lean`;
* a latent uniform rank `U : Ω → ℝ` (`U ~ Unif[0,1]`) plus a propensity map `p : α → ℝ`, replacing the binary `D` potentials and monotonicity by threshold crossing `D(z) = 1_{U ≤ p(z)}`;
* a **pairwise** Wald identity: for any `z₀, z₁ : α` with `p z₀ < p z₁` and positive measure on `{Z = z₀}, {Z = z₁}`,
  `(E[Y|Z=z₁] − E[Y|Z=z₀]) / (E[D|Z=z₁] − E[D|Z=z₀]) = LATE(z₀, z₁)`.

**Out of scope (follow-ups):** the marginal treatment effect `MTE` (def:po-iv-heckman-roy-mte) and the continuous-Z / regression-representative formulation (rem:po-iv-heckman-roy-local-iv); both need the `IsRegressionFunction` infrastructure of `PO/Analysis/Regression.lean` to extend to non-singleton instruments.

## 9f''. `PO/ID/Exact/DynamicLATE/{Setup,Consistency,Bridges,WhenToTreat}.lean` — Two-Period Dynamic LATE (PO framework)

Formalises the two-period dynamic IV/LATE identification of Sojitra (2025) in the bare potential-outcome framework: `subsec:po-dynamic-late`, `def:po-dynamic-late-system`, `def:po-dynamic-late-assumptions`, `def:po-dynamic-late`, `def:po-dynamic-late-observable-functionals`, `prop:po-dynamic-late-when-to-treat`, `rem:po-dynamic-late-bridge`, `rem:po-dynamic-late-lean`. Generalises `LATE.lean` to two periods with sequential encouragements `Z₁,Z₂`, noncompliant treatments `D₁,D₂`, baseline state `S₀ : POVar P γ₀`, intermediate state `S₁ : POVar P γ₁`, and real outcome `Y`.

**Phase A scope.** Definitions, observable functionals, the assumption bundle, the four bridge identities of `rem:po-dynamic-late-bridge`, and the algebraic ratio identifications `whenToTreat_wald`, `mixtureLATE_wald`, plus the heterogeneous (`S₀`-conditional) versions. The bridge proofs and the structural composition-consistency rewrites are filled.

**Out of scope (Phase B):** `prop:po-dynamic-late-always-treat` and `cor:po-dynamic-late-staggered` (always-treat LATE under cross-period mean-independence / staggered-compliance). Will live in a future `AlwaysTreat.lean`.

**Status as of 2026-04-27 redesign.** The bridges are refactored around a per-stage workhorse (in `PO/Conditioning/EventCondExpBundle.lean`) and a layer of structural pointwise consistency rewrites (in `DynamicLATE/Consistency.lean`).  The Dynamic LATE files in this section typecheck with their local bridge and ratio proofs filled; remaining proof debt, if any, is inherited only from broader project-wide Mathlib/measure-theory stubs already documented elsewhere.

**Setup.lean** also gained:

* Helpers `encouragementRegime_disjoint_treatmentRegime` and `encTreatRegime`.

## 9g. `PO/ID/Exact/ATE.lean` — Backdoor ATE Identification Theorem (PO framework)

Formalizes the standard backdoor-adjustment identification of the average treatment effect at the potential-outcome level. Mirrors the structure of `LATE.lean` but uses σ-algebra conditional expectations (instead of event-based `eventCondExp`) because the adjustment variable `X` is continuous. The covariate type `γ` is an arbitrary measurable space, so the file simultaneously handles discrete/continuous/vector-valued `X` (e.g. `γ := ℝⁿ`).

Core identity (CATE level):

    μ[Y(d) | σ(X)]  =ᵐ[μ]  μ[Y · 1_{D=d} | σ(X)] / P[D=d | σ(X)].

Integrated corollary: `ATE = adjustedATE`.

### Regression-adjustment: the adjustment functional is an observable regression

Third beat of the identification story (after `cate_backdoor`, `ate_backdoor`): `adjustedCE d` — the σ(X)-stratified adjustment functional — equals the **observable outcome regression** `E[Y | D=d, X]`, a functional of the observed law of `(X,D,Y)` only (overlap, NO unconfoundedness). Certifies that the back-door nuisance `μ` is a genuine regression problem (the one `ML/Causal/RegressionBridge.lean` solves). Heavy step factored into the reusable Mathlib kernel `condExp_setIndicator_condExp_of_le` (§10k').

## 9g'. `PO/ID/Exact/ATT.lean` — Backdoor ATT Identification Theorem (PO framework)

Mirrors `PO/ID/Exact/ATE.lean` but identifies the **average treatment effect on the treated** (ATT). Reuses `POBackdoorSystem` (and its `Assumptions`/`adjustedCE`/`propScore`/`CATE`) verbatim. Adds the population-treated-fraction `propTreated`, the PO-level `ATT = E[A·(Y(1)−Y(0))] / π_T`, the observable outcome-regression form `adjustedATT = E[A·(μ₁(X)−μ₀(X))] / π_T`, an extended assumption bundle `ATTAssumptions` (adds `0 < propTreated`), and the AIPW corollary at the σ(X) representative level. The two main theorems delegate the heavy lifting to private helpers:

* **Outcome-regression numerator equality** (per arm `d`): `∫ A · Y(d) dμ = ∫ A · adjustedCE d dμ` — by tower over σ(X) and the unconfoundedness factorization `μ[A·Y(d)|σ(X)] = μ[A|σ(X)] · μ[Y(d)|σ(X)] = e(X)·CATE d`, then `cate_backdoor` to swap `CATE d ↦ adjustedCE d`. The σ(X)-measurable side does the same tower step on the OR side.
* **AIPW IPW-correction vanishing**: `∫ (1−A) · (e/(1−e)) · (Y − adjustedCE false) dμ = 0` — pull `e/(1−e)` (σ(X)-measurable) out of `μ[·|σ(X)]`, rewrite `(1−A)·Y = (1−A)·Y(false)` via consistency, factor by unconfoundedness, then collapse `(1−A)·Y(false) − (1−A)·adjustedCE false` because `μ[Y(false)|σ(X)] =ᵐ adjustedCE false`.
* **Treated-arm consistency rewrite**: `∫ A·(Y − adjustedCE false) dμ = ∫ A·(adjustedCE true − adjustedCE false) dμ` — apply the OR numerator equality at `d = true` to the `A·Y` piece (using `Y = A·Y(1) + (1−A)·Y(0)` consistency-collapsed to `A·Y = A·Y(1)` on the treated set).

| Declaration | Signature | Description | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POBackdoorSystem.propTreated S` | `ℝ` | Marginal treatment probability `π_T = E[1_{D=1}] = ∫ dVar.indicator true dμ` | **Defined** |
| `POBackdoorSystem.ATT S` | `ℝ` | PO-level ATT `(∫ A · (Y(true) − Y(false)) dμ) / π_T` | **Defined** |
| `POBackdoorSystem.adjustedATT S` | `ℝ` | Observable outcome-regression form `(∫ A · (adjustedCE true − adjustedCE false) dμ) / π_T` | **Defined** |
| `POBackdoorSystem.ATTAssumptions S` | `structure extends Assumptions S { propTreated_pos }` | Extended bundle: `Assumptions` + `0 < propTreated`. The `< 1` half of overlap (already in `Assumptions.overlap`) suffices for the AIPW corollary | **Defined** |
| `POBackdoorSystem.propScore_false_ae` | `S.propScore false =ᵐ[μ] (1 - S.propScore true)` | Indicator-pair sum identity transported through `μ[·|σ(X)]` (private) | **Proved** |
| `POBackdoorSystem.{stronglyMeasurable_adjustedCE_comap, measurable_adjustedCE, integrable_adjustedCE}` | various | σ(X)-strong-measurability, ambient measurability, and a.e. integrability of `adjustedCE d` (private; integrability via `cate_backdoor` transport from `CATE d = condExpGiven Y(d)`) | **Proved** |
| `POBackdoorSystem.att_numerator_arm` | `(hA : Assumptions S) (d) → ∫ A · Y(d) dμ = ∫ A · adjustedCE d dμ` | Per-arm OR numerator equality (private); fed by tower + `condExp_mul_of_condIndep` + `cate_backdoor` | **Proved** |
| `POBackdoorSystem.propScore_ne_zero` | `(hA : Assumptions) (d) → ∀ᵐ ω, propScore d ω ≠ 0` | Both-arm non-vanishing of propensity from `Assumptions.overlap` (mirrors the ATE helper) (private) | **Proved** |
| `POBackdoorSystem.condExp_indicator_residual_adjusted_zero` | `μ[(1−A) · (Y − adjustedCE false) | σ(X)] =ᵐ 0` | Residual zero-conditional-mean for the `A=0` arm using `adjustedCE false` (private) | **Proved** |
| `POBackdoorSystem.weighted_false_residual_integral_zero` | `∫ (1−A) · (e/(1−e)) · (Y − adjustedCE false) dμ = 0` (under `hIPW` integrability + `Assumptions`) | IPW-correction vanishing (private) | **Proved** |

| `POBackdoorSystem.ATT_eq_adjustedATT` | `(hA : ATTAssumptions S) → S.ATT = S.adjustedATT` | **Main ATT identification.** Reduces to numerator equality via `congr 1` (denominator `propTreated > 0`) and applies `att_numerator_arm` at `d = true, false` | **Proved** |

The extra `hIPW` integrability hypothesis is honest about the fact that `e/(1−e)` is unbounded under bare-positivity overlap; this is the standard registered hypothesis for the Hahn (1998) ATT IF | **Proved** |

## 9g''. `PO/ID/Exact/QTE/QuantileEffect.lean` — Backdoor Quantile Treatment Effect (Firpo 2007)

Marginal quantile treatment effect `QTE(τ) = F_{Y(1)}⁻¹(τ) − F_{Y(0)}⁻¹(τ)`
under Firpo (2007) ignorability: unconfoundedness + common support (`0 < e_d < 1`,
in `Assumptions`; strict overlap is *not* an identification assumption). Reuses
`POBackdoorSystem` (binary `D`, real `Y`, covariate `X`) and its `Assumptions`
from §9g; covariates enter only in identification, not the estimand (standard
marginal QTE). The quantile layer makes QTE a *functional of the two
potential-outcome laws*: once those laws are identified by observable measures,
QTE is the difference of their quantiles.

| Declaration | Signature | Description | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
The distributional engine (`ipwDensity`, `ipwLaw`, `cfUnderLaw_eq_ipwLaw`) lives
in `DistributionalBackdoor.lean` (§9g''b) and is imported here; this file is the quantile
layer on top.

| Declaration | Signature | Description | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POBackdoorSystem.qtdQuantile S d μ τ` | `ℝ` | `τ`-quantile of `Y(d)` (`yVar.cfUnderQuantile dVar d`). | **Defined** |
| `POBackdoorSystem.qte S μ τ` | `ℝ` | QTE estimand `F_{Y(1)}⁻¹(τ) − F_{Y(0)}⁻¹(τ)`. | **Defined** |
| `POBackdoorSystem.qtdQuantile_eq_quantile_cfUnderLaw` | `= Stat.quantile (cfUnderLaw …) τ` | Quantile of `Y(d)` = quantile of its law. | `rfl` |
| `POBackdoorSystem.qte_eq_of_law_eq` | `cfUnderLaw … true = ν₁ → cfUnderLaw … false = ν₀ → qte = quantile ν₁ τ − quantile ν₀ τ` | **QTE as a functional of the identified laws** — the payoff of the quantile layer; reduces QTE identification to distributional identification. | **Proved** |
| `POBackdoorSystem.qte_backdoor` | `qte P.μ τ = quantile (ipwLaw 1) τ − quantile (ipwLaw 0) τ` | Backdoor QTE identification; chains `qte_eq_of_law_eq` with the proven `cfUnderLaw_eq_ipwLaw`. | **Proved** |

## 9g''b. `PO/ID/Exact/QTE/DistributionalBackdoor.lean` — Distributional backdoor (Firpo 2007)

Lifts the mean-level backdoor (`ate_backdoor`/`cate_backdoor`, §9g) to the whole
law of `Y(d)`: under Firpo ignorability (unconfoundedness + bare common support
`0 < e_d`), `Law(Y(d))` equals the observable inverse-probability-weighting law.
This is the engine behind §9g'' QTE identification.

## 9g'''. `PO/ID/Exact/PartialLinear/{Setup,Identification}.lean` — Partially Linear Model (continuous treatment, PO framework)

The partially linear regression (PLR) model `Y = g(X) + θ·D + noise` as a causal
model under the **standard backdoor PO framework with a real-valued (continuous)
treatment** `D ∈ ℝ`. `Setup.lean` builds the continuous-treatment substrate and the
homogeneous structural model; `Identification.lean` identifies the structural slope
`θ` as the Robinson partialling-out estimand (the causal bridge). All declarations
**proved** (sorry-free).

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `POPartialLinearSystem` | structure | Continuous-treatment backdoor subsystem: real treatment node `D`, real outcome `Y`, covariate `X`, value-space equivs, node distinctness. Mirrors `POBackdoorSystem` with `D : ℝ`. |
| `POPartialLinearSystem.YofD d` | `P.Ω → ℝ` | The potential outcome `Y(d)` under dose `d : ℝ` (`yVar.cfUnder dVar d`). |
| `POPartialLinearSystem.sigmaX` / `sigmaXD` | `MeasurableSpace P.Ω` | σ-algebra generated by the covariate, resp. by the covariate and treatment jointly; `sigmaX_le_sigmaXD` records the inclusion. |
| `POPartialLinearModel` | structure (extends system) | Adds the homogeneous linear dose-response `Y(d) = b(X)+θ·d+U`, the backdoor mean-independence `E[U∣σ(X,D)]=0`, and consistency. |
| `POPartialLinearModel.factualY_eq` | `Y =ᵐ b(X)+θ·D+U` | Observed-data form of the structural model, from consistency + the dose-response restriction. |
| `POPartialLinearModel.causal_homogeneity` | `Y(d)−Y(d') =ᵐ θ·(d−d')` | The causal reading: `θ` is the constant per-unit treatment effect. |
| `POPartialLinearModel.mReg` / `lReg` | `P.Ω → ℝ` | Treatment / outcome regressions on the covariate, `E[D∣σX]` and `E[Y∣σX]`. |
| `POPartialLinearModel.condExp_U_sigmaX` | `E[U∣σX] =ᵐ 0` | The structural error has zero mean given the covariate (backdoor + tower). |
| `POPartialLinearModel.condExp_resid_sigmaX` | `E[D−m₀(X)∣σX] =ᵐ 0` | The treatment residual is conditionally mean-zero. |
| `POPartialLinearModel.integral_U_resid` | `E[U·(D−m₀(X))] = 0` | Orthogonality of the structural error to the treatment residual (needs `Integrable U`). |
| `POPartialLinearModel.lReg_eq` | `ℓ₀(X) =ᵐ b(X)+θ·m₀(X)` | Decomposition of the outcome regression. |
| `POPartialLinearModel.robinson_estimand_eq_theta` | `E[(Y−ℓ₀)(D−m₀)] / E[(D−m₀)²] = θ` | **The causal bridge**: the Robinson partialling-out estimand equals the structural slope, given residual treatment variation `E[(D−m₀)²]≠0`. |

## 9h. `PO/ID/Exact/DTR/` — Sequential Backdoor Identification (Dynamic Treatment Regime, general `n`)

Formalizes `prop:po-dynamic-backdoor` from `Basic Concepts.tex` (subsection
`subsec:po-dynamic-regime`) for arbitrary horizon `n ≥ 1`, in the bare
potential-outcome framework.  Reuses the bundle-conditioned conditional
expectation machinery from `PO/Conditioning/Bundle.lean`.

The identification target is the **iterated-conditional-expectation form**

    (historyBundle 0).condExpGiven (Y_of dbar)  =ᵐ[μ]  innerReg dbar (n - 1)

where `innerReg dbar j` is a recursively-defined CE-ratio chain over `n`
stages (innermost level `j = 0` conditions on the full history
`historyBundle (n - 1) = (S 0, D 0, …, S (n - 1))`; outermost level
`j = n - 1` conditions on `historyBundle 0 = (S 0,)`).  Integrated form:
`E[Y(dbar)] = ∫ innerReg dbar (n - 1) ∂μ`.

**Treatment-space and state-space conventions.**  One homogeneous
treatment space `δ : Type` (with `[MeasurableSpace δ] [MeasurableSingletonClass δ]`)
shared by all stages, and per-stage state types `γ : Fin n → Type`.  A
treatment sequence is `dbar : Fin n → δ`.  The `n = 2, δ = Bool`
specialization recovers the legacy two-stage statement (with
`dbar 0 = d₁` and `dbar 1 = d₂`).

**Per-sequence sequential exchangeability.**  Sequential exchangeability is
quantified per `dbar` (mirroring `def:po-dynamic-assumptions` literally),
avoiding the `Fin (|δ|^n)`-wide counterfactual bundle that the n=2
prototype used.  The conditioning σ-algebra at stage `k` is the full
σ-algebra of `historyBundle k` (the `{D̄_{k-1} = d̄_{k-1}}` qualifier from
the tex is dropped per the agreed simplification).

The code is split into five files: Setup / Helpers / Induction /
StrongCancellation / Main.  The dedicated `StrongCancellation.lean` file
houses the unified inductive predicate that merges the cancellation
identity with integrability of `innerReg`, needed under the (relaxed)
*pointwise* overlap hypothesis.

### `DTR/Induction.lean` — Base case and inductive step

The backward-induction identity (★ at depth `j`) is

    innerReg dbar j · indD dbar (n-1-j)
      =ᵐ[μ]
    indD dbar (n-1-j) · (historyBundle (n-1-j)).condExpGiven (Y_of dbar)

| Declaration | Signature | Description | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PODTRSystem.cdtr_base` | `[StandardBorelSpace P.Ω] [IsFiniteMeasure P.μ]`, `S.Assumptions`, `(dbar : Fin n → δ)`, `0 < n` → (★ at `j = 0`) | **Innermost-stage cancellation** (`j = 0`).  Generalizes `step_1` of the legacy n=2 proof.  Chain: consistency rewrite `factualY · indD n =ᵐ Y_of · indD n` (via `indD_eq_indicator_event` + `factualAgrees_regime` + `POVar.factual_mul_indicator_eq_cf_mul_indicator` + `yVar_notMem_regime`); factorisation `indD n = indD (n-1) · (dVar ⟨n-1⟩).indicator` via `indD_factor_split`; pull-out of `indD (n-1)` from the numerator condExp (σ-strongly-measurable via `stronglyMeasurable_indD_sigma_history`); stage-`(n-1)` exchangeability via `CondIndepCFBundle.project` + `condExp_mul_of_condIndep`; pointwise cancellation case-splitting on `indD_eq_zero_or_one`, with overlap_{n-1} discharging the nonzero branch | **Proved** |
| `PODTRSystem.cdtr_step` | `[StandardBorelSpace P.Ω] [IsFiniteMeasure P.μ]`, `S.Assumptions`, `(dbar : Fin n → δ)`, `(j : ℕ)`, `j + 1 < n`, `n - j - 2 < n`, `Integrable (S.innerReg dbar j) P.μ`, IH (★ at `j`) → (★ at `j + 1`) | **Inductive step** (`j → j + 1`).  Generalizes `step_2`–`step_4` of the legacy n=2 proof.  Let `k := n - j - 2`.  Via `condExpRatio_eq_of_mul`: (A) numerator-denominator product identity using IH + `indD_factor_split` + reverse pull-out of `(dVar ⟨k⟩).indicator` inside `σ(historyBundle (k+1))` via `stronglyMeasurable_indicator_dVar_sigma_history` + tower down to `σ(historyBundle k)` via `historyBundle_sigma_mono_step` and `condExpGiven_tower_of_le` + stage-`k` exchangeability via `condExp_mul_of_condIndep`.  (B) Denominator nonvanishing via `overlap_k`.  Multiplied back by `indD k` on both sides.  The extra `Integrable (innerReg j)` hypothesis (added 2026-04-26 along with the pointwise-overlap relaxation) supplies the LHS pull-out integrability previously taken from `innerReg_integrable`. | **Proved** |

### `DTR/StrongCancellation.lean` — Strengthened cancellation identity (a.e. equality)

Under the **pointwise** overlap hypothesis, the proof of integrability of
`innerReg dbar j` is interlocked with the cancellation identity.  This
file proves a single unified inductive predicate

    P j ↔ (innerReg dbar j =ᵐ[μ] indD dbar (n-1-j) · μ[Y_of dbar | σ_{n-1-j}])
          ∧ Integrable (innerReg dbar j) μ

| Declaration | Signature | Description | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PODTRSystem.cdtr_strong` | `[StandardBorelSpace P.Ω] [IsFiniteMeasure P.μ]`, `S.Assumptions`, `(dbar : Fin n → δ)`, `0 < n`, `∀ j < n` → `(strong identity at j) ∧ Integrable (innerReg j)` | **Strengthened cancellation identity (joint with integrability).**  By induction on `j`: base case `j = 0` reuses `cdtr_base` for the weak form and case-splits on `indD m ∈ {0,1}` to upgrade to the strong form (vanishing on `{indD m = 0}` from numerator/denominator both factoring through `indD m`).  Step case `j → j+1` calls `cdtr_step` with the integrability part of the IH, then upgrades via `indD_factor_split` and the strong IH to show `μ[innerReg j · ind_k | σ_k]` factors through `indD k`, hence `innerReg(j+1) =ᵐ 0` on `{indD k = 0}`. | **Proved** |
| `PODTRSystem.innerReg_integrable` | `[StandardBorelSpace P.Ω] [IsFiniteMeasure P.μ]`, `S.Assumptions`, `j < n` → `Integrable (S.innerReg dbar j) P.μ` | Integrability of every iterated CE-ratio.  Re-derived from `cdtr_strong`'s second conjunct (replacing the previously sorry'd direct-bound proof in `Helpers.lean`). | **Proved** |

### `DTR/Main.lean` — Final theorems

| Declaration | Signature | Description | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PODTRSystem.cdtr_iter` | `[StandardBorelSpace P.Ω] [IsFiniteMeasure P.μ]`, `S.Assumptions`, `0 < n`, `∀ j < n` → (★ at `j`) | Backward-induction iterate combining `cdtr_base` (`j = 0`) and `cdtr_step` (`j → j + 1`); proved by `Nat.rec` on `j`, with index-bridging via `omega`.  Threads the integrability hypothesis required by `cdtr_step` from `cdtr_strong`. | **Proved** |
| `PODTRSystem.cdtr_backdoor` | `[StandardBorelSpace P.Ω] [IsFiniteMeasure P.μ]`, `S.Assumptions`, `(dbar : Fin n → δ)`, `0 < n` → `(S.historyBundle 0 _).condExpGiven (S.Y_of dbar) P.μ =ᵐ[P.μ] S.innerReg dbar (n - 1)` | **General-`n` CDTR backdoor identification.**  Specialise `cdtr_iter` at `j = n - 1`; the partial indicator `S.indD dbar 0 = fun _ => 1` collapses both `· indD 0` factors via `mul_one`/`one_mul` | **Proved** |
| `PODTRSystem.dtr_backdoor` | `[StandardBorelSpace P.Ω] [IsFiniteMeasure P.μ]`, `S.Assumptions`, `(dbar : Fin n → δ)`, `0 < n` → `S.dtrEffect dbar = S.adjustedDtr dbar` | **General-`n` integrated DTR identification.**  `E[Y(dbar)] = ∫ innerReg dbar (n - 1)`.  Two-line corollary of `cdtr_backdoor` via `MeasureTheory.integral_condExp` and `integral_congr_ae` | **Proved** |

**Status / known gaps.**
- Both `cdtr_backdoor` and `dtr_backdoor` are unconditional **for arbitrary `n ≥ 1`**, modulo the standing project-wide `Mathlib.CondIndep` stubs (`condExp_mul_of_condIndep`) shared with ATE.lean and DID.lean.  No `sorry` in any of the four DTR files.
- The **nested-integral form** that matches `prop:po-dynamic-backdoor` literally in the `.tex` (`∫ ⋯ ∫ μ[Y \| S̄_n, D̄_n=d̄_n] dP(S_n \| S̄_{n-1}, D̄_{n-1}=d̄_{n-1}) ⋯ dP(S_1)`) is *deferred*: it requires the not-yet-available `condDistrib`-as-kernel infrastructure (cf. `Causalean/Mathlib/CondDistrib.lean`, the *condDistrib → Kernel.condKernel migration*).
- The remark in the tex about **history-dependent regimes** `d_k : (S̄_k, D̄_{k-1}) → δ` is not formalized here; the same induction pattern would carry over once the corresponding regime-builder is available.

## 9i. `PO/ID/Exact/DID.lean` — Two-Period DID Identification of the ATT (PO framework)

Formalizes `def:po-did-system`, `def:po-did-assumptions`, and `prop:po-did-att`
from `Basic Concepts.tex` (lines 1693–1809): the two-period difference-in-differences
identification of the ATT in the bare potential-outcome framework.  Mirrors
`LATE.lean` / `ATE.lean` in style but is strictly simpler — no σ-algebra
conditional expectations, no independence assumption, no Wald ratio, no
monotonicity.  The whole file lives on the event-level `eventCondExp` layer
plus `POVar` consistency.

## 9i*. `PO/ID/Exact/CSDID.lean` — Callaway--Sant'Anna group-time DID identification

Formalizes `def:po-cs-did-system`, `def:po-cs-did-assumptions`, and
`prop:po-cs-did-att` from `Basic Concepts.tex` (lines 2439–2565): the
no-covariate Callaway--Sant'Anna staggered-adoption DID identification of the
group-time ATT(g, t) under irreversibility, no anticipation, and never-treated
parallel trends. Extends two-period `DID.lean` from one cohort + one
post-period to a finite horizon `T` with cohorts `G_g = {D_{g−1}=0, D_g=1}` and
never-treated event `C = ⋂_s {D_s = 0}`. Periods are 0-indexed in Lean
(`Fin T` with `2 ≤ T`), so the .tex bound `2 ≤ g ≤ t ≤ T` becomes
`1 ≤ g.val ≤ t.val < T`. Proof structure mirrors `PODIDSystem.att_did` line by
line; the only genuinely new ingredients are (i) recursive construction of the
treatment-path regimes `regOf g`, `regNT` via iterated `Regime.sqcup`, and
(ii) reduction of `cohortEvent` plus irreversibility to `FactualAgrees (regOf g)`
almost surely.

| `POCSDIDSystem.dVar`, `yVar` | `Fin S.T → POVar P Bool` / `Fin S.T → POVar P ℝ` | Per-period `POVar` wrappers around `D s`, `Y s` | **Defined** |
| `POCSDIDSystem.factualD`, `factualY`, `dEvent` | `Fin S.T → P.Ω → Bool` / `Fin S.T → P.Ω → ℝ` / `Fin S.T → Bool → Set P.Ω` | Factual treatment / outcome at period `s`; factual event `{D s = b}` | **Defined** |
| `POCSDIDSystem.measurable_factualD`, `measurable_factualY`, `measurableSet_dEvent` | `Measurable …` / `MeasurableSet …` | One-line delegations to the `POVar` API | **Proved** |
| `POCSDIDSystem.dTargetUpTo` | `POCSDIDSystem P → ℕ → Finset P.V` | Recursive standalone target: image of `S.D` on indices `< k`; lets us prove disjointness for the next `Regime.sqcup` step | **Defined** |

## 9i0. `PO/Analysis/Regression.lean` — Regression-Function Representatives

Shared predicate `IsRegressionFunction` and derived lemmas, extracted from the RDD
files so SharpRDD and FuzzyRDD can both use the same interface without duplication.

| `IsRegressionFunction μ X g f` | `Measure Ω → (Ω → ℝ) → (Ω → ℝ) → (ℝ → ℝ) → Prop` | `f : ℝ → ℝ` is a regression-function representative of `g` over `X`: measurability of `f`, integrability of `g` and of `f ∘ X`, and the integral identity `∫_{X⁻¹A} g = ∫_{X⁻¹A} f ∘ X` for all measurable `A` | **Defined** |
| `IsRegressionFunction.integrable_pushforward` | `IsRegressionFunction μ X g f → AEMeasurable X μ → Integrable f (μ.map X)` | `f` is integrable under the pushforward of `X` whenever `X` is AE-measurable | **Proved** |
| `IsRegressionFunction.sub` | `IsRegressionFunction μ X g₁ f₁ → IsRegressionFunction μ X g₂ f₂ → IsRegressionFunction μ X (g₁ - g₂) (f₁ - f₂)` | Linearity: difference of representatives is the representative of the difference | **Proved** |
| `IsRegressionFunction.aeEq_of_aeEq_response` | `g₁ =ᵐ[μ] g₂ → IsRegressionFunction μ X g₁ f₁ → IsRegressionFunction μ X g₂ f₂ → f₁ =ᵐ[μ.map X] f₂` | If two response variables are ae-equal, their regression representatives agree ae on the pushforward | **Proved** |

## 9i0a. `Panel/Analysis/Residualization.lean` — Population Residualization Core (FWL framework)

Framework primitives for the **population estimand-characterization layer**: a linear `L²` nuisance class, a residualization witness `(V_H, Ṽ)` decomposing a square-integrable variable against the class, the residualized population coefficient `β_H(Y, D) = E[D̃·Ỹ] / E[D̃²]`, and the **population Frisch–Waugh–Lovell theorem**. Pure measure-theoretic; no `POSystem`/`CausalModel`/`SWIGGraph` dependence. Downstream paper-specific files (Słoczyński saturated OLS, TWFE decompositions, event-study, 2SLS, …) instantiate `ResidualizationWitness` for their nuisance class (controls, unit + time fixed effects, cohort effects, …) and reduce to the FWL ratio via this theorem. Specifies `def:po-estimand-residualization-witness`, `def:po-estimand-residualized-coefficient`, and `prop:po-estimand-fwl` from `doc/basic_concepts/po/estimand_characterization/residualization_core.md`.

| Declaration | Signature | Description | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `LinearL2Class μ` | `structure { mem : (Ω → ℝ) → Prop, memLp, zero_mem, add_mem, smul_mem }` | A linear class of `MemLp 2 μ` real-valued functions on `Ω`, predicate-style: `mem` carves out the underlying set, with closure under scalar multiplication and addition, and every member required to be square-integrable | **Defined** |
| `ResidualizationWitness μ H V` | `structure { VH, Vtilde : Ω → ℝ, VH_mem, Vtilde_memLp, decomp : V =ᵐ[μ] VH + Vtilde, orthogonal }` | Population residualization witness for `V` against `H`: bundles the in-class projection `V_H ∈ H`, the L²-residual `Ṽ`, the a.e. decomposition `V = V_H + Ṽ`, and population orthogonality `∀ h ∈ H, ∫ Ṽ·h dμ = 0` | **Defined** |
| `residualizedCoefficient μ H wY wD` | `noncomputable def : ℝ` | Residualized population coefficient `β_H(Y, D) := (∫ D̃·Ỹ dμ) / (∫ D̃·D̃ dμ)`, the population Frisch–Waugh–Lovell representation of the coefficient on `D` in a linear projection that also includes the nuisance terms `H`. Positivity of the denominator is supplied at theorem-use time | **Defined** |
| `residualizedCoefficient_eq_of_normalEqs` | `(Y_memLp) (D_memLp) (wY) (wD) (hDtilde_pos : 0 < ∫ D̃²) (β) (Hβ) (Hβ_mem) (h_normal_D) (h_normal_H) → β = residualizedCoefficient μ H wY wD` | **Population Frisch–Waugh–Lovell theorem** (`prop:po-estimand-fwl`): if `β` and `Hβ ∈ H` jointly satisfy the population normal equations for projecting `Y` on `D` and `H` (`∫ (Y − βD − Hβ)·D = 0` and `∀ h ∈ H, ∫ (Y − βD − Hβ)·h = 0`), and `E[D̃²] > 0`, then `β` equals the residualized coefficient. Proof: build `h* = wY.VH − β·wD.VH − Hβ ∈ H`, derive `∫ e·D̃ = 0` from the two normal equations and `wD.decomp`, expand `e = h* + (Ỹ − β·D̃)` a.e., use `wD.orthogonal h*` to kill `h*`, divide by `hDtilde_pos.ne'` | **Proved** |

| `CellBridge.cell_integral_div_mul_cellMass` / `cellMean_mul_cellMass` | `((∫ F·𝟙{X=i}) / cellMass) * cellMass = ∫ F·𝟙{X=i}` | Dividing by cell mass and multiplying back recovers the raw indicator-weighted integral, including zero-mass cells by totalized division | **Proved** |

| `CellBridge.integral_eq_sum_cell` | `Integrable F μ → ∫ F dμ = Σ_i ∫ F·𝟙{X=i} dμ` | Integrates an integrable function by summing over finite cells | **Proved** |

## 9i0a-VariableIntensityIV. `PO/ID/Exact/VariableIntensityIV/{OrderedTreatment,VariableIntensity}.lean` — Variable-Intensity IV ACR (Angrist-Imbens)

Specific-paper scaffold for Angrist-Imbens (1995) variable treatment intensity and average causal response, formulated **inside the potential-outcome framework** (`POSystem`): the instrument, treatment intensity, and outcome are system variables; potential intensities `D(z)` and treatment-indexed potential outcomes `Y(d)` are genuine `POVar.cfUnder` counterfactuals; consistency (`D=D(Z)`, `Y=Y(D)`) is the canonical `POSystem.Consistency` and instrument independence is `POSystem.IndepCF` over a counterfactual bundle (not ad-hoc structure fields). `OrderedTreatment.lean` holds the finite ordered-intensity algebra (adjacent margins, crossing indicators, telescoping identities) directly — its sole consumer is `VariableIntensity.lean` in this folder, so it lives here rather than under `Panel` — and re-exports the shared generic `NormalizedWeights` normalized-weight helpers. `VariableIntensity.lean` packages a directed instrument-cell contrast, crossing events, indicator-weighted ACR, conditional-margin ACR, Wald/2SLS interface definitions, and the headline ACR characterization statements. Companion NL doc: `doc/basic_concepts/po/estimand_characterization/angrist_imbens_variable_intensity.md`.

| `OrderedTreatment.ordered_telescope_identity` | `a ≤ b → intensityValue b - intensityValue a = Σ_j crossingIndicator a b j` | Identity-function version of the ordered telescoping lemma, equating intensity movement with crossed-margin count | **Proved** |

| `OrderedTreatment.sum_normalizedWeight_eq_one` | `0 < Σ_i a_i → Σ_i normalizedWeight a i = 1` | Normalized finite weights sum to one when the normalizing total is positive | **Proved** |

## 9i0a-MultipleInstrumentIV. `PO/ID/Exact/MultipleInstrumentIV/{FiniteIndex,ResponseTypes,Population,Main,POBridge}.lean` — Multiple-Instrument IV (Mogstad-Torgovitsky-Walters)

Specific-paper finite-support algebra for the MTW multiple-IV characterization.  This layer works with an ordered saturated first-stage index, a finite matrix first-stage projection, support masses, tail coefficients, binary response types, response-type effects, a saturated finite-support population bridge, and an observed measure-backed population 2SLS bridge.  It proves the ordered-tail coefficient nonnegativity, the finite tail-sum interchange identity, the response-type ratio representation, the population-bridge equality from reduced-form/first-stage moments to the finite response-type ratio, the observed `E[h(Z)Y] / E[h(Z)D]` bridge to that ratio, and the positive-weight normalization result under MTW sign alignment.

`POBridge.lean` grounds this algebra in an explicit potential-outcome system (`POMultipleIVSystem`): the response type `G = (D(z⁰),…,D(z^{K-1}))` is a genuine counterfactual, and under `Assumptions` (consistency + per-cell instrument independence `Z ⟂ (D(zᵏ),Y(1),Y(0))`) the two `ObservedBridge` conditional-mean fields are *derived*, not assumed — discharging Gap G5 of the faithfulness audit.  Its flagship `POMultipleIVSystem.observedBeta2SLS_eq_responseTypeWeightedSum` restates the observed 2SLS ratio as the response-type weighted sum `Σ_g ω_g Δ_g` with `Δ_g = E[Y(1)-Y(0) | G=g]`, i.e. entirely in potential-outcome language, via the same drop-of-conditioning + total-law pattern as `PO/ID/Exact/LATE.lean`.  Companion NL doc: `doc/basic_concepts/po/estimand_characterization/mogstad_torgovitsky_walters_multiple_iv.md`.

## 9i0a-UniformTwoWayPanel. `Panel/UniformTwoWayPanel.lean` — Uniform Balanced Two-Way Panel Algebra

Paper-agnostic finite balanced-panel helpers for TWFE and two-way Mundlak arguments under the uniform unit-period measure. Lives directly under `Panel/` (general panel substrate, not estimand-characterization-specific) and exposes bridge lemmas showing it is the equal-unit-weight specialization of `WeightedTwoWayPanel`.

## 9i0a-FlexibleDIDMundlak. `Panel/EstimandCharacterization/FlexibleDIDMundlak/{TWFE,VectorTWFE,VectorMundlak,DID,PopulationBridge,PopulationOrigin}.lean` — Wooldridge TWFE/Mundlak and Flexible DID

Specific-paper formalization scaffold for `doc/basic_concepts/po/estimand_characterization/wooldridge_twfe_mundlak_did.md`. `TWFE.lean` proves the scalar finite-panel slice of Wooldridge's TWFE and two-way Mundlak equivalence by instantiating the shared `UniformTwoWayPanel.finite_residualized_coefficient_eq_of_normalEqs` finite FWL handoff. `DID.lean` is a finite-cell composition theorem: it now DERIVES the untreated-prediction recovery from no-anticipation + conditional parallel trends + additivity (no longer an assumed field), eliminates the former opaque `Prop`+`_holds` placeholders, and derives the POLS/ETWFE cell links from finite-cell residual normal equations justified by a saturated block-diagonalization lemma. **G5 de-scaffold (2026-05-30):** `m0`'s exact untreated fit is no longer a posited field — `SaturatedUntreatedRegression` now carries the genuine weighted least-squares projection origin (`untreatedWeight`, `untreatedWeight_pos`, `untreatedNormalEq`: `m0` solves the untreated-only normal equations against the additive class `H0`), and the exact fit `m0 = YgMean` on untreated cells is the DERIVED theorem `untreatedFit` (the projection is exact because no-anticipation + conditional parallel trends place the untreated observed mean inside `H0`). **G9 de-scaffold (2026-05-30):** the finite imputation estimand is now bridged to the population conditional expectation — `PopulationBridge.lean` proves `thetaImp g t = eventCondExp μ cohortEvent Δ` (θ^imp = E[Δ∣G=g]) via the law of iterated expectations over the finite covariate partition, under explicit identification hypotheses (covariate weights are conditional cell probabilities; cell residuals are within-cell conditional means). **G1 de-scaffold (2026-05-30):** the scalar-only restriction is removed — `VectorTWFE.lean` introduces the genuine K-vector TWFE problem with a `Matrix K K ℝ`-valued residualized Gram matrix `Q_ddotX`, the full-rank condition `IsUnit (gram X).det`, and the matrix normal equation; existence and uniqueness of the closed-form coefficient `(gram X)⁻¹ (Σ ddot X ddot Y)` are proved, and `ScalarTWFEProblem` is shown to be the `K = Fin 1` specialization (`ScalarTWFEProblem.toVector` + `toVector_betaTWFE`). **`VectorMundlak.lean` (2026-05-30)** completes Theorem A in vector form: the matrix Frisch-Waugh-Lovell handoff `matrix_fwl_eq_of_normalEqs` (generalizing the scalar finite FWL), the K-vector two-way Mundlak nuisance span `IsVectorTwoWayMundlakNuisance`, the coding-free `VectorTWMFit`, and the equivalence `vec_twfe_twm_equivalence : fit.beta = P.betaTWFE` plus the optional-controls-invariance corollary. The remaining deferred Wooldridge gap is the population conditional-expectation origin of `m0` itself (G5 measure layer).

### `FlexibleDIDMundlak/PopulationBridge.lean` — finite estimand/projection → population conditional expectation (audit G9 + G5 population half)

Bridges the finite-cell imputation estimand and the saturated projection `m0` to population conditional expectations, reusing the conditional finite-partition total law `Causalean.PO.eventCondExp_eq_sum_condProb_mul_eventCondExp`. Hypothesis-driven: identification hypotheses connect the finite scaffold's primitive means to a probability model — they are exactly the paper's *definitions* (θ^imp = E[Δ∣G=g]; m0 = E[Y(∞)∣G,t,C]), not strengthenings.

### `FlexibleDIDMundlak/PopulationOrigin.lean` — `ofPopulation` constructor making the m0 conditional-expectation origin definitional (audit G5 measure layer)

Closes the *measure-layer* half of G5: instead of *assuming* `Y0Mean g t c = E[Y(∞)∣cell]` (the `hY0` hypothesis above), it builds a `StaggeredATTCells` whose cell means are *defined* as that `eventCondExp`, so `hY0` holds by `rfl`. Mirrors `DCDHPanel.ofPopulation`. The cell-weight data (`cohortShare`, `covarWeight`) is supplied as a witness (an FWL/partition construction orthogonal to the conditional-expectation origin); the pointwise consistency inputs are the paper's consistency axiom restricted to each cell.

## 9i0a-ImputationEventStudy. `Panel/EstimandCharacterization/ImputationEventStudy/Imputation.lean` — Robust Imputation Event Studies (BJS)

Specific-paper finite-cell formalization of the Borusyak-Jaravel-Spiess robust imputation event-study characterization. The module works directly with finite treated and untreated cell index types, arbitrary signed target weights, treated/untreated regressor rows, primitive observed-law means, a nuisance vector, and treated-cell effects. It proves the population imputation identification theorem (taking `PredictionIdentified` as a propositional existence hypothesis and extracting the witness internally) and the intentionally-weak `linear_unbiased_of_imputation_representation` algebra helper. The **source-strength** linear-unbiased representation theorem and the combined iff characterization now live in the companion `PanelBridge.lean` (§9i0a-ImputationEventStudyBridge), where the finite left-null-space adjustment is rebased onto the panel `WeightedSupport`/`Subspace` substrate. A staggered-adoption two-way-FE grounding (closing the abstract-index scope gap) lives in `PanelGrounding.lean` (§9i0a-ImputationEventStudyGrounding). The Gauss-Markov/BLUE efficiency half of `prop:po-estimand-bjs-linear-unbiased-imputation` is in `Efficiency.lean` (§9i0a-ImputationEventStudyEfficiency), built on the finite Gauss-Markov layer §13gm. Companion NL doc: `doc/basic_concepts/po/estimand_characterization/borusyak_jaravel_spiess_imputation.md`.

| Declaration | Signature | Description | Status |

| `ImputationEventStudy.BJSPanel` | `structure { qT, qU, a, EY_T, EY_U, EY0_T, EY0_U, beta0, tau }` | Finite BJS treated/untreated cell design: regressor rows, arbitrary target weights, observed means, untreated potential-outcome means, nuisance vector, and treated-cell effects | **Defined** |
| `BJSPanel.theta` | `BJSPanel Treated Untreated Regressor → ℝ` | Target weighted sum `∑ c, a c * tau c`; weights may be signed and need not sum to one | **Defined** |
| `BJSPanel.targetForTau` | `(Treated → ℝ) → ℝ` | Target functional evaluated at an arbitrary unrestricted treated-effect vector, used in the linear-unbiasedness statement | **Defined** |

## 9i0a-ImputationEventStudyBridge. `Panel/EstimandCharacterization/ImputationEventStudy/PanelBridge.lean` — Imputation Event Study ↔ panel substrate bridge

Connects the bespoke finite design-matrix algebra of the BJS imputation scaffold to the shared panel inner-product / subspace substrate (`Causalean/Panel/Weighted/`). The OLS imputation estimator is the *uniform-weight* special case of the panel WLS substrate, so the untreated cells carry the uniform `WeightedSupport`; the keystone lemma proves the BJS "left-null-space of `Q_U`" condition **is** `ip`-orthogonality to the regressor column span. The source-strength linear-unbiased theorem and the combined iff characterization (moved here from `Imputation.lean`, statements verbatim) consume that substrate-based left-null-space adjustment; `DecidableEq Untreated` is obtained internally via `Classical.decEq`, so their public signatures are unchanged.

| `BJSPanel.regressorColumn` | `Regressor → (Untreated → ℝ)` | The `r`-th regressor column `u ↦ q_{ur}` as an array over untreated cells | **Defined** |
| `BJSPanel.columnSpan` | `Submodule ℝ (Untreated → ℝ)` | Span of all regressor columns; orthogonality to it is the BJS left-null-space condition | **Defined** |
| `BJSPanel.ip_untreatedSupport_regressorColumn` | `ip v (regressorColumn r) = (\|U\|)⁻¹ * ∑ u, v u * qU u r` | The panel inner product of an untreated vector with a regressor column equals the BJS left-null-space sum, rescaled by the uniform weight | **Proved** |
| `BJSPanel.ip_regressorColumn_eq_zero_iff` | `ip v (regressorColumn r) = 0 ↔ ∑ u, v u * qU u r = 0` | `ip`-orthogonality to a single column ⟺ that column's left-null coordinate vanishes | **Proved** |
| `BJSPanel.columnSpan_ip_orthogonal_iff` | `(∀ h ∈ columnSpan, ip v h = 0) ↔ ∀ r, ∑ u, v u * qU u r = 0` | **Keystone bridge**: a vector is `ip`-orthogonal to the regressor column span iff it satisfies the BJS left-null-space condition (the panel-substrate restatement of "`v` lies in the left null space of `Q_U`") | **Proved** |
| `BJSPanel.exists_imputationWeights_of_gap_orthogonal` | `(hc0 : a c0 ≠ 0) → H0 → (gap ip-orthogonal to columnSpan) → ∃ H, ∀ u, ∑ c, a c * H.weight c u = -vU u` | Audit M3 left-null-space row adjustment, phrased through the panel substrate: one nonzero target row absorbs the orthogonal gap, yielding imputation weights representing the untreated coefficients | **Proved** |
| `BJSPanel.linear_unbiased_of_prediction_identified` | `unbiasedForAllTau → PredictionIdentified → (∃ c, a c ≠ 0) → ∃ H, vT = a ∧ vU = -aᵀH ∧ (∀ YT YU, value YT YU = ∑ c, a c * (YT c - ∑ u, H.weight c u * YU u)) ∧ observedValue = psiImp H.weight` | Source-strength BJS linear-unbiased representation theorem; now consumes `exists_imputationWeights_of_gap_orthogonal` (empty-`Untreated` case handled separately) instead of an inline finite-algebra construction | **Proved** |
| `BJSPanel.bjs_linear_unbiased_iff_imputation_form` | `PredictionIdentified → (∃ c, a c ≠ 0) → (unbiasedForAllTau ↔ ∃ H, vT = a ∧ vU = -aᵀH ∧ (∀ YT YU, value = ∑ a_c (YT c - ∑ h_cu YU u)) ∧ observedValue = psiImp H.weight)` | Combined iff characterization (`prop:po-estimand-bjs-linear-unbiased-imputation`, identification half): unbiased for every tau iff BJS imputation form; (⟹) is `linear_unbiased_of_prediction_identified`, (⟸) is pure row-span algebra | **Proved** |

## 9i0a-ImputationEventStudyGrounding. `Panel/EstimandCharacterization/ImputationEventStudy/PanelGrounding.lean` — Imputation Event Study staggered-adoption grounding

Closes the abstract-index scope gap (audit G5) *constructively*: exhibits `BJSPanel` as an instance built from genuine panel primitives — units `I`, periods `Fin T`, and a staggered-adoption path `g : I → WithTop (Fin T)` via `Causalean.Panel.AdoptionPath`. Treated cells are those whose treatment has switched on (`g i ≤ t`); untreated cells are those still untreated (`t < g i`), faithfully including every never-treated cell and every pre-adoption cell of a treated unit. The regressor design is the canonical two-way fixed-effect block `I ⊕ Fin T`, so the untreated-outcome model `E[Y(0)] = α_i + λ_t` holds by construction and the BJS hypotheses discharge to a concrete panel.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `ImputationEventStudy.UntreatedCell` | `(g : I → WithTop (Fin T)) → Type` | Subtype of still-untreated cells (`AdoptionPath.lt (g i) t`); includes never-treated and pre-adoption cells | **Defined** |

## 9i0a-ImputationEventStudyEfficiency. `Panel/EstimandCharacterization/ImputationEventStudy/Efficiency.lean` — Imputation Event Study Efficiency / BLUE half

The efficiency half of `prop:po-estimand-bjs-linear-unbiased-imputation`: under spherical errors the OLS imputation estimator is the minimum-variance linear unbiased estimator (Gauss-Markov / BLUE). The BJS imputation estimator is recognized as the OLS estimator for the *event-study design* `designFull` (a treated-cell indicator block stacked with the covariate block), so the result is a direct instantiation of the finite Gauss-Markov theorem `GaussMarkov.variance_blue_spherical` (§13gm) at that design. The unbiasedness-to-design-constraint bridge uses the hoisted `LinearEstimator.vT_eq_a` and `LinearEstimator.nuisance_coord`. An additive fixed-effect-block bridge (`designFull_col_mem_indicatorSpan`) identifies the τ-columns of `designFull` with the panel `IndicatorSpan` substrate (`Causalean/Panel/Weighted/IndicatorSpan.lean`), connecting the event-study FE design to the panel indicator-span layer; the BLUE proof itself stays on the finite Gauss-Markov substrate (§13gm), the correct home for the variance argument. No `sorry`/`admit`/`axiom`. Companion NL doc section C3.

| Declaration | Signature | Description | Status |
|---|---|---|---|

| `BJSPanel.cFull` | `BJSPanel Treated Untreated Regressor → (Treated ⊕ Regressor → ℝ)` | Target functional in design coordinates: target weights `a` on the τ block, zero on the covariate block | **Defined** |
| `BJSPanel.weightOf` | `LinearEstimator P → (Treated ⊕ Untreated → ℝ)` | A linear estimator's full weight vector over all observed cells (`Sum.elim vT vU`) | **Defined** |
| `BJSPanel.weightOf_vecMul_designFull` | `unbiasedForAllTau → weightOf L ᵥ* designFull P = cFull P` | Unbiasedness bridge: an unbiased estimator's weight satisfies the design constraint (captures both `vT = a` and the nuisance left-null constraint) | **Proved** |
| `BJSPanel.bjs_ols_imputation_min_variance_spherical` | `(∀ i, MemLp (Y i) 2 μ) → SphericalFamily Y μ σ → IsUnit ((designFull P)ᵀ * designFull P).det → unbiasedForAllTau L → Var[∑ olsWeight … * Y] ≤ Var[∑ weightOf L * Y]` | **BJS efficiency theorem (BLUE):** for a full-rank event-study design and spherical cell outcomes, the OLS imputation estimator has variance no larger than any linear unbiased estimator of the target | **Proved** |
| `BJSPanel.treatedClassifier` | `(Treated ⊕ Untreated) → Option Treated` | Classifier on observed cells: each treated cell to its own label, every untreated cell to `none`; its `Some`-indicators are the τ-columns of `designFull` | **Defined** |
| `BJSPanel.designFull_col_eq_cellIndicator` | `(fun i => designFull P i (Sum.inl d)) = cellIndicator treatedClassifier (some d)` | Each treated-cell fixed-effect column of `designFull` is the panel cell indicator of the treated-cell classifier | **Proved** |

## 9i0a-HeterogeneousTWFE. `Panel/EstimandCharacterization/HeterogeneousTWFE/{FinitePanel,FWLBridge,PopulationBridge}.lean` — de Chaisemartin-D'Haultfoeuille (2020) TWFE Signed Weights

Specific-paper finite-cell formalization of the de Chaisemartin-D'Haultfoeuille TWFE heterogeneous-effects warning. `FinitePanel.lean` works over finite group-time cells with positive weights `π_gt`, binary treatment `D_gt`, observed outcomes `Y_gt`, untreated outcomes `Y0_gt`, treatment effects `τ_gt`, and a residualized-treatment witness `D̃_gt` against the group-plus-time fixed-effect span. It proves the finite FWL decomposition `β^twfe = B0 + ∑_{D=1} ω_gt τ_gt`, the zero-untreated-residual-contrast corollary, the fact that treated-cell weights sum to one while inheriting the sign of `D̃`, and the constructive sign-reversal theorem. `FWLBridge.lean` closes audit gaps **G2/G6**: for the uniform balanced panel it builds a genuine `DCDHPanel` whose `D̃` is the *derived* Frisch-Waugh-Lovell residual (double-demeaned treatment `ddot D` from `UniformTwoWayPanel`), with the membership and orthogonality fields PROVED rather than posited — only nonzero double-demeaned treatment variation (`S_D > 0`), binary treatment, and consistency remain as primitives. Companion NL doc: `doc/basic_concepts/po/estimand_characterization/de_chaisemartin_dhaultfoeuille_twfe.md`.
