## 10a'. `Mathlib/CondDistribWitness.lean` — Witness-kernel form of a conditional distribution

The measure-theoretic core of a backdoor / Rule-2 argument, stated purely in terms of
Mathlib's `condDistrib` (no SCM machinery).  When the outcome is a measurable function of the
conditioning variable and a residual coordinate, its conditional law is the pushforward of the
residual's conditional law by that function — the "witness kernel".

| Declaration | Signature | Description | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ProbabilityTheory.witnessKernel` | `Kernel (𝒳 × 𝒵) 𝒴`, `p ↦ (condDistrib C Z μ p.2).map (h p.1 p.2)` | Packages the posterior witness kernel `p ↦ (condDistrib C Z μ p.2).map (h p.1 p.2)` as a `Kernel`; Markov when `μ` is finite. | **Proved** |
| `ProbabilityTheory.condDistrib_map_of_condDistrib_fst_eq` | If `Y = h X Z C` pointwise and `C ⊥ X ∣ Z` (as `condDistrib C (X,Z) μ =ᵐ condDistrib C Z μ`), then `condDistrib Y (X,Z) μ =ᵐ (fun p => (condDistrib C Z μ p.2).map (h p.1 p.2))` | The witness-kernel form of a conditional distribution under conditional independence; the SCM-agnostic heart of the backdoor / Rule-2 identification. Proof by uniqueness of disintegration on rectangles. | **Proved** |
| `ProbabilityTheory.condDistrib_map_of_funext` | If `Y = H Z C` pointwise then `condDistrib Y Z μ =ᵐ[μ.map Z] (fun z => (condDistrib C Z μ z).map (H z))` | The **no-treatment** (`X`-free) specialization of the witness lemma: when the conditioning variable `Z` already carries all the information used to split `Y`, no conditional-independence hypothesis is needed. Consumed by the do-side bridge `doSide_M2_pullback_eq_M1_witness`. | **Proved** |

## 10b. `Mathlib/CondIndep.lean` — Graph-independent CI axioms (re-export)

Re-exports the four sub-modules below.  Existing `import Causalean.Mathlib.CondIndep`
statements continue to work unchanged.

### 10b-i. `Mathlib/CondIndep/SemiGraphoid.lean` — Semi-graphoid axioms on `ValuesOn` projections

Weak union and contraction for `CondIndepFun` specialized to `ValuesOn I Ω` projections.
Requires `Causalean.SCM.Model.SCM`.

### 10b-ii. `Mathlib/CondIndep/CondExp.lean` — CondExp + CondIndepFun lemmas

Drop-of-conditioning, product factorization, weak union via `prodMk`, and extension
by an `m`-measurable function.  No SCM import required.

### 10b-iii. `Mathlib/CondIndep/AELift.lean` — A.e.-equality/inequality lifts under overlap

Single-arm a.e.-lift and essential-bound inheritance for potential-outcome variables.

### 10b-iv. `Mathlib/CondIndep/Integrability.lean` — Integrability via condExp indicators

σ-projection of indicator positivity and integrability bound from a condExp product identity.

## 10d'. `Mathlib/IIDCenteredSum.lean` — Conditional 2nd-moment bound for centered i.i.d. sums

fold-B empirical-process bound in `Stat/SampleSplit/FoldBEmpiricalProcess.lean`: for a
finite family of i.i.d. samples independent of a sub-σ-algebra `m_A`, the
expected square of the centered scaled sum is bounded by the expected

nuisance subspace `H` admitting an orthogonal projection.  Causal- and

`Panel/FWLInstanceL2.lean` (§9i0a-FWLInstanceL2)

estimand papers a shared, measure-theory-native FWL engine.  (The finite
weighted-support tower `Weighted/FWL.lean` does **not** instantiate this file:
its inner product is only positive-semidefinite, so it carries its own FWL
built on `Mathlib/SemiInnerProjection`; the two are connected at the data level
via `Weighted/OfProbabilityMeasure.lean`.)  NL artifact:
`doc/basic_concepts/mathlib/fwl.md`.

## 10h. `Mathlib/TwoStateMarkov.lean` — two-state Markov transition matrix, stationary projection, geometric ergodicity

Project-generic shim (depends only on Mathlib; no causal/panel/Causalean
content) for the two-state Markov chain on `Fin 2` with rows

`(1 - a, a)` and `(b, 1 - b)`. Carries the two transition/stationary
matrix definitions and the substrate for long-T compact-uniform
convergence required by
`CausalSmith/Panel/Q1_SpectralThreshold/LongT.lean`: spectral
decomposition of the transition matrix plus uniform geometric
convergence to the stationary projection on compact subsets of the open
transition-parameter square `(0,1)²`. **Both definitions and all 4
theorems are in place; all theorems proved.**

This file consolidates the two definitions (previously local to
`CausalSmith/CausalSmith/Panel/Q1_SpectralThreshold/Basic.lean`) and the
four ergodicity theorems (previously in
`CausalSmith/CausalSmith/Mathlib/MarkovErgodicity.lean`, now deleted)
into a single neutral Causalean module. `Q1_SpectralThreshold/Basic.lean`
re-exports the two definitions under the short names so existing
downstream code is unchanged.

| Declaration | Signature | Description | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Causalean.Mathlib.TwoStateMarkov.transitionMatrix` | `(a b : ℝ) → Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℝ` | The 2×2 row-stochastic transition matrix with rows `(1 - a, a)` and `(b, 1 - b)`. `noncomputable`. | **Defined.** |
| `Causalean.Mathlib.TwoStateMarkov.stationaryProjection` | `(a b : ℝ) → Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℝ` | The rank-one projector whose two rows both equal the stationary distribution `(b/(a+b), a/(a+b))`. `noncomputable`. | **Defined.** |
| `Causalean.Mathlib.TwoStateMarkov.transitionMatrix_pow_eq_spectral` | `(a b : ℝ) (ha_pos : 0 < a) (ha_lt_one : a < 1) (hb_pos : 0 < b) (hb_lt_one : b < 1) → ∀ k, M^k = Π + (1 - a - b)^k • (1 - Π)` | Spectral decomposition: powers of the transition matrix split into the stationary projection plus a geometrically-decaying correction along `1 - Π`. **Proved.** |
| `Causalean.Mathlib.TwoStateMarkov.one_minus_a_b_abs_lt_one` | `(0 < a) (0 < b) (a < 1) (b < 1) → |1 - a - b| < 1` | Pointwise spectral gap on the open transition-parameter square. **Proved.** |
| `Causalean.Mathlib.TwoStateMarkov.one_minus_a_b_uniform_gap_on_compact` | `(K : Set (ℝ × ℝ)) (IsCompact K) (K ⊆ (0,1)²) → ∃ ρ < 1, ∀ p ∈ K, |1 - p.1 - p.2| ≤ ρ` | Uniform spectral gap on compact subsets via `IsCompact.exists_isMaxOn` + averaging the maximum with `1`. **Proved.** |
| `Causalean.Mathlib.TwoStateMarkov.transitionMatrix_pow_tendsto_stationary_uniform` | `(K compact ⊆ (0,1)²) → ∀ ε > 0, ∃ N, ∀ k ≥ N, ∀ p ∈ K, ∀ i j, |((M p.1 p.2)^k - Π p.1 p.2) i j| ≤ ε` | Uniform geometric convergence of `M^k` to the stationary projection on compact subsets, combining the spectral decomposition (entries of `1 - Π` bounded by `1`) with the uniform gap (geometric decay rate `ρ < 1`). **Proved.** |

architecture consumed by `Panel/Subspace.lean`.

Proof uses the restricted Gram map `H →ₗ Dual ℝ H`, shows each right-hand side lies in its range via the PSD radical fact and dual-annihilator/range duality, then chooses a linear right inverse of the range restriction. | **Proved.** |

## 10i. `Mathlib/StandardGaussian.lean` — standard Gaussian on a finite-dim inner-product space

Constructs the standard Gaussian measure on an arbitrary finite-dimensional
real inner-product space `E` (mean zero, covariance = inner product) and proves
its basic moments. Construction: take `b := stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ E`, build the
product of `n = finrank ℝ E` standard real Gaussians on `Fin n → ℝ`, transport
to `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)` via `toLp`, then pull back to `E` along the
isometry `b.repr.symm`. Upstream candidate.

| Declaration | Signature | Description | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Causalean.Mathlib.stdGaussian` | `[FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [BorelSpace E] → Measure E` | The standard Gaussian measure on `E`: `(prod of gaussianReal 0 1).map toLp` pulled back along `b.repr.symm`. | **Proved.** |
| `Causalean.Mathlib.isProbabilityMeasure_stdGaussian` | `IsProbabilityMeasure (stdGaussian E)` | Probability measure (pushforward of a `Measure.pi` of probability measures). | **Proved.** |
| `Causalean.Mathlib.isGaussian_stdGaussian` | `IsGaussian (stdGaussian E)` | Gaussian law; via `iIndepFun.hasGaussianLaw` for the product, then `isGaussian_map_equiv`. | **Proved.** |
| `Causalean.Mathlib.stdGaussian_mean` | `∫ x, x ∂(stdGaussian E) = 0` | Mean is zero; each coordinate `gaussianReal 0 1` has mean 0, pushed through the continuous-linear maps. | **Proved.** |
| `Causalean.Mathlib.covarianceBilin_stdGaussian` | `covarianceBilin (stdGaussian E) u v = ⟪u, v⟫_ℝ` | Covariance bilinear form equals the inner product. Via `covarianceBilin_map` (adjoint of isometry = inverse), `covarianceBilin_apply_pi`, coordinate covariances (Kronecker delta from independence + unit variance), and `OrthonormalBasis.repr` isometry. | **Proved.** |
| `Causalean.Mathlib.stdGaussian_map_normSq_eq_pi` | `(stdGaussian E).map ‖·‖² = (Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin (finrank ℝ E) => gaussianReal 0 1)).map (∑ (w i)²)` | Exposes the product-of-1-D-Gaussians structure of the squared-norm law (rotation-invariance of `‖·‖²` strips the orthonormal-basis transport), used for χ² atomlessness. | **Proved.** |

## 10j. `Mathlib/OperatorSqrt.lean` — positive square root of a positive operator

Builds the **operator square root** of a positive symmetric operator on a
finite-dimensional real inner-product space — a result Mathlib lacks (it has the
spectral theorem and `LinearMap.IsPositive`, but no operator sqrt). Construction:
in the orthonormal eigenbasis `b` with real eigenvalues `μ` (both from
`LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvectorBasis`/`eigenvalues`), `posSqrt` acts as
`√(μ i)` on each eigenvector (via `Basis.constr`). Upstream candidate. All in
namespace `LinearMap.IsPositive` (with `hT : T.IsPositive`).

| Declaration | Signature | Description | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `eigBasis` / `eigVals` | `OrthonormalBasis (Fin (finrank ℝ E)) ℝ E` / `Fin _ → ℝ` | Orthonormal eigenbasis and real eigenvalues of the positive operator `T`. | **Proved.** |
| `eigVals_nonneg` | `0 ≤ hT.eigVals i` | Eigenvalues of a positive operator are nonnegative (`μ i = ⟪T (b i), b i⟫ ≥ 0`). | **Proved.** |
| `posSqrt` | `E →ₗ[ℝ] E` | The square root: `posSqrt (b i) = √(μ i) • b i`, extended by `Basis.constr`. | **Proved.** |
| `posSqrt_mul_self` | `hT.posSqrt ∘ₗ hT.posSqrt = T` | Square law, via `Real.mul_self_sqrt` and `Basis.ext`. | **Proved.** |
| `posSqrt_inner` | `⟪posSqrt x, y⟫ = ∑ i, √(μ i) ⟪b i,x⟫ ⟪b i,y⟫` | Symmetric weighted-sum form of the quadratic data. | **Proved.** |
| `posSqrt_isSymmetric` / `posSqrt_isPositive` | `IsSymmetric` / `IsPositive` | `posSqrt` is itself symmetric and positive. | **Proved.** |
| `posSqrtCLM` | `E →L[ℝ] E` | `posSqrt` packaged as a continuous linear map. | **Proved.** |
| `posSqrtCLM_isSelfAdjoint` / `posSqrtCLM_adjoint` | `IsSelfAdjoint posSqrtCLM` / `adjoint posSqrtCLM = posSqrtCLM` | Self-adjointness of the continuous square root. | **Proved.** |
| `posSqrtCLM_comp_self` | `posSqrtCLM ∘L posSqrtCLM = T.toContinuousLinearMap` | Continuous square law. | **Proved.** |

## 10j'. `Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Cholesky.lean` — real Cholesky factorization (existence + uniqueness)

The **Cholesky factorization** of a real symmetric positive-definite matrix `M : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ`: there is a unique upper-triangular matrix `U` with strictly positive diagonal such that `M = Uᵀ U` (here "upper-triangular" means `j < i → U i j = 0`, all strictly-below-diagonal entries vanish). Existence is derived from Mathlib's LDL decomposition (`LDL.lower_conj_diag`) by absorbing the square roots of the diagonal factor: `U = √D · Lᵀ` where `L = LDL.lower` and `D = LDL.diag`. Uniqueness reduces to the fact that an orthogonal upper-triangular matrix with positive diagonal is the identity. Mathlib has LDL but no Cholesky; upstream candidate. Built for the causal-disentanglement formalization. Namespace `Causalean.Mathlib.LinearAlgebra`. Sorry-free (axioms: `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`).

| Declaration | Statement | Description | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `IsUpperTri` / `isUpperTri_iff_blockTriangular` | `∀ i j, j < i → U i j = 0` / `↔ U.BlockTriangular id` | Strict upper-triangularity predicate and its identification with Mathlib's `BlockTriangular id`. | **Proved.** |
| `ldl_lowerInv_diag_one` | `LDL.lowerInv hM i i = 1` | The Gram-Schmidt lower-inverse matrix is unitriangular (diagonal entries are `1`). | **Proved.** |
| `ldl_diagEntries_pos` | `0 < LDL.diagEntries hM i` | The LDL diagonal entries of a positive-definite matrix are strictly positive (each is `xᵀMx > 0` for the nonzero `x = lowerInv` row). | **Proved.** |
| `ldl_lowerInv_blockTriangular` / `ldl_lower_blockTriangular` | `(…).BlockTriangular toDual` | `LDL.lowerInv` and `LDL.lower` are lower-triangular. | **Proved.** |
| `ldl_lower_diag_one` | `LDL.lower hM i i = 1` | `LDL.lower` is unitriangular (inverse of a unitriangular lower-triangular matrix). | **Proved.** |
| `cholesky_exists` | `∃ U, (∀ i j, j<i → U i j = 0) ∧ (∀ i, 0 < U i i) ∧ M = Uᵀ U` | **Existence.** Every real positive-definite matrix factors as `Uᵀ U` with `U` upper-triangular, positive-diagonal. | **Proved.** |
| `orthogonal_upperTri_pos_diag_eq_one` | `Wᵀ W = 1 → upper-tri → pos-diag → W = 1` | **Key uniqueness lemma.** An orthogonal upper-triangular matrix with positive diagonal is the identity (its transpose is both upper and lower triangular, hence diagonal, hence `±1`, hence `1`). | **Proved.** |
| `cholesky_unique` | `M = Uᵀ U = Vᵀ V → (both upper-tri pos-diag) → U = V` | **Uniqueness.** The factorization is unique: `W = V U⁻¹` is orthogonal upper-triangular with positive diagonal, so `W = 1`. | **Proved.** |

## 10k. `Mathlib/MeasureTheory/PartitionIntegral.lean` — finite-partition integral algebra

Decomposing an integral over the fibers of a finite-valued measurable map `H : Ω → ι` (a finite partition of the sample space). Causal-agnostic, Mathlib-shaped measure theory (a Mathlib-PR candidate); relocated here from `Stat/` so any layer (estimation, panel cell algebra, partial-ID) can use it without pulling in `Stat/` or `PO/`. Complements `Causalean.PO.integral_eq_sum_measure_mul_eventCondExp` (the `eventCondExp`/measure-weighted form for an explicit set family): here the form is measurable-map / set-integral, plus the cell-constant pull-out the `PO` lemma does not provide. Index type carries `[Fintype ι] [MeasurableSpace ι] [MeasurableSingletonClass ι]`; no measurability of the cell-weight `c : ι → ℝ` is needed (it is constant on each fiber). Namespace `Causalean.Mathlib.MeasureTheory`.

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `integral_eq_sum_setIntegral_fiber` | `∫ f = ∑ h, ∫_{H⁻¹{h}} f` | **Fiber decomposition.** For integrable `f` and finite-valued measurable `H`, the integral splits as the sum of set-integrals over the fibers. Wraps `integral_iUnion_fintype` over the fiber cover of `univ`. **Proved.** |
| `integral_cellConst_mul` | `∫ c(H ω)·f ω = ∑ h, c h · ∫_{H⁻¹{h}} f` | **Cell-constant pull-out.** An integrand weighted by a cell-dependent value `c (H ω)` decomposes with `c h` pulled out per cell. Workhorse for panel cell-by-cell regression algebra and cell-weighted-average estimands. No measurability of `c` required. **Proved.** |
| `integral_cellConst` | `∫ c(H ω) = ∑ h, c h · μ(H⁻¹{h})` | **Cell-weight aggregation.** For a finite measure, the integral of a cell-constant function is the cell-weighted sum of cell masses. Special case of `integral_cellConst_mul` with `f ≡ 1`. **Proved.** |

## 10k'. `Mathlib/MeasureTheory/CondExpIndicatorTower.lean` — conditioning ↔ inner-regression weighting

Causal-agnostic conditional-expectation identity (a Mathlib-PR candidate; namespace `MeasureTheory`): the measure-theoretic kernel behind "regression adjustment = inverse-propensity weighting". Reused by `regression_adjustment` (§9g) and earmarked for the ATT/DTR sequential analogs.

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `condExp_setIndicator_condExp_of_le` | `(hm : m ≤ m') (hm' : m' ≤ m0) [SigmaFinite (μ.trim hm')] (hs : MeasurableSet[m'] s) (hf : Integrable f μ) → μ[s.indicator f \| m] =ᵐ μ[s.indicator (μ[f\|m']) \| m]` | **Masked outcome ↔ inner regression.** Conditioning the masked `1_s·f` on coarse `m` equals conditioning its inner regression `μ[f\|m']` (with `s` `m'`-measurable). Proof: inner `condExp_indicator` + tower `condExp_condExp_of_le`. With `m=σ(X)`, `m'=σ(D,X)`, `s={D=d}`, dividing by `μ[1_s\|m]` turns the LHS into the IPW/adjustment functional, the RHS into the regression. **Proved.** |

## 10k''. `Mathlib/MeasureTheory/FiniteAtomicMeasure.lean` — probability measures carried by finitely many atoms

Model-agnostic measure theory for a probability measure whose mass sits on a finite embedded family of points: the decomposition into weighted Dirac measures, transfer of an almost-sure property down to a single positive-mass atom, and the automatic integrability that finite atomic support buys. Promoted out of the transported-LATE frontier run, where the finite-cell model class needs all three.

<!-- GEN:Causalean.Mathlib.MeasureTheory.FiniteAtomicMeasure -->
| Decl | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Mathlib.MeasureTheory.measure_eq_fin_sum_smul_dirac_of_range` | `(∀ (i : ι), MeasurableSet {cell i}) → μ (Set.range ⇑cell) = μ Set.univ → μ = ∑ i, μ {cell i} • MeasureTheory.Measure.dirac (cell i)` | Let `μ` be a finite measure and `cell` an injective family of finitely many points of the sample space, indexed by a finite type `ι`. If every singleton `{cell i}` is measurable and `μ` assigns its full mass to the range of `cell`, i.e. `μ` puts no mass outside these finitely many points, then `μ` equals the sum, over the index `i`, of the point mass `μ {cell i}` scaling the Dirac measure at `cell i`. |
| `Mathlib.MeasureTheory.property_at_of_ae_of_singleton_pos` | `(∀ᵐ (y : 𝒳) ∂μ, p y) → μ {x} ≠ 0 → p x` | An almost-sure property holds at every point to which the measure assigns nonzero mass. |

## 10k'''. `Mathlib/MeasureTheory/SetIntegralRecovery.lean` — recovering a measure or a pointwise bound from set integrals

Two dual "know it on every measurable set, conclude it globally" facts: a finite measure whose mass on every event equals the integral of a nonnegative weight over that event *is* the reweighted measure, and a function whose set integrals are dominated by the measure of the set is bounded by one almost everywhere. The second deliberately avoids assuming integrability — the proof truncates to bounded slices, which is what makes it usable when the function is only pinned down by set-integral identities.

<!-- GEN:Causalean.Mathlib.MeasureTheory.SetIntegralRecovery -->
| Decl | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Mathlib.MeasureTheory.measure_eq_withDensity_of_toReal_setIntegral` | `MeasureTheory.Integrable w μ → (∀ (A : Set α), MeasurableSet A → (ν A).toReal = ∫ (x : α) in A, w x ∂μ) → ν = μ.withDensity fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (w x)` | If a weight function `w` is integrable with respect to a reference measure `μ` and a finite measure `ν`'s mass on every measurable event `A` equals, as a real number, the integral of `w` over `A` against `μ`, then `ν` is obtained from `μ` by weighting with the nonnegative part of `w`: `ν = μ.withDensity (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (w x))`. |
| `Mathlib.MeasureTheory.abs_le_one_ae_of_setIntegral_le_measure` | `Measurable f → (∀ (A : Set Ω), MeasurableSet A → \|∫ (x : Ω) in A, f x ∂mu\| ≤ (mu A).toReal) → ∀ᵐ (x : Ω) ∂mu, \|f x\| ≤ 1` | A measurable function is bounded in absolute value by one almost everywhere if the absolute value of its integral over every measurable event is at most that event's measure. |
<!-- /GEN -->

## 10k''''. `Mathlib/MeasureTheory/AnalyticSetUniversalMeasurability.lean` — universal measurability of analytic events

This roll-up exposes a reusable descriptive-set-theory bridge for statistical arguments on Polish sample spaces: analytic events are measurable after completing any finite Borel sampling measure. It also supplies the minimal function-level corollary needed for upper-semi-analytic losses, whose completed lower integral agrees with their outer integral under the original measure. The results are Mathlib-shaped, paper-agnostic measure theory in the native `MeasureTheory` namespace.

<!-- GEN:Causalean.Mathlib.MeasureTheory.AnalyticSetUniversalMeasurability -->
_(no documented declarations in Causalean.Mathlib.MeasureTheory.AnalyticSetUniversalMeasurability)_
<!-- /GEN -->

### `Mathlib/MeasureTheory/AnalyticSetUniversalMeasurability/Capacity.lean` — Choquet capacities

The Choquet-capacity machinery establishes compact approximation for analytic events in Polish spaces. Its representative result says an analytic event has capacity equal to the supremum over its compact subsets.

<!-- GEN:Causalean.Mathlib.MeasureTheory.AnalyticSetUniversalMeasurability.Capacity -->
| Decl | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `MeasureTheory.ChoquetCapacity` | `(Ω : Type u_2) → [TopologicalSpace Ω] → Type u_2` | A Choquet capacity on a topological sample space bundles an extended-real-valued set function that is monotone under set inclusion, continuous from below along increasing sequences of sets, finite on every compact set, and right-continuous at compact sets: any strict upper bound on a compact set's value is already an upper bound on some open neighborhood of that compact set. |
| `MeasureTheory.instCoeFunChoquetCapacityForallSetENNReal` | `CoeFun (MeasureTheory.ChoquetCapacity Ω) fun x => Set Ω → ENNReal` | A Choquet capacity coerces to its underlying extended-nonnegative set function. |
| `MeasureTheory.ChoquetCapacity.mono` | `s ⊆ t → c.toFun s ≤ c.toFun t` | Capacity values are monotone under inclusion. |
| `MeasureTheory.ChoquetCapacity.isCompact_lt_top` | `IsCompact K → c.toFun K < ⊤` | Capacity values on compact sets are finite. |
| `MeasureTheory.ChoquetCapacity.exists_isOpen_superset_lt` | `IsCompact K → ∀ {a : ENNReal}, c.toFun K < a → ∃ U, K ⊆ U ∧ IsOpen U ∧ c.toFun U < a` | A strict upper bound for the capacity of a compact set also bounds some open neighborhood. |
| `MeasureTheory.ChoquetCapacity.IsCapacitable` | `MeasureTheory.ChoquetCapacity Ω → Set Ω → Prop` | A set is capacitable when its capacity is the supremum of the capacities of its compact subsets. |
| `MeasureTheory.AnalyticSet.isCapacitable` | `MeasureTheory.AnalyticSet s → c.IsCapacitable s` | Choquet's capacitability theorem. On a Polish sample space, if a set `s` is analytic — the continuous image of a Polish space, or empty, then `s` is capacitable for every Choquet capacity `c`: the capacity of `s` equals the supremum, over the compact subsets of `s`, of their capacities. |
| `MeasureTheory.Measure.toChoquetCapacity` | `(μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω) → [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure μ] → MeasureTheory.ChoquetCapacity Ω` | The outer-measure set function associated with a finite Borel measure on a Polish space is a Choquet capacity. |
| `MeasureTheory.Measure.toChoquetCapacity_apply` | `μ.toChoquetCapacity.toFun s = μ s` | The capacity induced by a finite measure assigns every event exactly that measure's outer mass. |

Capacitability for the outer measure of a finite Borel measure yields the library’s public universal-measurability theorem for analytic events.

## 12. `Stat/` — Causal-agnostic statistical primitives

Foundation layer for the estimation and inference modules: i.i.d. samples, convergence
modes, asymptotic linearity, Neyman orthogonality, and one-shot sample
splits. Mirrors `doc/basic_concepts/po/estimation.tex` Sections 1–5. Files
here are deliberately project-agnostic and are candidates for upstream
contribution to Mathlib.

**Folder layout.** The top level keeps only the foundational `Sample.lean` and
the `SampleSplit.lean` umbrella; everything else is grouped by topic into
subfolders: `Limit/`
(convergence modes, continuous mapping, WLLN), `CLT/` (asymptotic linearity,
multivariate CLT, Gaussian limit, χ²), `Inference/` (Δ-method, variance
estimation, studentization, Wald), `Quantile/` (cdf/quantile inference stack),
`MEstimation/` (Z/M-estimator CLT), `Orthogonality/` (Neyman orthogonality,
conditional-op helpers), `SampleSplit/` (cross-fitting + fold-restricted CLT),
`Minimax/` (Le Cam / Fano / Assouad lower bounds, §12w),
and `Concentration/` (vendored toolbox, §12'). Module paths below reflect this.

### 12np. `Stat/Nonparametric/Approximation/HolderInterpolation.lean` — Multivariate Hölder interpolation

This reusable minimax lower-bound primitive turns a pointwise separation between
Hölder-smooth functions into a local L¹ separation. It supplies the generic
moment-cancelling product kernel and the resulting multidimensional interpolation
inequality used by two-point and Assouad arguments.

<!-- GEN:Causalean.Stat.Nonparametric.Approximation.HolderInterpolation.Defs -->

| `Stat.Nonparametric.supBall_eq_pi` | `Causalean.Stat.Nonparametric.supBall x0 r = Set.univ.pi fun i => Set.Icc (x0 i - r) (x0 i + r)` | A closed sup-norm ball — the axis-aligned cube of half-width `r` centred at a point — is exactly the product of the coordinate intervals of radius `r` around the centre's coordinates. |

### 12a0. `Stat/Coupling/ProductLossMonotoneCoupling/` — Product-loss monotone couplings

Coupling-based statistical primitives for extremal dependence with fixed real marginals.
This stack builds explicit comonotone and countermonotone quantile couplings, proves
the sharp Fréchet-Hoeffding cdf envelopes, derives Hoeffding's covariance identity,
and concludes that the product expectation is maximized and minimized by those two
monotone couplings under finite second moments.

### 12a2. `Stat/Sample/EmpiricalMass.lean`

The empirical frequency of a single point in an i.i.d. sample, with its exact first two moments — the mean recovers the population mass, and the second moment is the multinomial formula `p² + (p − p²)/m`.

<!-- GEN:Causalean.Stat.Sample.EmpiricalMass -->
| Decl | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Stat.empiricalMass` | `(Fin N → 𝒳) → 𝒳 → ℝ` | The empirical mass of a point is the fraction of sample observations equal to that point. |
| `Stat.abs_empiricalMass_le_one` | `\|Causalean.Stat.empiricalMass sample x\| ≤ 1` | The absolute empirical mass of any point is at most one, including for the empty sample. |
| `Stat.integral_empiricalMass` | `0 < m → ∀ (a : 𝒳), MeasurableSet {a} → (∫ (sample : Fin m → 𝒳), Causalean.Stat.empiricalMass sample a ∂MeasureTheory.Measure.pi fun x => μ) = μ.real {a}` | Expected empirical mass. Given a positive sample size $m$ and a measurable singleton `{a}`, the expectation, under the $m$-fold product sampling measure, of the empirical mass of the point `a` — the fraction of sample observations equal to `a` — equals the population probability of `{a}`. |
| `Stat.integral_empiricalMass_sq` | `0 < m → ∀ (a : 𝒳), MeasurableSet {a} → (∫ (sample : Fin m → 𝒳), Causalean.Stat.empiricalMass sample a ^ 2 ∂MeasureTheory.Measure.pi fun x => μ) = μ.real {a} ^ 2 + (↑m)⁻¹ * (μ.real {a} - μ.real {a} ^ 2)` | Second moment of the empirical mass. Given a positive sample size $m$ and a measurable singleton `{a}`, the second moment, under the $m$-fold product sampling measure, of the empirical mass of the point `a` equals the squared population probability of `{a}` plus the usual binomial sampling correction $(1/m)(\mu(\{a\})-\mu(\{a\})^2)$. |
<!-- /GEN -->

### 12a3. `Stat/Sample/CollisionEstimator.lean`

### 12a4. `Stat/Sample/EffectiveSampleSize.lean`

Kish design effect and effective sample size for a weighted i.i.d. sample. When the weights have population mean one their second moment is the design effect, and dividing the nominal sample size by it gives the effective sample size; this file supplies the "design effect is at least one" fact and the empirical statistic's mean, its variance bound under a fourth-moment envelope, and its lower-tail bound.

### 12a5. `Stat/Sample/OccupancyWeightedMean/` — occupancy-weighted within-group means

Totalized occupancy-weighted differences of treated and control within-group
sample means, together with a weak-second-moment variance bound under fixed
overlap. The construction covers empty samples, empty group types, zero-mass
groups, and empirical zero-count boundaries without bounded outcomes.

### 12a6. `Stat/Sample/FiniteStratumMarkedRatioMse/` — fixed-stratum marked ratios

Totalized finite-stratum arm means and treated-minus-control scores for a
deterministic set of categories. The error decomposition keeps centered mark
noise, empirical category-mass fluctuation, and the remainder from empirically
empty arms separate. Exact missing-count moments and overlap bounds combine to
give square-integrability and boundary-safe mean-squared-error guarantees under
cellwise second moments, without requiring bounded outcomes.

Given a measurable event `E` in the space of length-`n` outcome tuples whose product-measure probability under `n` independent copies of the population law is at least $1-\delta$, the pullback of `E` along the joint observable built from the first `n` coordinates of the i.i.d. sample is a measurable event on the underlying sample space, with probability at least $1-\delta$. |

| `Stat.measurePreserving_pi_restrict` | `MeasureTheory.MeasurePreserving (fun s i => s ↑i) (MeasureTheory.Measure.pi fun x => μ) (MeasureTheory.Measure.pi fun x => μ)` | Dropping the coordinates outside a decidable sub-index of an i.i.d. product sample leaves the i.i.d. product sample over that sub-index. |

| `Stat.map_pi_restrict_finset` | `MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun s i => s ↑i) (MeasureTheory.Measure.pi fun x => μ) = MeasureTheory.Measure.pi fun x => μ` | The law of the coordinates in a finite index set of an i.i.d. product sample is the product law over that finite set; this is the pushforward packaging of the measure-preserving statement. |
| `Stat.integral_comp_pi_restrict_finset` | `(∫ (s : ι → X), g fun i => s ↑i ∂MeasureTheory.Measure.pi fun x => μ) = ∫ (z : ↥S → X), g z ∂MeasureTheory.Measure.pi fun x => μ` | Averaging a function of the coordinates in a finite index set over the whole i.i.d. product sample is the same as averaging it over an i.i.d. product sample indexed by that finite set. |

| `IsLittleOp.mul_isBigOp` | `o_p(rn)·O_p(sn) = o_p(rn·sn)` | Requires `0 < rn n`, `0 < sn n` for all `n`. **Proved.** |
| `IsBigOp.add` | `O_p(rn) + O_p(rn) = O_p(rn)` | **Proved.** |
| `IsBigOp.mul_isLittleOp_one_isLittleOp` | Slutsky-style: `O_p(1)·o_p(1) = o_p(1)` | **Proved.** |

| `IsBigOp.const_mul_tendsto_zero` | `Xn = O_p(1)` ∧ `aₙ → 0` ⇒ `aₙ·Xn = o_p(1)` | Degenerate Slutsky: bounds the bad event `{ε < |aₙ Xn|}` by `{M < |Xn|}` once `|aₙ| < ε/M`, using only the deterministic shrinkage `|aₙ| → 0`. **Proved by Codex.** Δ-method helper. |

### 12b'. `Stat/Limit/ConvergenceVec.lean`

Vector analogue of `Convergence.lean`'s `Tendsto_dist` plus the Slutsky lemmas needed by the multivariate Δ-method (`Stat/Inference/DeltaMethod.lean`) and the vector asymptotic-normality corollary (`Stat/CLT/AsymptoticLinearityVec.lean`).

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Tendsto_dist_vec` | `def` | Vector convergence in distribution: `μ.map (Xn n)` converges weakly to `Q` in `ProbabilityMeasure E` for `E` a pseudo-metric space with `OpensMeasurableSpace`. Direct port of scalar `Tendsto_dist`. |
| `Tendsto_dist_vec.add_isLittleOp_one` | vector Slutsky absorption | `Xn ⇒ Q` and `‖Yn − Xn‖ = o_p(1)` ⇒ `Yn ⇒ Q`, on `[NormedAddCommGroup E] [BorelSpace E]`. **Proved by Codex** as a metric-space port of the scalar proof using the bounded-Lipschitz portmanteau characterization (`tendsto_iff_forall_lipschitz_integral_tendsto`); integrand `F : E → ℝ` is split over `{‖F (Yn) − F (Xn)‖ < L·ε/2}` and its complement, with the complement controlled via Lipschitz pullback through `‖Yn − Xn‖`. |
| `Tendsto_dist_vec.congr_ae` | eventual a.e. congruence | Vector analogue of `Tendsto_dist.congr_ae`. **Proved.** |
| `Tendsto_dist_vec.map_continuous` | continuous-map pushforward | `g : E → F` continuous ⇒ `Tendsto_dist_vec Xn Q μ` ⇒ `Tendsto_dist_vec (g ∘ Xn) (Q.map g) μ`. **Proved by Codex** via `MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure.tendsto_map_of_tendsto_of_continuous`. Used by the multivariate Δ-method to push forward by the Fréchet derivative `Dg`. |

### 12c'. `Stat/CLT/AsymptoticLinearityVec.lean`

Vector-θ companion to `AsymptoticLinearity.lean`. Adds the vector-valued asymptotic-linearity predicate `IsAsymLinearVec` parametric in a Euclidean space `E`, plus a bridge to the scalar form when `E = ℝ`, and the headline multivariate asymptotic-normality corollary.

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `IsAsymLinearVec θn θ₀ ψ S I` | structure | Vector-valued asymptotic linearity at `θ₀ : E` with vector IF `ψ : X → E`. Fields: `mean_zero` (Bochner integral), `finite_var` (`‖ψ‖² ∈ L¹`), `remainder` (norm `o_p(1)`). |
| `IsAsymLinearVec.normalizedSum`, `rescaledEstimator` | `def`s | Vector versions of the scalar accessors. |
| `IsAsymLinearVec.toScalar` | bridge | When `E = ℝ`, `IsAsymLinearVec` reduces to scalar `IsAsymLinear`. **Proved**: field-by-field rewrite using `‖x‖ = |x|` and `r • x = r * x` on `ℝ`. |
| `IsAsymLinear.toVec` | bridge | Scalar-to-vector lift. **Proved** (mirror of `toScalar`). |
| `IsAsymLinearVec.tendsto_normal_vec` | `theorem` | Multivariate analogue of `tendsto_normal`: given a vector CLT contact `_hCLT` (the partial-sum pushforward converges to `Q : ProbabilityMeasure E`), the rescaled estimator pushforward also converges to `Q`. **Proved by Codex** by absorbing `_h.remainder` into `_hCLT` via `Tendsto_dist_vec.add_isLittleOp_one`. The multivariate CLT itself is left to the caller. |

Envelope-based stochastic-order helpers + Cauchy–Schwarz packaging. Consumed by `PlugIn.lean` (single-factor bias) and `Remainder.lean` (product-rate AIPW bias). Causal-agnostic; candidate for upstream Mathlib contribution once stable.

### 12h. `Stat/SampleSplit/FoldBEmpiricalProcess.lean`

Empirical-process bounds on a centered evaluation-fold sum of a training-fold-measurable random function. Consumed by `DMLChernozhukov.lean` (one-shot) and `DMLCrossFit.lean` (K-fold). The file is structured in three layers:

1. **Abstract layer (private)** — parameterised over an arbitrary evaluation-fold schedule `eval : ℕ → Finset ℕ`, training σ-algebra `m_train : ℕ → MeasurableSpace Ω`, plus independence and iid-product-law hypotheses.
2. **OneShot wrappers** — preserved public signatures `foldB_centered_sum_isLittleOp_one` and `sqrtFoldB_integral_isLittleOp_one`, now thin instantiations of the abstract layer.
3. **K-fold corollaries** — new public lemmas under `KFoldSplit.*` namespace.

#### Abstract layer (private)

|---|---|---|
| `centeredEvalSum_sq_lintegral_le_core` / `centeredEvalSum_sq_lintegral_le` | `∫⁻ ω, ((1/√\|eval n\|) Σ_{eval n} (g(Z_i) − ∫g dP))² ∂μ ≤ ∫⁻ ω, ‖g(n,ω)‖²_{L²(P)} ∂μ` | Second-moment bound on the centered eval-sum, parametric in `(eval, m_train, h_train_le, h_indep, h_iid)`. **Proved** via the generic `iid_centered_sum_sq_lintegral_le` helper in `Causalean/Mathlib/IIDCenteredSum.lean`. |
| `evalSum_truncated_isLittleOp_one` | bounded `g` with `∫⁻ ‖g‖²₂ → 0` ⇒ centered eval-sum is `o_p(1)` | Markov / Chebyshev in `ENNReal` plus bounded convergence. **Proved by Codex (A0)** via `MeasureTheory.meas_ge_le_lintegral_div`. Eventual `0 < (eval n).card` from a separate `h_eval_card_grow` hypothesis. |

Fix a probability space `(Ω, Q)`, real-valued functions `A`, `B`, `K` on it, and a region of the line with finite Lebesgue measure. Suppose further a positive scale `kappa`, a nonnegative inflation factor `inflation` and nonnegative slack `Y`, with `Kbar` controlled by `inflation · kappa` and the bad-event contribution `(vol region) · q` controlled by `Y / t`, where `t` is defined as `n · mu² / kappa`. Then the `Q`-expected restricted volume of the affine-inversion set built from `A`, `B` and the shrinking radius `L · √(K/n)` is at most `max(vol region, 4·√inflation·L + Y) · min(1, t^(-1/2))`. |

### 12j. `Stat/Inference/DeltaMethod.lean`

Smooth-function CLT. Two forms; both proved.

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `deltaMethod_scalar` | `theorem` | If `√n (T_n − t₀) ⇒ N(0, σ²)` and `g : ℝ → ℝ` differentiable at `t₀` with derivative `g'`, then `√n (g T_n − g t₀) ⇒ N(0, g'² σ²)`. **Proved by Codex.** Pipeline: tightness of `√n (T_n − t₀)` via `Tendsto_dist.tightness`; consistency `T_n − t₀ →_p 0` via `IsBigOp.const_mul_tendsto_zero` against `(√n)⁻¹ → 0`; remainder `Rn := √n · (g(T_n) − g t₀ − g' (T_n − t₀))` is `o_p(1)` from `HasDerivAt.isLittleO_sub` on the localizing event `{|T_n − t₀| < ρ}`; finally `Tendsto_dist.const_mul_tendsto_gaussian` for `g' · √n (T_n − t₀)` and `Tendsto_dist.add_isLittleOp_one` to absorb `Rn`. |
| `deltaMethod` | `theorem` | Multivariate form: `√n • (T_n − t₀) ⇒ Q` (vector limit) and `g : E → F` Fréchet-differentiable at `t₀` with derivative `Dg : E →L[ℝ] F` ⇒ `√n • (g T_n − g t₀) ⇒ Q.map Dg`. **Proved by Codex.** Vector port of the scalar pipeline: `‖√n • (T_n − t₀)‖` is `O_p(1)` via `Tendsto_dist_vec.map_continuous` along `‖·‖ : E → ℝ` plus `Tendsto_dist.tightness`; consistency `T_n − t₀ →_p 0` in norm; remainder controlled by `HasFDerivAt.isLittleO_sub`; linear pushforward `Dg` via `Tendsto_dist_vec.map_continuous` again; vector Slutsky absorption via `Tendsto_dist_vec.add_isLittleOp_one`. |

### 12j'. `Stat/Inference/HadamardDeriv.lean` + `Stat/Inference/FunctionalDelta.lean`

**Directional (Hadamard) functional delta method.** The Fréchet delta method (12j) cannot reach lattice functionals: an interval-identified parameter's sharp endpoints are `sup'`/`inf'` of separately estimable quantities (`PartialID/.../IntersectionBound.lean` `iInter_Icc_eq_Icc : ⋂ⱼ [Lⱼ,Uⱼ] = [sup' L, inf' U]`; Manski MIV envelopes; combined MTR+MTS bounds), and `max`/`min` are only *Hadamard directionally* differentiable — with a **nonlinear** derivative at a tie, which is exactly the binding/kink regime where bound inference is delicate (Hirano–Porter 2012; Fang–Santos 2019). References: van der Vaart (1998) §20.2; Shapiro (1991).

`HadamardDeriv.lean` (analysis core, no probability):

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `HasHadamardDirDerivAt φ φ' θ` | def | Sequential Hadamard directional differentiability over normed spaces: for every `h`, every `hₙ → h`, every `tₙ → 0⁺`, `(tₙ)⁻¹ • (φ(θ + tₙ•hₙ) − φθ) → φ' h`. `φ'` is positively homogeneous, *not* assumed linear. |
| `HasFDerivAt.hasHadamardDirDerivAt` | theorem | **Fréchet ⇒ Hadamard**: a Fréchet-differentiable `φ` (derivative `L`) is Hadamard directionally differentiable with derivative `L`. *(One `sorry`: the `(tₙ)⁻¹ • rₙ → 0` remainder step — standard `IsLittleO` divide-by-rate, off the critical path; the `max`/`min` results below do not use it.)* |
| `maxDirDeriv a b` / `minDirDeriv a b` | def | Directional derivative of `max`/`min : ℝ×ℝ → ℝ` at `(a,b)`: a coordinate projection off the diagonal, and `max`/`min` itself (sublinear) at the tie `a=b`. |
| `continuous_maxDirDeriv` / `continuous_minDirDeriv` | theorem | The directional derivatives are continuous. |
| `hasHadamardDirDerivAt_max` / `hasHadamardDirDerivAt_min` | theorem | `max`/`min` are Hadamard directionally differentiable at every `(a,b)` with the derivatives above. **Sorry-free, axiom-clean.** Tie case: `max(b+t h₁, b+t h₂) = b + t·max(h₁,h₂)`; off-diagonal: the dominating coordinate is eventually selected. |

`FunctionalDelta.lean` (the delta theorem; consumes the existing `Tendsto_dist_vec` weak-convergence infra):

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `isLittleOp_one_of_measure_ne_tendsto_zero` | theorem | Reusable Slutsky device: if `μ{Yₙ ≠ Xₙ} → 0` then `Yₙ − Xₙ = o_p(1)`. The ingredient for the *off-diagonal* case (lattice functional selects one coordinate except when the estimated ordering is wrong, an event of vanishing probability). **Proved.** |
| `instIsProbabilityMeasure_map_max` / `_min` | instance | The lattice pushforward `Q.map (z ↦ max/min z.1 z.2)` of a probability measure `Q` is a probability measure. Global instance, so the `Tendsto_dist` conclusions below need *not* assume it. |
| `sqrt_mul_max_sub` / `sqrt_mul_min_sub` | lemma | **The exact tie identity** `√n·(max/min âₙ b̂ₙ − a) = max/min(√n(âₙ−a), √n(b̂ₙ−a))` — the rescaled image equals the lattice functional applied to the joint rescaled deviation, with no remainder. |
| `maxStat_aemeasurable` / `minStat_aemeasurable` | lemma | The image statistic `√n·(max/min âₙ b̂ₙ − a)` is `AEMeasurable` for every `n`, *derived* from the joint deviation's measurability via the tie identity — so the delta theorems need *not* assume it. |
| `deltaMethod_max_tie` | theorem | **Directional delta method for `max` at a tie.** If `√n • ((âₙ,b̂ₙ) − (a,a)) ⇒ Q` on `ℝ×ℝ`, then `√n·(max âₙ b̂ₙ − a) ⇒ Q.map (z ↦ max z.1 z.2)` (generally *non-Gaussian* — the law of `max(Z₁,Z₂)`). The binding/kink case the Fréchet method cannot reach. **Sorry-free, axiom-clean.** Proof: the exact identity `√n(max âₙ b̂ₙ − a) = max(√n(âₙ−a), √n(b̂ₙ−a)) = max∘Sₙ` (`sqrt_mul_max_sub`), then continuous mapping (`Tendsto_dist_vec.map_continuous`) + `congr_ae`; no linearization remainder. Hypotheses: only the joint-deviation measurability `hSn_meas` and the joint CLT `hCLT` — the pushforward-probability instance and the image-statistic measurability are now discharged automatically (via the instance / `maxStat_aemeasurable`). |
| `deltaMethod_min_tie` | theorem | Companion for `min`. **Sorry-free, axiom-clean.** Same discharged-assumption shape. |

*Off-diagonal (`a ≠ b`) and the abstract `sup'`/`inf'`-over-finite-families forms are the natural follow-ups; the tie case is the novel/hard one and the reusable `isLittleOp_one_of_measure_ne_tendsto_zero` is the device for the off-diagonal reduction.*

### 12k. `Stat/MEstimation/ZEstimator.lean`

Parametric-inference regularity bundle (structure layer). Houses only `ZEstimatorRegularity`; the headline theorem `zEstimator_clt` lives downstream in `Stat/MEstimation/ZEstimatorCLT.lean` to keep the import DAG acyclic (the proof needs `Stat/MEstimation/EmpiricalExpansion.lean`, which itself imports this file for the structure).

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ZEstimatorRegularity ψ θ₀ P` | structure | Identification (`∫ ψ(·;θ₀) dP = 0`), Jacobian `J₀ : E →L[ℝ] E` + invertibility witness, Fréchet-derivative spec, finite var, measurability, plus three smoothness fields: `jacobian_continuity` (`ContinuousAt` of `θ ↦ ∫ ψ(·;θ) dP` at `θ₀`; redundant with `J₀_spec` but exposed for downstream convenience), `psi_int_neighborhood` (`ψ(·;θ)` is `P`-integrable on a neighborhood of `θ₀`), and `score_envelope` (integrable `L²` derivative envelope: ∃ `δ>0`, ∃ nonneg measurable `F : X → ℝ` with `F²∈L¹(P)` such that `‖ψθz−ψθ₀z‖ ≤ ‖θ−θ₀‖·F z` for all `z : X` and all `‖θ−θ₀‖<δ` (pointwise — produced by MVT on smooth scores; needed to transfer the bound to random sample-dependent `θn`) — this is the LaTeX-spec form of `def:par-smoothness` and is what discharges `score_diff_L2_isLittleOp_sqrt` via Markov + iid LLN on `F²`). Reference: `def:par-smoothness` (van der Vaart 1998 §5.6). |

### 12l. `Stat/MEstimation/EmpiricalExpansion.lean`

Empirical-process / linearization layer feeding `zEstimator_clt`. References: `def:par-smoothness`, `thm:par-z-clt` in `doc/basic_concepts/Semi-parametric Inference/parametric_inference.tex`; van der Vaart (1998) §5.6 Thm 5.41; Newey-McFadden (1994) §7.

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `StochEquicontAt ψ θ₀ P μ S θn` | `def` | Asymptotic-equicontinuity predicate at `θ₀` along `θn`: `∀ ε>0, ∃ δ>0` such that the empirical-process gap `(√n)⁻¹ Σ (ψ(θn,Z_i)−ψ(θ₀,Z_i)) − √n ∫ (ψ(θn,·)−ψ(θ₀,·)) dP` exceeding `ε` on `{‖θn−θ₀‖<δ}` has vanishing probability as `n→∞`. Standard Donsker-class hypothesis (van der Vaart 1998 Lemma 19.24 / §19.4); exposed as a hypothesis pending Mathlib's empirical-process layer. |
| `score_diff_L2_isLittleOp_sqrt` | `theorem` | Under `ZEstimatorRegularity` (in particular `score_envelope`) + consistency `θn →_p θ₀`, the sample mean square `(1/n) Σ_{i<n} ‖ψ(θn,Z_i) − ψ(θ₀,Z_i)‖²` is `o_p(1)`. ### 12l'. `Stat/MEstimation/ZEstimatorCLT.lean`

Headline theorem layer for the parametric-inference workhorse. Z- / M-estimator CLT for vector-valued estimating equations. OLS, MLE, IV-2SLS instantiate it. Imports `Stat/MEstimation/EmpiricalExpansion.lean`.

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `zEstimator_clt` | `theorem` | Under `ZEstimatorRegularity`, consistency, asymptotic equicontinuity (`hStochEquicont : StochEquicontAt ψ θ₀ P μ S θn`), the rate hypothesis `hRate : ‖θn − θ₀‖ = O_p(1/√n)`, and empirical-moment vanishing, `θn` is asymptotically linear at `θ₀` with IF `−J₀⁻¹ · ψ(·; θ₀)` (Chernozhukov form). Conclusion is `IsAsymLinearVec`. Reference: van der Vaart 1998 Thm 5.41. **Proved.** All three `IsAsymLinearVec` fields discharged: `mean_zero` (push `−J₀⁻¹` through Bochner integral via `identification`), `finite_var` (operator-norm bound on `J₀_inv` + `finite_var`), and `remainder` (combine `localStochasticExpansion` + `hMoment`, then bound the rescaled remainder by `J₀_inv` and the finite-dim left-inverse derived from `J₀_inverse`). The Donsker-step content is encapsulated in the `hStochEquicont` hypothesis, to be discharged per-instance until Mathlib's empirical-process layer lands. |

### 12l''. `Stat/MEstimation/ExtremumConsistency.lean` — discharging the CLT's consistency and equicontinuity hypotheses

Additive bridge: re-exposes the headline CLTs (`zEstimator_clt`, `gmm_asymptotically_linear`) with their two *opaque* hypotheses derived from clean primitives. **Consistency** `hConsistent` is derived from the primitive extremum conditions via the empirical-process layer's `mEstimator_consistent_of_glivenkoCantelli` (§12ep.c) — classical reduction (Newey–McFadden 1994 Thm 2.1; van der Vaart 1998 Thm 5.7): consistency follows from a Glivenko–Cantelli criterion plus a well-separated population maximum. **Equicontinuity** `hStochEquicont : StochEquicontAt` is derived from the *class-level* Donsker property `AsymptoticEquicont` (§12ep.d) via `stochEquicontAt_of_asymptoticEquicont` — the estimator-indexed modulus is reconstructed from the function-class property plus consistency. The original `hConsistent`/`hStochEquicont`-taking theorems are unchanged and remain available for callers who establish those by other means. Imports `Stat/GMM/AsymptoticNormality.lean` + `Stat/EmpiricalProcess/MEstimatorConsistency.lean` + `Stat/EmpiricalProcess/Equicontinuity/Modulus.lean`.

### 12l'''. Finite Poisson M-estimation substrate

Finite-dimensional Poisson projection tools: a total maximizer selector,
existence and uniqueness under positive weights and an injective linear design,
deterministic argmax stability and finite-table consistency, continuity under
mean perturbations, a one-cell implicit derivative, and the sign of a selected
scalar coefficient from a conditional nuisance fit.

### 12m. `Stat/Limit/ContinuousMapping.lean`

Estimator-agnostic convergence-in-probability primitives. Extracted from the (formerly `private`) helpers in `Estimation/NPIV/DR/AsymptoticNormal.lean` so any estimator can reuse them. Consumed by `Stat/Inference/Studentize.lean`.

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Tendsto_inProb.comp_continuousAt` | `Xn →_p c` ∧ `ContinuousAt g c` ⇒ `g∘Xn →_p g c` | Continuous-mapping theorem in probability at a **constant** limit `c`. ε-δ pullback of `ContinuousAt` through `tendstoInMeasure_iff_dist`. **Proved.** |
| `Tendsto_inProb.pi_comp_continuousAt` | finite `ι`, coordinatewise `Yₙᵢ →_p cᵢ`, `ContinuousAt g c` ⇒ `g(Yₙ) →_p g(c)` | Finite-Pi continuous-mapping theorem in probability. Converts coordinate tails to a finite union bound, then applies continuity in the product metric. **Proved.** |
| `Tendsto_inProb.matrix_comp_continuousAt` | entrywise `Mₙᵢⱼ →_p M₀ᵢⱼ`, `ContinuousAt g M₀` ⇒ `g(Mₙ) →_p g(M₀)` | Matrix-valued corollary of the finite-Pi theorem, reindexing entries by `K×K`. **Proved.** |
| `Tendsto_inProb.inv` | `Yn →_p Y₀` ∧ `Y₀ ≠ 0` ⇒ `1/Yn →_p 1/Y₀` | Reciprocal continuity (special case of `comp_continuousAt` via `continuousAt_inv₀`). **Proved.** |
| `Tendsto_inProb.sub_const` | `Yn →_p Y₀` ⇒ `Yn − Y₀ →_p 0` | Center a convergence-in-probability statement at its constant limit. **Proved.** |
| `Tendsto_inProb.sub` | `Xn →_p a` ∧ `Yn →_p b` ⇒ `Xn − Yn →_p a − b` | Difference of two convergent-in-probability sequences (constant limits); ε/2 union bound (Mathlib lacks `TendstoInMeasure.sub`). **Proved.** |
| `Tendsto_inProb.isLittleOp_one` | `Yn →_p 0` ⇒ `Yn = o_p(1)` | Convergence in probability to zero is `o_p(1)`. **Proved.** |
| `Tendsto_inProb.isBigOp_one` | `Xn →_p c` ⇒ `Xn = O_p(1)` | In-probability tightness at a constant limit. **Proved.** |

### 12n. `Stat/Limit/WLLN.lean`

Generic weak law of large numbers for `IIDSample`, plus the consistent-variance corollary. Generalizes the Panel-specific `iidPanel_sampleMean_ae` (boundedness weakened to integrability; a.s. limit converted to in-probability). Supplies the `σ̂ₙ →_p σ²` consistency input that the studentized/Wald layer takes as a hypothesis.

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `IIDSample.measurable_sampleMean` | `Measurable g` ⇒ `Measurable (S.sampleMean g N)` | Measurability of the sample mean (finite sum of `g ∘ Z i`, scaled). **Proved.** |
| `IIDSample.sampleMean_tendsto_inProb` | `Integrable (g∘Z₀)` ⇒ `S.sampleMean g →_p ∫ g dP` | WLLN: i.i.d. sample mean converges in probability to the population mean. Wraps `strong_law_ae_real` (a.s.) then `tendstoInMeasure_of_tendsto_ae` on the finite measure `μ`; law transfer via `integral_map` + `S.law`. Requires `[IsProbabilityMeasure P]`. **Proved.** |
| `IIDSample.sampleSecondMoment_tendsto_inProb` | `Integrable (ψ²∘Z₀)` ⇒ `S.sampleMean ψ² →_p ∫ ψ² dP` | Consistent variance for a known influence function `ψ`: `(1/n)Σψ(Zᵢ)² →_p σ²`. Direct corollary with `g := ψ²`. **Proved.** |

### 12n.a. `Stat/Limit/ObservationDependentVanTrees/` — observation-dependent Bayesian Cramér–Rao bounds

Reusable van Trees infrastructure for σ-finite dominated observation models in which the estimand may depend jointly on the parameter and the observation. The final theorem combines guarded density-zero score algebra, absolute-continuity integration by parts, product-measure Fubini, and weighted L² Cauchy–Schwarz.

### 12n'. `Stat/SampleSplit/FoldBWLLN.lean`

Fold-B weak law of large numbers: the analogue of `sampleMean_tendsto_inProb` averaged over the evaluation fold `B(n)` of a `OneShotSplit` (a growing index subset) instead of the full sample. Unlike the full-sample WLLN (an SLLN/a.e. argument) this is a finite-variance Chebyshev argument over the fold, so it restricts cleanly to `B(n)`. Supplies the missing substrate for fold-B sample-mean consistency (e.g. the Jacobian-consistency input of the partially linear feasible-DML estimator).

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `OneShotSplit.foldB_sampleMean_tendsto_inProb` | `MemLp g 2 P` ⇒ `(1/\|B(n)\|)Σ_{i∈B(n)} g(Zᵢ) →_p ∫ g dP` | **Fold-B WLLN.** For a fixed finite-variance `g`, the fold-B sample mean converges in probability to the population mean. Proof: per-index variance/mean transport via `IdentDistrib.variance_eq`/`map`, `IndepFun.variance_sum` over the finset `B(n)` gives `Var = Var(g)/\|B(n)\|`, Chebyshev (`meas_ge_le_variance_div_sq`) and `\|B(n)\|→∞` (`foldB_card_tendsto`) close it (empty folds handled via the eventual filter). **Proved.** |

Multivariate CLT via the **Cramér–Wold device**, the vector analogue of `clt_normalized_sum`. Discharges the multivariate CLT contact `_hCLT` taken as a hypothesis by `IsAsymLinearVec.tendsto_normal_vec` and `deltaMethod` (vector Δ-method). Weak convergence on a finite-dim real inner-product space `E` is reduced to pointwise charFun convergence (Lévy continuity, `ProbabilityMeasure.tendsto_iff_tendsto_charFun` from the `Clt` package); each direction's charFun is the scalar charFun of the projected sum `⟪t, vecNS⟫`, handled by the scalar CLT.

**Limit-law status:** the Cramér–Wold reduction and per-direction charFun limit `→ exp(−½∫⟪t,ψ⟫² dP)` are fully proven, sorry-free. The theorems here keep the target `Q` abstract, parameterized by `charFun Q t = exp(−½∫⟪t,ψ⟫² dP)`. That abstract hypothesis is **discharged concretely** in `Stat/CLT/GaussianLimit.lean` (see 12n'''c): `gaussianLimit ψ` is the covariance-`Σ` Gaussian built explicitly, and `IIDSample.clt_normalizedSum_vec` is the multivariate CLT against it with no abstract `Q`/charFun hypothesis remaining.

|---|---|---|

| `Tendsto_dist_vec.of_charFun_tendsto` | pointwise charFun convergence ⇒ `Tendsto_dist_vec` | **Cramér–Wold wrapper**. **Proved.** |
| `IIDSample.clt_normalizedSum_vec_of_charFun` | Gaussian-charFun `Q` ⇒ `vecNS ⇒ Q` | **Multivariate CLT contact**; discharges `_hCLT`. **Proved.** |
| `IsAsymLinearVec.tendsto_normal_vec_clt` | vector asym-linearity + Gaussian-charFun `Q` ⇒ rescaled estimator ⇒ Q | **End-to-end vector asymptotic normality** (no CLT hypothesis). **Proved.** |

### 12n''''. `Stat/Inference/WaldVec.lean`

Multivariate Wald / confidence-ellipsoid asymptotic coverage — the vector analogue of the scalar `Tendsto_dist.wald_coverage`. The Wald statistic `Wₙ = (√n(θ̂ₙ−θ₀))ᵀ Σ̂ₙ⁻¹ (√n(θ̂ₙ−θ₀))` is already ℝ-valued, so an ellipsoid `{θ : Wald ≤ c}` has coverage `χ(Iic c)` via one-sided portmanteau. The construction of `Wₙ` and the proof `Wₙ ⇒ χ` (continuous mapping of the joint limit through `(t,S) ↦ tᵀS⁻¹t`) is the caller's input, exactly as the scalar `wald_coverage` takes `Sₙ ⇒ N(0,1)`. The limit `χ` is kept abstract here, but identifying the image of the concrete Gaussian `gaussianLimit` (12n'''c) under the quadratic form `S ↦ SᵀΣ⁻¹S` as `χ²_d` is now **closed** in `Stat/Inference/ChiSquaredWald.lean` (12n'''d).

|---|---|---|
| `Tendsto_dist.wald_coverage_Iic` | `Wₙ ⇒ χ` ∧ `χ(∂Iic c)=0` ∧ bridge ⇒ `coverProb → χ(Iic c)` | **Ellipsoid coverage** via one-sided portmanteau on `Set.Iic c`. **Proved.** |
| `Tendsto_dist.wald_coverage_Iic_of_noAtoms` | `Wₙ ⇒ χ` (`[NoAtoms χ]`) ∧ bridge ⇒ `coverProb → χ(Iic c)` | Same, boundary-null discharged automatically for any atomless limit (e.g. non-degenerate χ²). **Proved.** |

### 12n'''d. `Stat/CLT/ChiSquared.lean` + `Stat/Inference/ChiSquaredWald.lean`

**χ² identification of the Wald limit.** `ChiSquared` *defines* the χ²_d law and `ChiSquaredWald` whitens `gaussianLimit` through the Wald quadratic form to recognise its image as χ²_d, closing the open step flagged in `WaldVec`. χ²_d is defined as the law of `‖W‖²` for `W ~ stdGaussian` (textbook squared-norm definition; the `Gamma(d/2,1/2)` density form is not developed — Mathlib has no χ²). The whitening: `gaussianLimit = stdGaussian.map √Σ`, and with `Σ` non-degenerate (injective ⇒ invertible in finite dim), `⟪√Σ w, Σ⁻¹(√Σ w)⟫ = ‖w‖²` by self-adjointness of `√Σ`.

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `chiSqDist` | `ℕ → Measure ℝ` | The χ²_d law: `(stdGaussian (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))).map ‖·‖²`. `IsProbabilityMeasure` instance. **Proved.** |
| `stdGaussian_map_linearIsometryEquiv` | `(stdGaussian E).map ι = stdGaussian F` for `ι : E ≃ₗᵢ F` | `stdGaussian` is isometry-invariant; matched characteristic functions (`charFun_isGaussian_centered` + `Measure.ext_of_charFun`, covariance preserved by `ι`). **Proved.** |
| `stdGaussian_map_normSq` | `(stdGaussian E).map ‖·‖² = chiSqDist (finrank ℝ E)` | The squared-norm law depends only on dimension. **Proved.** |
| `noAtoms_pi_normSq` / `noAtoms_chiSqDist` | `1 ≤ d ⇒ NoAtoms (chiSqDist d)` | χ²_d is atomless for `d ≥ 1` (squared first coordinate atomless, Fubini over the independent remainder; reduced to a product of 1-D Gaussians via `stdGaussian_map_normSq_eq_pi`). **Proved.** |
| `secondMomentInv` | `E →L[ℝ] E` | `Σ⁻¹ = (√Σ)⁻¹∘(√Σ)⁻¹` from injectivity of `Σ`; `secondMomentInv_secondMomentLM` / `secondMomentLM_secondMomentInv` certify it is the two-sided inverse. **Proved.** |
| `gaussianLimit_waldForm_map` | `(gaussianLimit ψ).map (S ↦ ⟪S, Σ⁻¹ S⟫) = chiSqDist (finrank ℝ E)` | **The χ² identification** (whitening through `√Σ`). **Proved.** |
| `Tendsto_dist.wald_coverage_chiSq` | `Wₙ ⇒ χ²_d` (`1≤d`) ∧ bridge ⇒ `coverProb → χ²_d(Iic c)` | WaldVec ellipsoid coverage specialised to the identified atomless limit `chiSqDist d`. **Proved.** |

### 12n'''e. `Stat/CLT/ChiSquaredProjection.lean` — squared-norm of a projected Gaussian is χ²

The law of `‖P z‖²` for an **orthogonal projection** `P` (self-adjoint idempotent) and `z ~ stdGaussian` is `χ²_{rank P}`. Reusable beyond GMM (F-tests, score/LM tests, rank-deficient Wald). Proof: corestrict `P` to its range `S`, transport by the orthonormal-basis isometry `S ≃ₗᵢ EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin r)`; the pushforward of `stdGaussian E` is `stdGaussian S` (centered, covariance = inner product, via `Measure.ext_of_charFun` — the crux is that the corestriction's adjoint is the inclusion because `P` fixes its range), then `stdGaussian_map_normSq`.

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `stdGaussian_map_normSq_orthogonalProjection` | `IsSelfAdjoint P` ∧ `P ∘L P = P` ⇒ `(stdGaussian E).map (‖P·‖²) = chiSqDist (finrank ℝ (range P))` | **Projected-Gaussian χ².** The squared norm of an orthogonally-projected standard Gaussian is `χ²` with rank-of-projection degrees of freedom. **Proved, axiom-clean.** |

Generic studentized-CLT and Wald-coverage engine, abstracted off the concrete TRAE-DR estimator (the NPIV/DR theorems now instantiate these). Portmanteau / Gaussian-boundary helpers are made public here.

Scales `Xn` by `1/σ₀` (`const_mul_tendsto_gaussian`); the remainder `Xn·(1/σ̂ − 1/σ₀)` is `O_p(1)·o_p(1)` via `tightness` + `comp_continuousAt`; absorbs with `add_isLittleOp_one`. **Proved.** |

### 12o'. `Stat/Bootstrap/` — Nonparametric bootstrap standard error

The econometric workhorse use of the bootstrap (`vce(bootstrap)`): estimate the standard error of an asymptotically-linear estimator by the bootstrap, then form a studentized / Wald interval. The key fact is that the nonparametric (multinomial / Efron) bootstrap variance of `√n(X̄* − X̄)` is **exactly** the empirical variance `(1/n)Σ(ψ(Zᵢ) − ψ̄ₙ)²` — not an asymptotic approximation — so a *consistent* bootstrap SE plugs straight into the generic studentized CLT / Wald coverage of `Stat/Inference/Studentize.lean`. The nonparametric percentile / percentile-t refinements (which need conditional weak convergence) remain out of scope, but the **Gaussian multiplier (wild) bootstrap** below now supplies an *exact* distributional law on the conditioned sample. Three files: `Variance.lean` (the exact variance identity + consistency), `CI.lean` (studentized CLT + Wald coverage), and `GaussianMultiplier.lean` (exact multiplier-bootstrap law).

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `IIDSample.bootstrapVar` | `noncomputable def`, `ℕ → Ω → ℝ` | Bootstrap variance: the conditional variance `E*[ψ²] − (E*ψ)² = sampleMean(ψ²) − (sampleMean ψ)²` of a single multinomial-bootstrap draw `ψ(Z*₁)` over the empirical distribution. |
| `IIDSample.bootstrapVar_eq_centered` | `bootstrapVar = (1/n)Σ(ψ(Zᵢ) − ψ̄ₙ)²` | **Exact variance identity** (`E*[(ψ−E*ψ)²]`), the centered empirical second moment; holds for every `n` (`field_simp`/`ring` after the centered-sum expansion). **Proved, axiom-clean.** |
| `IIDSample.bootstrapVar_nonneg` | `0 ≤ bootstrapVar S ψ n ω` | Nonnegativity — it is a sum of squares (`bootstrapVar_eq_centered`). **Proved.** |
| `IIDSample.bootstrapVar_tendsto_inProb` | meas/int/sq-int/mean-zero `ψ` ⇒ `bootstrapVar →ₚ ∫ ψ² dP` | **Consistency of the bootstrap variance**: `sampleMean(ψ²) →ₚ ∫ψ²` and `(sampleMean ψ)² →ₚ (∫ψ)²=0`, subtracted via `Tendsto_inProb.sub`. **Proved, axiom-clean.** |
| `IIDSample.bootstrapSE` | `noncomputable def`, `√(bootstrapVar)` | Bootstrap standard error of `√n θ̂` — the bootstrap estimate of the asymptotic SD `√(∫ψ²)`. |
| `IIDSample.bootstrapSE_tendsto_inProb` | same hyps ⇒ `bootstrapSE →ₚ √(∫ ψ² dP)` | **SE consistency**; `Tendsto_inProb.sqrt` of the variance consistency. Supplies the `σ̂ →ₚ σ₀` input of `div_tendsto_inProb_gaussian`. **Proved.** |
| `IIDSample.bootstrapStudentized` | `noncomputable def`, `√n(θ̂−θ₀)/σ̂ₙ` | The bootstrap studentized statistic (full-sample index family). |
| `bootstrap_studentized_tendsto` | `IsAsymLinear θn θ₀ ψ S range` ∧ `0<∫ψ²` ⇒ `√n(θ̂−θ₀)/σ̂ₙ ⇒ N(0,1)` | **Bootstrap studentized CLT**: `IsAsymLinear.tendsto_normal` (numerator `⇒ N(0,∫ψ²)`) + bootstrap-SE consistency through `Tendsto_dist.div_tendsto_inProb_gaussian`. **Proved, axiom-clean.** |
| `bootstrap_wald_coverage` | + `z>0` ∧ coverage-event bridge ⇒ `coverProb → N(0,1)([−z,z])` | **Bootstrap Wald asymptotic coverage**; instantiates `Tendsto_dist.wald_coverage` on the bootstrap studentized statistic. `z = z_{1−α/2}` gives the `1−α` interval `θ̂ₙ ± z_{1−α/2}·σ̂ₙ/√n`. **Proved, axiom-clean.** |

#### 12o''. `Stat/Bootstrap/GaussianMultiplier.lean` — exact Gaussian multiplier (wild) bootstrap law

The multiplier/wild bootstrap (van der Vaart §23; Mammen) attaches i.i.d. mean-zero multipliers `ξᵢ` to the recentred data `aᵢ = xᵢ − x̄ₙ`. With **standard Gaussian** multipliers the perturbed statistic is, on a *fixed* data vector, **exactly** a centred Gaussian — no CLT and no conditional-distribution machinery, because a linear combination of independent Gaussians is Gaussian with variances adding. Both declarations **proved, sorry-free, axiom-clean**.

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `map_weighted_sum_gaussian` | `iIndepFun ξ`, each `μ.map (ξ i) = gaussianReal 0 1` ⇒ `μ.map (ω ↦ ∑ i, a i · ξ i ω) = gaussianReal 0 ⟨∑ i, (a i)², _⟩` | **Core fact**: a weighted sum of i.i.d. standard Gaussians has law `N(0, ∑ aᵢ²)`. `Finset` induction peeling one summand: each `aᵢ ξᵢ ~ N(0, aᵢ²)` (`gaussianReal_map_const_mul`), the partial sum is independent of the new term (`iIndepFun.indepFun_finset_sum_of_notMem`), and their laws convolve (`gaussianReal_add_gaussianReal_of_indepFun`). |
| `multiplierBootstrap_law` | as above with `aᵢ = n^{-1/2}(xᵢ − x̄)` ⇒ law of `Tₙ* = n^{-1/2} ∑ i, (xᵢ − x̄) ξᵢ` is `gaussianReal 0 ⟨sₙ², _⟩` | **Exact law of the studentized multiplier-bootstrap mean**: the bootstrap statistic is exactly `N(0, sₙ²)` with `sₙ² = (1/n) ∑ (xᵢ − x̄)²` the fixed sample variance. Since `sₙ² →ₚ σ²`, this is the distributional bootstrap counterpart of the CLT limit `N(0, σ²)`. |

#### 12p. `Stat/Quantile/Quantile.lean` — Quantile function (generalized inverse of a cdf)

Causal-agnostic statistical primitive: the lower quantile function of a real
probability measure, `quantile μ τ := sInf {x | τ ≤ cdf μ x}`, the
left-continuous generalized inverse of Mathlib's `ProbabilityTheory.cdf`.
Mathlib has the cdf but no generalized inverse; this file supplies it plus the
order (Galois) characterisation. Project-agnostic; upstream-candidate.

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `quantileSet μ τ` | `def`, `Set ℝ` | The super-level set `{x | τ ≤ cdf μ x}` defining the quantile. |
| `quantile μ τ` | `noncomputable def`, `ℝ` | `sInf (quantileSet μ τ)` — the `τ`-quantile (left-continuous generalized inverse of the cdf). |
| `quantileSet_up_closed` | `lemma` | `x ∈ quantileSet μ τ → x ≤ x' → x' ∈ quantileSet μ τ` (cdf monotone). **Proved.** |
| `bddBelow_quantileSet` | `lemma` | For `0 < τ`, the super-level set is bounded below (cdf → 0 at −∞). **Proved.** |
| `nonempty_quantileSet` | `lemma` | For `τ < 1`, the super-level set is nonempty (cdf → 1 at +∞). **Proved.** |
| `le_cdf_quantile` | `lemma` | For `τ < 1`, `τ ≤ cdf μ (quantile μ τ)`. Uses right-continuity of the cdf. **Proved.** |
| `le_cdf_of_quantile_le` | `lemma` | For `τ < 1`, `quantile μ τ ≤ x → τ ≤ cdf μ x`. **Proved.** |
| `quantile_le_of_le_cdf` | `lemma` | For `0 < τ`, `τ ≤ cdf μ x → quantile μ τ ≤ x` (`csInf_le`). **Proved.** |
| `quantile_le_iff` | `theorem` | **Galois connection** on `(0,1)`: `quantile μ τ ≤ x ↔ τ ≤ cdf μ x`. **Proved.** |
| `quantile_mono` | `lemma` | Quantile monotone in `τ` on `(0,1)`. **Proved.** |

#### 12q. `Stat/Quantile/EmpiricalCDF.lean` — Empirical cumulative distribution function

Sample analogue of `cdf P`, `F̂ₙ(y) = (1/n) Σ 1{Z_i ≤ y}` (the `sampleMean` of the indicator `cdfStat y`), with its fixed-`y` influence function `cdfIF P y z = 1{z ≤ y} − F(y)`. Because `√n (F̂ₙ(y) − F(y))` *is* the normalized influence-function sum, the empirical cdf is asymptotically linear with an identically-zero remainder, giving the fixed-`y` CLT directly. Causal-agnostic base layer for `Stat/Quantile/SampleQuantile.lean`; upstream-candidate.

|---|---|---|

| `measurable_cdfStat`, `cdfStat_nonneg`, `cdfStat_le_one`, `cdfStat_sq` | `lemma`s | Measurability; `0 ≤ 1{·≤y} ≤ 1`; idempotence `(1{·≤y})² = 1{·≤y}`. **Proved.** |
| `integrable_cdfStat` | `lemma` | `cdfStat y` is integrable (bounded on a finite measure). **Proved.** |
| `integral_cdfStat` | `lemma` | `∫ 1{·≤y} dP = cdf P y` (= `P.real (Iic y)`). **Proved.** |
| `IIDSample.empiricalCDF S y` | `noncomputable def`, `ℕ → Ω → ℝ` | The empirical cdf `F̂ₙ(y)`, the `sampleMean` of `cdfStat y`. |
| `cdfIF P y` | `noncomputable def`, `ℝ → ℝ` | Fixed-`y` influence function `1{z ≤ y} − F(y)`. |

| `cdfIF_variance` | `lemma` | `∫ cdfIF² dP = F(y)(1 − F(y))`, the Bernoulli variance of `{Z ≤ y}`. **Proved.** |
| `isLittleOp_zero` | `lemma` | The zero sequence is `o_p(1)`. **Proved.** |

#### 12r. `Stat/Quantile/SampleQuantile.lean` — Sample-quantile asymptotics (Bahadur representation)

`√n`-asymptotic normality of a quantile-estimator sequence `q̂ₙ` for the `τ`-quantile of `P`, via the Bahadur representation with influence function `ψ_τ(z) = (τ − 1{z ≤ q₀})/f₀` and asymptotic variance `τ(1−τ)/f₀²`. The hard empirical-process (Donsker / asymptotic-equicontinuity) content — the `o_p(n^{-1/2})` Bahadur remainder — is **exposed as a hypothesis** in the `QuantileRegularity` bundle, mirroring the `StochEquicontAt` pattern of `Stat/MEstimation/EmpiricalExpansion.lean`; everything downstream is proved. Reusable by any quantile estimator (plain sample quantile, IPW-weighted QTE quantile, …) satisfying the expansion. References: Bahadur (1966); van der Vaart (1998) §21.

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `quantileIF τ q₀ f₀` | `noncomputable def`, `ℝ → ℝ` | Sample-quantile influence function `(τ − 1{z ≤ q₀})/f₀`. |
| `measurable_quantileIF` | `lemma` | Measurability of `quantileIF`. **Proved.** |
| `quantileIF_mean_zero` | `lemma` | `∫ ψ_τ dP = 0`, given `cdf P q₀ = τ`. **Proved.** |
| `quantileIF_sq_integrable` | `lemma` | `ψ_τ` is square-integrable (bounded by `(|τ|+1)/|f₀|`). **Proved.** |
| `quantileIF_variance` | `lemma` | `∫ ψ_τ² dP = τ(1−τ)/f₀²`, the classical sample-quantile asymptotic variance. **Proved.** |
| `QuantileRegularity S qn τ q₀ f₀` | `structure` (`Prop`) | Regularity bundle: `τ ∈ (0,1)`, density `f₀ > 0`, `cdf P q₀ = τ`, `HasDerivAt (cdf P) f₀ q₀`, and `bahadur` — the exposed Donsker remainder (= `IsAsymLinear.remainder` for `(q̂ₙ, q₀, ψ_τ)`). |
| `QuantileRegularity.isAsymLinear` | `lemma` | The bundle is an `IsAsymLinear` witness for `q̂ₙ` at `q₀` with IF `ψ_τ`. **Proved.** |
| `QuantileRegularity.tendsto_normal` | `theorem` | **Sample-quantile CLT** `√n (q̂ₙ − q₀) ⇒ N(0, τ(1−τ)/f₀²)`. **Proved** (specializes `IsAsymLinear.tendsto_normal` with the closed-form variance). |

#### 12s. `Stat/Quantile/EmpiricalQuantile.lean` — Sample quantile (empirical-cdf inverse)

The `τ`-sample quantile `q̂ₙ(τ) = quantile νₙ τ`, the generalized inverse of the empirical cdf, where `νₙ = (1/n) Σ_{i<n} δ_{Zᵢ}` is the empirical measure. Supplies the deterministic/structural facts (switching relation, monotonicity, atom bound) feeding the Bahadur derivation. **Fully proved, sorry-free, axiom-clean.**

|---|---|---|
| `IIDSample.empiricalMeasure S n ω` | `noncomputable def` | Empirical measure `(1/n) Σ_{i<n} δ_{Zᵢ}`. |
| `IIDSample.empiricalMeasure_isProbabilityMeasure` | `lemma` | For `0 < n`, `νₙ` is a probability measure. **Proved.** |
| `IIDSample.empiricalMeasure_real_Iic` | `lemma` | `νₙ.real (Iic y) = F̂ₙ(y)`. **Proved.** |
| `IIDSample.empiricalMeasure_cdf` | `lemma` | **cdf bridge** `cdf νₙ = F̂ₙ`. **Proved.** |
| `IIDSample.sampleQuantile S τ` | `noncomputable def` | Sample quantile `q̂ₙ(τ) = quantile νₙ τ`. |
| `IIDSample.sampleQuantile_le_iff` | `lemma` | **Switching relation** `q̂ₙ(τ) ≤ x ↔ τ ≤ F̂ₙ(x)` (`0<τ<1`, `0<n`). **Proved** (from `quantile_le_iff` + cdf bridge). |
| `IIDSample.empiricalCDF_monotone` | `lemma` | `y ↦ F̂ₙ(y)` is monotone. **Proved**. |
| `IIDSample.sampleQuantile_atom_bound` | `lemma` | **Atom bound** `\|F̂ₙ(q̂ₙ) − τ\| ≤ 1/n` a.s., under atomless `P` (`Continuous (cdf P)`); needs `[IsProbabilityMeasure μ]`. **Proved** (no-atoms from continuous cdf via `measure_singleton`/`leftLim`; a.s. tie-free from `IndepFun`+`NoAtoms`; discrete count `card(Cle q)=card(Clt)+card(Ceq)`, ties `≤1`, strict part `≤ nτ` via threshold below `q`). |

### 12v. `Stat/GMM/` — Generalized Method of Moments (Hansen 1982)

Abstract GMM stack over a moment model `g : E → X → F` (parameter `θ : E`,
moment vector valued in `F`, over-identified `dim E ≤ dim F`).  Three layers:
the pure operator-algebra **optimal-weighting theorem** (`VarianceAlgebra`), the
statistical **problem bundle + efficiency** (`Setup`), and **asymptotic
normality** as a corollary of the Z-estimator CLT (`AsymptoticNormality`).  All
declarations are namespace `Causalean.Stat`.  Spec: Hansen (1982); Newey &
McFadden (1994), §3.  All **sorry-free and axiom-clean**.

#### 12v.1. `Stat/GMM/VarianceAlgebra.lean` — sandwich/efficient variance algebra

Pure finite-dimensional operator algebra (no measure theory) on continuous
linear maps between real inner-product spaces.  Inverses are carried as *data
with two-sided witnesses* (mirroring `ZEstimatorRegularity.J₀_inv`), so no
operator inverse is constructed.

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `gmmBread G W` | `(adjoint G) ∘L W ∘L G : E →L E` | The **bread** `GᵀWG` of Jacobian `G : E →L F` and weighting `W : F →L F`; symmetric when `W` is, invertible at full-rank `G`, `W ≻ 0`. |
| `gmmSandwich G W Cov breadInv` | `breadInv ∘L Gᵀ ∘L W ∘L Cov ∘L W ∘L G ∘L breadInv` | The **sandwich asymptotic variance** `(GᵀWG)⁻¹ GᵀW Σ WG (GᵀWG)⁻¹`, given a two-sided inverse `breadInv` of the bread. (`Cov` = covariance `Σ`, since `Σ` is a reserved Lean token.) |
| `adjoint_inv_self` | `adjoint M = M` ∧ `M ∘L N = id` ⇒ `adjoint N = N` | Self-adjointness of a right inverse of a self-adjoint operator (left-inverse uniqueness). Single shared copy in `VarianceAlgebra.lean` (imported by `OverID.lean`; the former duplicate in `OverID.lean` is removed). |
| `adjoint_gmmBread` | `adjoint W = W` ⇒ `adjoint (gmmBread G W) = gmmBread G W` | (private) The bread is self-adjoint when `W` is. |
| `gmm_efficiency` | `(gmmSandwich G W Cov breadInv − effInv).IsPositive` | **GMM optimal-weighting theorem (Hansen 1982, Thm 3.2).** The sandwich variance dominates the efficient variance `effInv = (GᵀCov⁻¹G)⁻¹` in the Löwner order, with equality at `W = Cov⁻¹`. Proof: `V(W) − V★ = (A−B)Σ(A−B)ᵀ ⪰ 0` with `A = (GᵀWG)⁻¹GᵀW`, `B = (GᵀΣ⁻¹G)⁻¹GᵀΣ⁻¹`; the cross terms collapse to `V★` because `Σ`/`Σ⁻¹` cancel against the bread, and positivity is `IsPositive.conj_adjoint` on `Σ ⪰ 0`. **Proved, axiom-clean.** |

#### 12v.2. `Stat/GMM/Setup.lean` — GMM problem, influence function, efficiency

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `gmmScore G W g` | `fun θ x => adjoint G (W (g θ x))` | The **combined GMM score** `ψ(θ,x) = GᵀW g(θ,x)`; its empirical zero is the (linearized) GMM estimator (FOC of `ḡᵀWḡ`). |
| `gmmIF G W breadInv g θ₀` | `fun x => −(breadInv (adjoint G (W (g θ₀ x))))` | The **GMM influence function** `−(GᵀWG)⁻¹GᵀW g(θ₀,·)`. |
| `GMMProblem P` | structure | Moment model bundle: `g`, truth `θ₀`, weighting `W` (`hWsa : adjoint W = W`), Jacobian `G`, identification `∫ g(θ₀) dP = 0`, measurability/finite-variance of `g(θ₀)`, Fréchet-derivative spec `jac_spec`, covariance `Cov` with second-moment characterization `hCov`, and two-sided inverse witnesses for `Cov`, `GᵀWG`, `GᵀCov⁻¹G`. |
| `GMMProblem.score` / `influence` | `noncomputable def`s | The problem's combined score / influence function. |
| `GMMProblem.asympVar` | `gmmSandwich G W Cov breadInv` | The **sandwich asymptotic variance** of the problem. |
| `GMMProblem.effVar` | `effInv` | The **efficient variance** `(GᵀCov⁻¹G)⁻¹`. |
| `GMMProblem.cov_isPositive` | `prob.Cov.IsPositive` | The covariance is a positive operator — it is a second moment (`⟪Cov t,t⟫ = ∫ ⟪t,g⟫² ≥ 0`, symmetric). **Proved.** |
| `GMMProblem.efficiency` | `(prob.asympVar − prob.effVar).IsPositive` | **Hansen optimal-weighting theorem, statistical form**: the sandwich variance dominates the efficient variance in the Löwner order; the efficient GMM weighting is `W = Cov⁻¹`. Instantiates `gmm_efficiency`. **Proved, axiom-clean.** |

#### 12v.3. `Stat/GMM/AsymptoticNormality.lean` — GMM CLT via the combined-score Z-estimator

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `gmm_asymptotically_linear` | `IsAsymLinearVec θn θ₀ prob.influence S (range n)` | **GMM asymptotic linearity.** If `θn` solves the combined empirical moment `(1/n) Σ GᵀW g(Z_i;θn) = 0`, is consistent at rate `O_p(1/√n)`, and the combined score `prob.score` satisfies `ZEstimatorRegularity` (with `reg.J₀_inv = breadInv`), then `θn` is asymptotically linear with IF `−(GᵀWG)⁻¹GᵀW g(θ₀,·)`. Hence `√n(θn−θ₀) ⇒ N(0, asympVar)` via `IsAsymLinearVec.tendsto_normal_vec`. Reduces GMM to `zEstimator_clt` on `gmmScore`. **Proved, axiom-clean.** |

#### 12v.4. `Stat/GMM/OverID.lean` — over-identification (J / Hansen–Sargan) test

The whitened J-test: with the moment covariance normalised to the identity (the change of variables the `Σ̂⁻¹`-weighting performs), the residual maker `M = I − G(GᵀG)⁻¹Gᵀ` is an orthogonal projection of rank `m − k`, so the J-statistic limit `‖Mw‖²` is `χ²_{m−k}` via `stdGaussian_map_normSq_orthogonalProjection`. The general-covariance case is the change of variables `z ↦ Σ^{-1/2} z`. Inverses carried as data+witnesses (`heL`, `heR`).

**Deferred (known gap).** This file establishes only the *limit law* `‖Mw‖² ⇒ χ²_{m−k}` for a standard Gaussian `w` on the moment space. Wiring the **empirical** J-statistic `n·ḡₙ(θ̂)ᵀ Σ̂⁻¹ ḡₙ(θ̂)` to this limit — i.e. proving the empirical moments converge to `Mw` under the efficient weighting and applying continuous mapping — is left as future work (needs the moment-CLT contact point + the whitening change-of-variables at the estimator). The χ² target law itself is fully proved.

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `gmmHatMatrix G effInv` | `G ∘L effInv ∘L adjoint G` | The **hat matrix** `H = G(GᵀG)⁻¹Gᵀ`, orthogonal projection onto `range G`. |
| `gmmResidualMaker G effInv` | `id − gmmHatMatrix G effInv` | The **residual maker** `M = I − H`, orthogonal projection onto `(range G)^⊥`. |
| `gmmResidualMaker_isSelfAdjoint` / `_idempotent` | `IsSelfAdjoint M` / `M ∘L M = M` | `M` is an orthogonal projection (uses `effInv` self-adjoint + the inverse witnesses). **Proved.** |
| `gmmResidualMaker_finrank_range` | `finrank (range M) = finrank F − finrank E` | **Hansen–Sargan dof** `m − k`. Proof: `range M = ker H`, `range H = range G`, `G` injective (from `heL`); rank–nullity (`LinearMap.finrank_range_add_finrank_ker`) + `LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj`. **Proved.** |
| `jStatistic_chiSq` | `(stdGaussian F).map (‖M·‖²) = chiSqDist (finrank F − finrank E)` | **Headline: the whitened GMM J-statistic limit law is `χ²_{m−k}`.** Applies the projected-Gaussian χ² lemma to `M`. **Proved, axiom-clean.** |

### 12w. `Stat/Minimax/` — Minimax lower bounds (Le Cam two-point)

The converse direction of the inference stack: machinery to certify that *no*
estimator can do better than a given rate (optimality / sharpness), as opposed
to the achievability results in §12c–§12v. The whole program reduces to one
chain: *risk lower bound ← reduction to testing ← testing error ≥ 1 − TV ← TV ≤ f(KL)*.
The first three links are elementary (this folder); the KL bridge (Pinsker)
lives in `Pinsker.lean`. Project-agnostic; candidates for upstream Mathlib.

Three reduction tiers share the same testing core: **Le Cam** (`LeCam.lean`, §12w.2)
packs two hypotheses; **Fano** (`Fano.lean`, §12w.7) packs many pairwise-separated
ones (rates from `log`-cardinality); **Assouad** (`Assouad.lean`, §12w.8) packs a
`d`-cube of coordinate-wise tests (rates that grow with dimension). Fano and Assouad
are both proven *unconditionally* from the elementary testing bound — no entropy or
product-measure machinery — so the divergence input enters only through `tvDist`.

#### 12w.1. `Stat/Minimax/TotalVariation.lean` — statistical TV distance

Mathlib only carries `SignedMeasure.totalVariation` (Jordan norm); this file develops the testing-oriented statistical TV between two measures.

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `tvDist μ ν` | `⨆ A measurable, \|μ.real A − ν.real A\|` | **Total variation distance**: sup over measurable sets of the probability gap. |
| `abs_measureReal_sub_le_one` | `\|μ.real A − ν.real A\| ≤ 1` | Each defining term is bounded by 1 (probability measures). **Proved.** |
| `bddAbove_tvDist_range` | `BddAbove (range …)` | The defining family is bounded above by 1. **Proved.** |
| `abs_measureReal_sub_le_tvDist` | `\|μ.real A − ν.real A\| ≤ tvDist μ ν` | Each measurable set's gap is `≤ tvDist` (via `le_ciSup`). **Proved.** |
| `measureReal_sub_le_tvDist` | `ν.real A − μ.real A ≤ tvDist μ ν` | Signed-gap form. **Proved.** |
| `tvDist_nonneg`, `tvDist_le_one` | `0 ≤ tvDist μ ν ≤ 1` | Range. **Proved.** |
| `tvDist_symm` | `tvDist μ ν = tvDist ν μ` | Symmetry. **Proved.** |
| `one_sub_tvDist_le_test` | `1 − tvDist μ ν ≤ μ.real A + ν.real Aᶜ` | **The testing bound**: the total error of any test (rejection region `A`) is at least `1 − tvDist`. The single inequality driving the two-point method. **Proved, axiom-clean.** |

#### 12w.2. `Stat/Minimax/LeCam.lean` — Le Cam two-point method

The reduction from estimation to testing. Parameters live in a `[PseudoMetricSpace Θ] [OpensMeasurableSpace Θ]`; estimators are arbitrary measurable `est : Ω → Θ`.

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `measurableSet_error` | `MeasurableSet {ω \| s ≤ dist (est ω) θ}` | The error region of a measurable estimator is measurable (closed-set preimage). **Proved.** |
| `one_sub_tvDist_le_error_sum` | `1 − tvDist P₀ P₁ ≤ P₀.real {s ≤ dist(est,θ₀)} + P₁.real {s ≤ dist(est,θ₁)}` | **Summed form.** Under `2s`-separation `2s ≤ dist θ₀ θ₁`, the two error probabilities of any estimator sum to at least `1 − tvDist`. Proof = testing bound + triangle inequality + monotonicity. **Proved.** |
| `half_one_sub_tvDist_le_max_error` | `(1 − tvDist P₀ P₁)/2 ≤ max (P₀.real {…}) (P₁.real {…})` | **Headline (max form).** Every estimator has worst-case error probability at least `½(1 − tvDist P₀ P₁)`: the canonical minimax lower bound. **Proved, axiom-clean.** |

#### 12w.3. `Stat/Minimax/Pinsker.lean` — KL bridge

Bridges `tvDist` to Mathlib's `InformationTheory.klDiv`, making the two-point bound usable for concrete families (KL is computable for Gaussians etc.). **Pinsker's inequality is now proven unconditionally** — both the scalar core (`klFun_lower_bound`) and the measure-theoretic half (Scheffé `≤` + weighted Cauchy–Schwarz). `PinskerBound` remains as a reusable `Prop` packaging but is no longer a substrate gate.
