| `klFun_lower_bound` | `(3/2)(x−1)²/(x+2) ≤ klFun x` for `x ≥ 0` | Division-form Pinsker scalar engine. **Proved.** |
| `PinskerBound μ ν` | `Prop`: `tvDist μ ν ≤ √((klDiv μ ν).toReal/2)` | Reusable `Prop` packaging of the Pinsker bound for a pair. **Proven** by `pinskerBound_of_ac_of_ne_top`. |
| `pinskerBound_of_ac_of_ne_top` | `μ ≪ ν` + `klDiv μ ν ≠ ⊤` ⇒ `PinskerBound μ ν` | **Pinsker's inequality, proven unconditionally**: Scheffé `≤` (`tvDist_le_half_integral_abs_rnDeriv`) + weighted Cauchy–Schwarz (`√(p+2)` weight) + `klFun_lower_bound`. Both hyps are genuinely needed (`.toReal` collapses `klDiv = ⊤` to `0`). **Proved, axiom-clean.** |
| `pinskerBound_pi_iid` | one-sample `μ ≪ ν` + `Integrable (llr μ ν) μ` ⇒ `PinskerBound (μ^{⊗n}) (ν^{⊗n})` | i.i.d.-product Pinsker: product AC + `klDiv ≠ ⊤` discharged from marginals via `ProductKLLeCam.pi_iid_*`, then the unconditional inequality. **Proved.** |
| `klForm_two_point_lower_bound_of_pinsker` | from `PinskerBound P₀ P₁` + 2s-separation: worst-case error `≥ (1 − √(KL/2))/2` | KL-form minimax lower bound from a supplied `PinskerBound` term; composes with `half_one_sub_tvDist_le_max_error`. **Proved from hypothesis.** |
| `klForm_two_point_lower_bound` | `P₀ ≪ P₁` + `klDiv P₀ P₁ ≠ ⊤` + 2s-separation ⇒ worst-case error `≥ (1 − √(KL/2))/2` | **Unconditional** KL-form minimax lower bound: derives the Pinsker bridge via `pinskerBound_of_ac_of_ne_top` (no `PinskerBound` hypothesis). **Proved.** |

#### 12w.4. `Stat/Minimax/Scheffe.lean` — variational TV identity (≤ direction)

The Scheffé `≤` bound — the analytic workhorse for both the χ² route (`TV ≤ ½√χ²`) and discharging `PinskerBound`. Proved via the symmetric splitting `∫_A f = −∫_{Aᶜ} f` (sidesteps posPart/negPart machinery). The reverse `≥` (full equality) was deliberately skipped — the `≤` suffices downstream.

| `measureReal_sub_eq_setIntegral_rnDeriv_sub_one` | under `μ ≪ ν`: `μ.real A − ν.real A = ∫ x in A, ((μ.rnDeriv ν x).toReal − 1) ∂ν` | Signed-gap as a density integral. **Proved.** |
| `tvDist_le_half_integral_abs_rnDeriv` | `tvDist μ ν ≤ ½∫\|(μ.rnDeriv ν x).toReal − 1\| ∂ν` (prob measures, `μ ≪ ν`) | **Scheffé `≤`.** **Proved, axiom-clean.** |

#### 12w.5. `Stat/Minimax/ChiSquared.lean` — χ² divergence link

`chiSqDiv` and the χ² control of total variation — the divergence that makes two-point indistinguishability computable (and tensorizes over iid samples). Named `chiSqDiv` to avoid colliding with the χ² *distribution* `chiSqDist` (§12n'''d).

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `chiSqDiv μ ν` | `∫ ((μ.rnDeriv ν x).toReal − 1)² ∂ν` | χ²-divergence of μ relative to ν. |
| `chiSqDiv_nonneg` | `0 ≤ chiSqDiv μ ν` | Integrand is a square. **Proved.** |
| `tvDist_le_half_sqrt_chiSqDiv` | `tvDist μ ν ≤ ½·√(chiSqDiv μ ν)` (prob, `μ≪ν`, sq-deviation integrable) | **Cauchy–Schwarz on Scheffé** (Hölder `2,2` with `g≡1`, `∫1²∂ν=1`). **Proved, axiom-clean.** |
| `chiSqDiv_eq` | `chiSqDiv μ ν = (∫ (μ.rnDeriv ν x).toReal² ∂ν) − 1` (`μ≪ν`) | Expanded form via `∫ dμ/dν ∂ν = 1`. **Proved.** |

| `rnDeriv_prod_eq` | `(μ₁.prod μ₂).rnDeriv (ν₁.prod ν₂) =ᵐ fun z ↦ rnDeriv μ₁ ν₁ z.1 · rnDeriv μ₂ ν₂ z.2` | Product-measure RN-derivative factorization (assembled from `withDensity_rnDeriv_eq` + `prod_withDensity₀` + `rnDeriv_withDensity₀`; Mathlib has no packaged version). Reusable. **Proved.** |
| `chiSqDiv_prod` | `1 + chiSqDiv (μ₁.prod μ₂) (ν₁.prod ν₂) = (1+chiSqDiv μ₁ ν₁)(1+chiSqDiv μ₂ ν₂)` | **χ² tensorization** (binary). Via `rnDeriv_prod_eq` + `chiSqDiv_eq` + Fubini (`integral_prod_mul`). **Proved, axiom-clean.** |
| `chiSqDiv_map_measurableEquiv` | `chiSqDiv (μ.map e) (ν.map e) = chiSqDiv μ ν` for `e : Ω ≃ᵐ Ω'` (σ-finite) | **χ² is invariant under a measurable equivalence** (relabelling the sample space). Via `integral_map_equiv` + `MeasurableEmbedding.rnDeriv_map`. Reusable. **Proved, axiom-clean.** |
| `chiSqDiv_self` | `chiSqDiv ρ ρ = 0` (σ-finite) | Self-divergence vanishes (`rnDeriv_self =ᵐ 1`); the `n=0` base case. **Proved, axiom-clean.** |
| `pi_iid_absolutelyContinuous` | `μ ≪ ν ⇒ Measure.pi (fun _:Fin n ↦ μ) ≪ Measure.pi (fun _:Fin n ↦ ν)` | i.i.d. product a.c. (Mathlib has no `pi`-level a.c. lemma); induction via `piFinSuccAbove` + `AbsolutelyContinuous.prod`/`.map`. **Proved, axiom-clean.** |
| `one_add_chiSqDiv_pi_iid` | `1 + chiSqDiv (Measure.pi (fun _:Fin n ↦ μ)) (Measure.pi (fun _:Fin n ↦ ν)) = (1 + chiSqDiv μ ν)ⁿ` (finite `Ω`, prob, `μ≪ν`) | **n-fold i.i.d. χ² tensorization** — the iid scaling consumed by `n`-sample two-point/Le Cam bounds. Induction on `Fin n` via `measurePreserving_piFinSuccAbove` + `chiSqDiv_map_measurableEquiv` + binary `chiSqDiv_prod`; integrability discharged for free by `Integrable.of_finite` (restricted to `[Fintype Ω] [MeasurableSingletonClass Ω]`). **Proved, axiom-clean.** |
| `pi_iid_integrable_sq_dev` | `Integrable ((d(μ^⊗n)/d(ν^⊗n) − 1)²) (ν^⊗n)` from the one-sample integrability `hint` (general `[MeasurableSpace S]`, probs, `μ≪ν`) | **Integrability propagation** to the i.i.d. product: the squared density deviation stays integrable under `n`-fold products (L²(ν)-tensorization of the density). Supplies the side-condition that `one_add_chiSqDiv_pi_iid` got for free on a finite space. **Proved, axiom-clean.** |
| `one_add_chiSqDiv_pi_iid_general` | `1 + chiSqDiv (Measure.pi (fun _:Fin n ↦ μ)) (Measure.pi (fun _:Fin n ↦ ν)) = (1 + chiSqDiv μ ν)ⁿ` (general `[MeasurableSpace S]`, probs, `μ≪ν`, sq-deviation integrable) | **n-fold i.i.d. χ² tensorization on a GENERAL (possibly continuous) measurable space** — the continuum analogue of `one_add_chiSqDiv_pi_iid` (whose `[Fintype]` only discharged integrability for free). Same `chiSqDiv_prod` induction, with integrability supplied by `hint` + `pi_iid_integrable_sq_dev`. Needed by minimax two-point lower bounds whose sample space is a continuum (e.g. a covariate space). **Proved, axiom-clean.** |
| `chiSqDiv_prod_ancillary` | `chiSqDiv (μ.prod ρ) (ν.prod ρ) = chiSqDiv μ ν` (probs, `μ≪ν`, `hint` for `μ,ν`) | **Ancillary factor invariance**: a common product factor `ρ` cancels (`1 + χ²(ρ‖ρ) = 1`). The formal "an ancillary observation carries no information"; the bridge from finite-cell to continuous-`X` (§13sa.6). **Proved, axiom-clean.** |

#### 12w.5b. `Stat/Minimax/ChiSquaredFinite.lean` — finite / product specializations of χ²

The enabling step for the Ingster bound. **Proved, axiom-clean.** |

#### 12w.6. `Stat/Minimax/MinimaxRisk.lean` — real-functional / n-sample packaging

Causal-agnostic specialization of Le Cam to a real-valued functional estimated from `n` i.i.d. samples — the shape consumed by concrete minimax lower bounds (the causal structure-agnostic ATE theorem lives in `Estimation/`, not here).

The file also carries the **Bayes-risk step** (`integral_le_sSup_range_of_isProbabilityMeasure`): averaging a risk function against any prior probability measure is `≤` its worst case, which is how a minimax lower bound is certified by exhibiting one prior and bounding *its* average risk from below. Use it when the hard instance is a continuum prior rather than a finite hypothesis set (Le Cam/Fano); see its docstring for the statement.

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `real_two_point_lower_bound` | `2s ≤ \|θ₀−θ₁\|` ⇒ `(1−tvDist P₀ P₁)/2 ≤ max (P₀.real{s≤\|est−θ₀\|}) (P₁.real{s≤\|est−θ₁\|})` | Le Cam at `Θ=ℝ` (`dist a b = \|a−b\|`). **Proved.** |
| `two_point_lower_bound_of_tvDist_le` | same with explicit `tvDist P₀ P₁ ≤ c` ⇒ bound `(1−c)/2` | Convenience for plugging a TV upper bound. **Proved.** |
| `iid_two_point_lower_bound` | for laws `P₀,P₁` on `S`, functional `τ`, `n` samples (`Measure.pi (fun _:Fin n ↦ Pⱼ)`), `2s ≤ \|τ P₀ − τ P₁\|` ⇒ worst-case miss prob `≥ ½(1 − tvDist)` between the `n`-fold laws | **The n-sample minimax form.** **Proved.** |
| `two_point_lower_bound_of_chiSqDiv_le` | `chiSqDiv P₀ P₁ ≤ c` (+ `≪`, integrability) ⇒ worst-case miss prob `≥ (1 − ½√c)/2` | **χ²-form bound** (via `tvDist ≤ ½√χ²`); the directly-certifiable form since χ² is computable and tensorizes. **Proved, axiom-clean.** |

#### 12w.6a.i. `Stat/FiniteRaoBlackwell/` — guarded finite Rao–Blackwell reductions

Uniform finite allocation experiments often create statistic fibers that have zero probability
at some latent states. This subtree supplies a guarded finite conditional law, exact
disintegration, finite-prior posteriors, a factorization criterion for a shared conditional law,
and squared-loss Rao–Blackwell risk reductions. `KernelBridge` exposes the same constructions as
Markov kernels and connects their real-valued finite sums to `FiniteKernelBayes`.

`DesignPushforward` works directly with any finite randomization design, conditioning source values along a deterministic coarsening without passing through the uniform-experiment wrapper. Its caller-supplied default affects only null fibers, while disintegration, range preservation, and squared-loss contraction remain exact.

#### 12w.6a.ii. `Stat/Minimax/FinitePosteriorBayesRisk.lean` — finite posterior squared-loss Bayes risk

A finite prior and finite observation kernel determine a guarded posterior mean, an exact
squared-loss decomposition, and the resulting real-valued Bayes-risk infimum. Continuous priors
enter through the existing induced finite design, which also transfers estimator-wise integral
lower bounds to the corresponding finite and continuous-mixture Bayes risks.

#### 12w.6b. `Stat/Minimax/MarkovKernelTransport.lean` — randomized experiment transport

Blackwell garbling cannot improve squared-error estimation risk. A bounded target-experiment
estimator is averaged over the Markov kernel to produce its Rao--Blackwell pullback on the
source experiment; Jensen's inequality compares their risks, while an affine target change
rescales the lower bound by the squared slope. The finite-product construction applies the
kernel independently across coordinates and includes the empty sample.

<!-- GEN:Causalean.Stat.Minimax.MarkovKernelTransport -->
| Decl | Signature | Description |

#### 12w.7. `Stat/Minimax/Fano.lean` — multiple-hypothesis (M-ary) lower bound

Generalizes Le Cam from *two* hypotheses to *many* pairwise-`2s`-separated ones — the testing/TV form of Fano's lemma (Tsybakov §2.6, Le Cam–Birgé). An estimator induces disjoint acceptance regions `A i = {ω | dist(est ω, θ i) < s}`; comparing each `Pᵢ(A i)` to a *reference* hypothesis `i₀` costs one `tvDist`, bounding the total correct-recovery mass. Proven **unconditionally** from `measureReal_sub_le_tvDist` — no entropy/mutual-information machinery; divergence enters only through `tvDist` (bound it by KL/χ² via §12w.3/§12w.5). Uses a reference index `i₀` rather than the centroid mixture, so it does **not** depend on `Mixture.lean` (the symmetric mixture-centroid form is a strict sharpening that can be layered on).

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `acceptanceRegion est θ s` | `{ω \| dist (est ω) θ < s}` | Points the estimator places strictly within `s` of `θ`. |
| `measurableSet_acceptanceRegion` | `MeasurableSet (acceptanceRegion est θ s)` | Complement of the (closed) error region. **Proved.** |
| `acceptanceRegion_disjoint` / `_pairwiseDisjoint` | `2s ≤ dist θ₀ θ₁ ⇒ Disjoint (A θ₀) (A θ₁)`; pairwise version over a family | A point within `s` of both targets would force them within `2s`. **Proved.** |
| `sum_refReal_acceptance_le` | `∑ᵢ (P i₀).real (A i) ≤ 1` | Reference mass over disjoint regions is `≤ 1` (finite additivity + `≤ univ`). **Proved.** |
| `sum_correct_le` | `∑ᵢ (P i).real (A i) ≤ 1 + ∑ᵢ tvDist (P i₀) (P i)` | **Heart of Fano**: each `Pᵢ(A i)` vs reference costs one `tvDist`. **Proved.** |
| `fano_average_error` | `1 − (1 + ∑ᵢ tvDist (P i₀) (P i))/N ≤ (∑ᵢ (P i).real {s ≤ dist(est,θ i)})/N` (`N = card ι`) | **Average-error minimax lower bound** over the family. **Proved, axiom-clean.** |
| `fano_exists_error` | under `tvDist (P i₀) (P i) ≤ β`: `∃ i, 1 − 1/N − β ≤ (P i).real {s ≤ dist(est,θ i)}` | **Usable form**: large `N` + small `β` ⇒ some hypothesis forces error. **Proved, axiom-clean.** |

#### 12w.8. `Stat/Minimax/Assouad.lean` — hypercube lower bound (Assouad's lemma)

Packs a `d`-cube `{P τ : τ ∈ (Fin d → Bool)}` in which each coordinate is an independent two-point test — converting a `d`-fold product into a `d`-fold *sum* of testing bounds (rates that grow with dimension). A cube estimator `est : Ω → (Fin d → Bool)` decodes each bit; its expected **Hamming risk** counts mis-decoded coordinates. Proof = coordinate-flip averaging: pairing each vertex `τ` with its `j`-flip via an involution (`flipPerm`), the two coordinate-`j` masses are `(P τ).real S + (P (flip j τ)).real Sᶜ`, lower-bounded by `1 − tvDist` via `one_sub_tvDist_le_test`. **Unconditional**, no product-measure machinery.

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `flipBit j τ` / `flipPerm j` | `Function.update τ j (!τ j)`; as an `Equiv.Perm` | Flip the `j`-th cube coordinate (an involution; the perm reindexes cube-sums). **Proved involutive.** |
| `hammingRisk P est τ` | `∑ⱼ (P τ).real {ω \| est ω j ≠ τ j}` | Expected number of coordinates the estimator decodes incorrectly at vertex `τ`. |
| `measurableSet_decode_ne` | `MeasurableSet {ω \| est ω j ≠ b}` from `MeasurableSet {ω \| est ω j = b}` | Decoding-error sets are complements of level sets. **Proved.** |
| `decode_ne_flip_compl` | `{ω \| est ω j ≠ (flip j τ) j} = {ω \| est ω j ≠ τ j}ᶜ` | The `j`-th error set at the flipped vertex is the complement at `τ` (`a ≠ !b ↔ a = b`). **Proved.** |
| `hammingRisk_pair_ge` | `1 − tvDist (P τ) (P (flip j τ)) ≤ (P τ).real Sⱼτ + (P (flip j τ)).real Sⱼ(flip)` | **Per-vertex pair bound** = two-point testing bound on the `j`-th decoded bit. **Proved.** |
| `sum_decode_ge` | `∑_τ (1 − tvDist (P τ)(P (flip j τ))) ≤ 2·∑_τ (P τ).real {est j ≠ τ j}` | Per-coordinate cube-sum bound via the flip involution (`Equiv.sum_comp`). **Proved.** |
| `assouad_average` | under `tvDist (P τ)(P (flip j τ)) ≤ β`: `(d/2)(1 − β) ≤ (∑_τ hammingRisk P est τ)/card` | **Assouad (average form).** Large `d` + small `β` ⇒ many mis-decoded coordinates. **Proved, axiom-clean.** |
| `assouad_exists` | same hypotheses: `∃ τ, (d/2)(1 − β) ≤ hammingRisk P est τ` | **Existence form**: some vertex forces large Hamming risk. **Proved, axiom-clean.** |

#### 12w.9. `Stat/Minimax/Mixture.lean` — finite mixtures of measures

Generic finite mixture `∑ᵢ wᵢ • Pᵢ` and the **domination lemma** behind the fuzzy-hypothesis / second-moment method: a mixture over in-class hypotheses with a common functional value never assigns more mass than the worst single hypothesis, so an averaged risk is `≤` the supremum. Consumed by the structure-agnostic ATE lower bound (§13sa) for the `dominated` (realizability) obligation of `TwoPointWitness`.

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `mixture w P` | `∑ i, w i • P i` (`w : Fin K → ℝ≥0∞`) | Finite mixture of measures with `ℝ≥0∞` weights. |
| `mixture_apply` | `mixture w P A = ∑ i, w i · P i A` | Mass on a set is the weighted sum of the parts' masses. **Proved.** |
| `mixture_isProbabilityMeasure` | `∑ i, w i = 1 ⇒ IsProbabilityMeasure (mixture w P)` (parts prob) | A convex combination of probability measures is a probability measure. **Proved.** |
| `mixtureReal_le` | `∑ i, w i = 1, (∀ i, (P i).real A ≤ B) ⇒ (mixture w P).real A ≤ B` (parts prob) | **Domination**: a weighted average of per-part masses is `≤` a common bound. The averaging step in the fuzzy-hypothesis reduction. **Proved, axiom-clean.** |
| `exists_real_ge_mixture` | `∑ i, w i = 1 ⇒ ∃ i, (mixture w P).real A ≤ (P i).real A` (parts prob, `[Nonempty ι]`) | **Witness extraction**: a finite average is `≤` its maximal component, so some part carries at least the mixture's mass. Pulls a single hard DGP out of a mixture hypothesis. **Proved, axiom-clean.** |

#### 12w.10. `Stat/Minimax/HellingerAffinity.lean` — affinity of two common-measure densities

The *third* route from a hypothesis pair to a TV bound, alongside Pinsker (§12w.3) and
χ² (§12w.5). It applies when the two candidate laws are given as densities `f, g`
against **one** common dominating measure — the situation in every explicit two-tilt
construction — so no Radon–Nikodym derivative and no mutual absolute-continuity premise
is needed. The chain is: compute the coordinate *affinity* `∫ √(f·g)`, tensorize it over
the product (`densityAffinity_pi`), convert the product defect into a *sum* of coordinate
defects (`one_sub_prod_le_sum`), and finally read it as a TV bound
(`tvDist_le_sqrt_two_mul_one_sub_affinity`). This is what makes an `n`-fold product prior
tractable: only one coordinate integral has to be computed by hand.

Complementary to `BretagnolleHuber.lean`, which bounds the *same* affinity number **from
below** by `½·exp(−KL)` but works through `rnDeriv`; use this file when you own the
densities and that file when you own the KL divergence.

<!-- GEN:Causalean.Stat.Minimax.HellingerAffinity -->
| Decl | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Stat.densityAffinity` | `MeasureTheory.Measure α → (α → ℝ) → (α → ℝ) → ℝ` | The Hellinger (Bhattacharyya) affinity of two nonnegative densities taken against one common dominating measure: the integral of the square root of their pointwise product. It equals one when the two densities agree almost everywhere and falls toward zero as the two laws separate, so it measures how hard the two laws are to tell apart. |
| `Stat.hellingerSqDensity` | `MeasureTheory.Measure α → (α → ℝ) → (α → ℝ) → ℝ` | The squared Hellinger distance between two nonnegative densities against one common dominating measure, in the unhalved convention: the integral of the squared difference of their pointwise square roots. |
| `Stat.hellingerSqDensity_eq_two_mul_one_sub_affinity` | `MeasureTheory.Integrable f μ → MeasureTheory.Integrable g μ → 0 ≤ f → 0 ≤ g → ∫ (x : α), f x ∂μ = 1 → ∫ (x : α), g x ∂μ = 1 → Causalean.Stat.hellingerSqDensity μ f g = 2 * (1 - Causalean.Stat.densityAffinity μ f g)` | For two integrable nonnegative densities that each integrate to one, the unhalved squared Hellinger distance is exactly twice the affinity defect, i.e. twice one minus the affinity. This is the algebraic identity that lets an affinity computation be read as a Hellinger distance and back. |
| `Stat.tvDist_le_sqrt_two_mul_one_sub_affinity` | `MeasureTheory.Integrable f μ → MeasureTheory.Integrable g μ → 0 ≤ f → 0 ≤ g → ∫ (x : α), f x ∂μ = 1 → ∫ (x : α), g x ∂μ = 1 → Causalean.Stat.tvDist (μ.withDensity fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (f x)) (μ.withDensity fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (g x)) ≤ √(2 * (1 - Causalean.Stat.densityAffinity μ f g))` | Cauchy–Schwarz on the Hellinger affinity. For a dominating measure `μ` and functions `f`, `g` such that `f` is `μ`-integrable, `g` is `μ`-integrable, `f` is pointwise nonnegative, `g` is pointwise nonnegative, `f` integrates to `1` against `μ`, and `g` integrates to `1` against `μ` — so that `f dμ` and `g dμ` are probability densities — the total variation distance between the two weighted laws is at most the square root of twice the affinity defect, `√(2(1 − densityAffinity μ f g))`. This is the Cauchy–Schwarz half of the standard total-variation–Hellinger comparison, and it is what converts an affinity computation into a Le Cam two-point bound. |

generic liminf/limsup frontier-risk packaging over arbitrary model classes.

This proof chain gives a finite decision-problem minimax theorem for dependent finite
observation spaces. It uses the existing `FiniteDesign` expectation and `minimaxValue`
interfaces, derives the conditional Jensen mixing step for squared loss, and returns an
ordinary randomized procedure together with an attaining least-favorable finite prior.

## 12ep. `Stat/EmpiricalProcess/` — Uniform LLN (Glivenko–Cantelli) & extremum-estimator consistency

Empirical-process layer written for the econometrics workflow (van der Vaart
1998, Ch. 19; Newey & McFadden 1994, §2). A *function class* is an indexed family
`f : ι → X → ℝ`; the empirical process measures how far the sample means `Pₙ f_i`
sit from the population means `P f_i = ∫ f_i dP`, **uniformly over the class**.
This is the uniform law of large numbers that the M-estimation CLT stack
(`Stat/MEstimation/`) previously had to assume. All declarations **proved,
sorry-free**.

### 12ep.a `Stat/EmpiricalProcess/Basic.lean` — vocabulary

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `IIDSample.empiricalProcess f i n` | `def`, `Ω → ℝ` | The centred-scaled process `√n · (Pₙ f_i − P f_i)` at class member `i` — the object whose weak limit (a Gaussian process) is the subject of Donsker theory. |
| `IIDSample.supDeviation f n` | `def`, `Ω → ℝ` | Finite-class sup deviation `⨆ i, \|Pₙ f_i − P f_i\|` (meaningful as a statistic when `ι` is finite). |
| `GlivenkoCantelli S f` | `def`, `Prop` | **(Weak) uniform LLN**: for every `ε > 0`, `μ {ω | ∃ i, ε ≤ \|Pₙ f_i − P f_i\|} → 0`. Stated existentially (not via `⨆`) so it is meaningful for infinite/uncountable classes without lattice-junk artefacts. |
| `L1Bracketing f P ε` | `structure` | A finite `L¹(P)` `ε`-bracketing: `m` brackets `[lo j, hi j]` (`j : Fin m`) with integrable endpoints, `P`-mean width `∫ (hi j − lo j) dP ≤ ε`, and an `assign : ι → Fin m` sandwiching each member `lo (assign i) ≤ f i ≤ hi (assign i)`. |
| `HasL1Bracketing f P` | `def`, `Prop` | Finite `L¹(P)` bracketing numbers: an `ε`-bracketing exists for every `ε > 0`. The classical sufficient condition for Glivenko–Cantelli. |

### 12ep.b `Stat/EmpiricalProcess/GlivenkoCantelli.lean` — uniform LLN theorems

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `glivenkoCantelli_of_fintype` | `[Finite ι]`, each `f i` measurable & `P`-integrable ⇒ `GlivenkoCantelli S f` | A **finite** class of integrable functions is Glivenko–Cantelli. Union bound over coordinates, each vanishing by the pointwise WLLN (`IIDSample.sampleMean_tendsto_inProb`). **Proved.** |
| `glivenkoCantelli_of_hasL1Bracketing` | each `f i` measurable, `HasL1Bracketing f P` ⇒ `GlivenkoCantelli S f` | A class with **finite `L¹(P)` bracketing numbers** is Glivenko–Cantelli (van der Vaart 1998, Thm 19.4; Newey–McFadden Lemma 2.4). Each member is sandwiched in a bracket of mean-width `≤ ε/2`, so its deviation is controlled by the `2m` bracket-endpoint deviations plus `ε/2`; the endpoints vanish by the finite case. **Proved.** |

Private helpers: `tendsto_measure_zero_of_le` (measure squeeze), `integrable_pullback` (transfer `P`-integrability to `μ`), `dev_tendsto_zero` (single-statistic WLLN rephrased from the `edist`/`ℝ≥0∞` `TendstoInMeasure` to the real `\|·\|` event), `sampleMean_mono`.

### 12ep.c `Stat/EmpiricalProcess/MEstimatorConsistency.lean` — extremum-estimator consistency

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `mEstimator_consistent_of_glivenkoCantelli` | `GlivenkoCantelli S m` + sample-argmax domination over `θ₀` + well-separated population max ⇒ `∀ ε>0, μ {ω | ε ≤ dist (θ̂ₙ ω) θ₀} → 0` | **Consistency of extremum / M-estimators** (Newey–McFadden 1994, Thm 2.1; van der Vaart 1998, Thm 5.7). `θ̂ₙ` maximizing the sample criterion `θ ↦ Pₙ m(θ,·)` is consistent for the population maximizer `θ₀`. **Consumes** the `GlivenkoCantelli` engine: the uniform-convergence hypothesis is exactly that predicate. Proof is the classical `M(θ₀) − M(θ̂ₙ) ≤ 2·sup_θ\|Mₙ−M\|` sandwich versus the separation gap `η`. **Proved, sorry-free.** |
| `mEstimator_consistent_of_bracketing` | finite `L¹(P)` bracketing of `m` + argmax domination + well-separated max ⇒ consistency | **Bracketing headline corollary**: composes `glivenkoCantelli_of_hasL1Bracketing` with the consistency theorem, so a verifiable bracketing condition (instead of an assumed uniform LLN) yields consistency directly. **Proved, sorry-free.** |

### 12ep.d `Stat/EmpiricalProcess/Equicontinuity/` — stochastic equicontinuity & the `StochEquicontAt` reduction

The empirical-process / Donsker layer at the **parametric** scale, discharging the
`StochEquicontAt` hypothesis consumed by `zEstimator_clt` and
`gmm_asymptotically_linear`. **Key structural finding:** `StochEquicontAt`
(fixed `δ`, inner limit `0`, gap evaluated at the *random* estimator `θn`) is only
true when `θn →_p θ₀` — it secretly bundles consistency. The honest decomposition
is **class-level asymptotic equicontinuity (`AsymptoticEquicont`, independent of
`θn`) + consistency ⟹ `StochEquicontAt`**. The uniform-in-`n` control of the
empirical process comes from the variance identity `Var(√n(Pₙ−P)f) = Var_P f` via
Chebyshev — no CLT and no chaining for the base cases. All declarations below are
**proved, sorry-free, axiom-clean**. `E` is a finite-dimensional real inner-product
space (the `Z`-estimator parameter/value space).

`Process.lean` — vocabulary:

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `IIDSample.empProcVec S f n` | `def`, `Ω → E` | **Vector-valued centered empirical process** `Gₙ(f)(ω) = (√n)⁻¹ • Σ_{i<n} f(Zᵢ ω) − √n • ∫ f dP`; the `E`-valued analogue of `empiricalProcess`. |
| `IIDSample.empProcVec_eq_stochEquicont_gap` | `rfl` bridge | `empProcVec` of the score difference `ψ(θ,·)−ψ(θ₀,·)` equals the centered gap `R_n` of `StochEquicontAt`. |

`SecondMoment.lean` — the uniform-in-`n` Chebyshev workhorse:

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `IIDSample.measurable_empProcVec` | `Measurable (fun ω => empProcVec f n ω)` | Measurability of the process in `ω`. |
| `empProcVec_sq_lintegral_le` | `f ∈ L²(P)` ⇒ `∫⁻ ‖Gₙ(f)‖² dμ ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (∫ ‖f‖² dP)` | **Second-moment / variance identity at the empirical scale**, uniformly in `n`. Proved coordinate-wise: Parseval (`OrthonormalBasis.sum_sq_inner_right`) reduces `‖Gₙ(f)‖²` to a sum of scalar centered i.i.d. sums, each bounded by `Causalean.Mathlib.iid_centered_sum_sq_lintegral_le`. No CLT, no chaining. |
| `empProcVec_chebyshev` | `0<ε` ⇒ `μ {‖Gₙ(f)‖ > ε} ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (∫ ‖f‖² dP) / ENNReal.ofReal (ε²)` | **Chebyshev bound** (second moment + Markov, `meas_ge_le_lintegral_div`). The uniform-in-`n` modulus that drives equicontinuity: as `‖f‖_{L²(P)}` shrinks, the tail shrinks at a rate independent of sample size. |

`Modulus.lean` — the class-level predicate and the reduction:

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `AsymptoticEquicont ψ θ₀ P μ S` | `def`, `Prop` | **Class-level asymptotic equicontinuity** (the Donsker content, independent of any estimator): `∀ ε>0, ∀ η>0, ∃ δ>0, ∀ᶠ n, μ {ω | ∃ θ, ‖θ−θ₀‖<δ ∧ ε < ‖Gₙ(ψ(θ,·)−ψ(θ₀,·))(ω)‖} ≤ η`. Existential over `θ` (not a non-measurable `sup`) so outer-measure bookkeeping is automatic. |
| `empProcVec_atEstimator_tendsto_zero` | `AsymptoticEquicont` + `θn →_p θ₀` ⇒ `Gₙ(ψ(θn,·)−ψ(θ₀,·)) →_p 0` (unconditional) | The empirical process at the estimator vanishes — textbook union bound (split on `{‖θn−θ₀‖≥δ}` via consistency; on the complement the gap is witnessed by `θ=θn`). |
| `stochEquicontAt_of_asymptoticEquicont` | `AsymptoticEquicont` + `θn →_p θ₀` ⇒ `StochEquicontAt ψ θ₀ P μ S θn` | **The reduction.** Discharges the estimator-indexed `StochEquicontAt` hypothesis of `zEstimator_clt`/`gmm_asymptotically_linear` from the clean class-level Donsker property plus consistency. |
| `empProcVec_isLittleOp_of_L2` | deterministic `θn` with `∫ ‖ψ(θn,·)−ψ(θ₀,·)‖² dP → 0` ⇒ gap is `o_p(1)` | **Deterministic-curve equicontinuity** (non-vacuousness witness): direct from `empProcVec_chebyshev`, no chaining, no consistency. The base case certifying the `AsymptoticEquicont` machinery is satisfiable. |

`MaximalInequality.lean` — sub-exponential maximal inequality (chaining primitive):

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `HasSubexponentialMGF.measure_abs_ge_le` | `μ.real {ε ≤ \|X\|} ≤ 2 exp(−ε²/(2(v+bε)))` | Two-sided sub-exponential tail, from the one-sided `measure_ge_le` applied to `X` and `−X`. |
| `measure_exists_abs_ge_le` | finite family ⇒ `μ.real {∃ i∈t, ε ≤ \|Yᵢ\|} ≤ t.card · 2 exp(−ε²/(2(v+bε)))` | **Maximal inequality** for the max of finitely many mean-zero sub-exponential variables (union bound). The reusable primitive a bracketing/chaining maximal inequality is built from. |
| `measure_sup'_ge_le` | same bound for `μ.real {ε ≤ t.sup' (fun i => \|Yᵢ\|)}` | `sup'` form of the maximal inequality. |

**Remaining frontier.** Discharging `AsymptoticEquicont` for an *infinite* class
over a continuum of `θ` (genuine bracketing-entropy / Ossiander chaining, van der
Vaart 1998 Lemma 19.34) is the real Mathlib gap — the `√n` bracketing bias is
intrinsic and cannot be tamed without chaining (finite classes are trivially
equicontinuous). `MaximalInequality.lean` provides the single-scale primitive for
that future chaining argument.

### 12ep.e `Stat/EmpiricalProcess/CrossFitRate.lean` — conditional / cross-fit `O_p` rate

Paper-agnostic workhorse behind every cross-fit / DML "remainder-is-negligible"
step: the centered empirical mean of a (possibly cross-fit / conditional) score is
`O_p(n^{-1/2} · (second-moment)^{1/2})`, stated over an arbitrary score and
σ-field. Reuses the existing `O_p` predicate `Causalean.Stat.IsBigOp` (no second
predicate) and the conditional second-moment engine
`Causalean.Mathlib.iid_centered_sum_sq_lintegral_le`. The Markov "L²-envelope ⇒ `O_p`"
step (previously inlined privately in `Estimation/OrthogonalMoments/DMLCrossFit.lean`)
is extracted here as the reusable primitive. All declarations **proved, sorry-free,
axiom-clean**.

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `IsBigOp.mono_rate` | `0 ≤ rₙ ≤ sₙ`, `O_p(rₙ)` ⇒ `O_p(sₙ)` | **Weaken to a larger rate** — a larger envelope is a weaker statement. |
| `IsBigOp.scale_rate` | `c>0`, `O_p(c·rₙ)` ⇒ `O_p(rₙ)` | **Absorb a positive constant rate factor** into the witness `M`. |
| `IsBigOp.const_rate_collapse` | `0 ≤ N`, `O_p(fun _ => N)` ⇒ `O_p(fun _ => 1)` | **Collapse a fixed constant rate to the unit rate** (normalizes fold-sum `O_p(1)` conclusions). |
| `IsBigOp.const_mul` | `O_p(rₙ)` ⇒ `c·Xₙ = O_p(rₙ)` | **Constant multiple** of the random sequence keeps the rate. |
| `IsBigOp.add'` | `O_p(rₙ) + O_p(sₙ) = O_p(rₙ+sₙ)` (nonneg rates) | **Additivity at the sum rate** (`IsBigOp.add` is the `rₙ=sₙ` special case). |
| `IsBigOp.of_abs_le` | pointwise `\|Xₙ\| ≤ \|Yₙ\|`, `Yₙ = O_p(rₙ)` ⇒ `Xₙ = O_p(rₙ)` | **Domination rule** for stochastic big-O. |
| `IsBigOp.zero` | `0 = O_p(rₙ)` | Constant-zero sequence is stochastically bounded at any rate. |
| `IsBigOp.finset_sum` | finite sum of terms each `O_p(rₙ)` ⇒ sum is `O_p(rₙ)` | Finite-sum bookkeeping for stochastic big-O; constants absorb the finite index set. |
| `IsBigOp.mul` | `0≤rₙ`, `0≤sₙ`, `Xₙ=O_p(rₙ)`, `Yₙ=O_p(sₙ)` ⇒ `XₙYₙ=O_p(rₙsₙ)` | **Product rule** for stochastic big-O at two nonnegative rates. |
| `IsBigOp.of_sq_lintegral_le` | `Xₙ` a.e.-meas., `0 ≤ Vₙ`, `∫⁻ (Xₙ)² dμ ≤ Vₙ` ⇒ `Xₙ = O_p(√Vₙ)` | **The Markov primitive.** A deterministic second-moment envelope yields the matching `O_p` rate (Chebyshev: `μ{M√Vₙ<\|Xₙ\|} ≤ 1/M²`). The reusable core every cross-fit rate proof consumes. |
| `isBigOp_centered_crossFit_sum` | eval set `s n` ⊥ sub-σ-field `m_A n`, conditionally iid; score `g n` `(m_A n ⊗ σ_X)`-measurable & `L²(P)`; deterministic `Vₙ ≥ ∫_Ω ‖g n ω‖²_{L²(P)} dμ` ⇒ centered fold sum `= O_p(√Vₙ)` | **Lemma B — the conditional / cross-fit lift** (the deliverable). `∫ g n ω dP = 𝔼[g\|m_A n](ω)` is the conditional mean (eval fold ⊥ `m_A n`), so the sum is `√\|s n\|·(ℙₙg − 𝔼[g\|m_A n])`. Second moment via the engine, rate via `of_sq_lintegral_le`. Estimand-agnostic; weak-overlap clipped-AIPW is the first consumer. |
| `IIDSample.sampleMean_sub_sq_lintegral_le` | iid sample, `f ∈ L²(P)`, `0<n` ⇒ `∫⁻ (ℙₙf − ∫f dP)² dμ ≤ E_P[f²]/n` | **Lemma A second-moment bound.** `(1/√n)Σ(f(Zᵢ)−m) = √n(ℙₙf−m)`, so the engine bound divides by `n`. |
| `IIDSample.sampleMean_sub_meas_ge_le` | `0<n`, `t>0` ⇒ `μ{t ≤ \|ℙₙf − ∫f dP\|} ≤ E_P[f²]/(n·t²)` | **Chebyshev tail** for the centered sample mean (second-moment bound + Markov). |
| `IIDSample.sampleMean_sub_isBigOp` | iid sample, `f ∈ L²(P)` ⇒ `(ℙₙf − ∫f dP) = O_p(√(E_P[f²]/n))` | **Lemma A — the unconditional `O_p` rate.** Feeding the centered statistic `f−∫f` (whose `E_P[(·)²]=Var_P f`) gives the sharp `O_p(√(Var_P f/n))` form. The `(ℙₙ−P)φ^bd` consumer. |

## 12x. `Stat/UStatistic/` — U-statistics: Hoeffding decomposition, exact variance, and the CLT

The reusable statistical primitive behind variance estimators, rank/sign statistics,
and the higher-order influence-function estimators (§HOIF). The development has two
layers with a one-way bridge:

- **Order-`m` (the general theory).** `OrderM/` builds the fixed-order U-statistic on
  ordered injective `m`-tuples, its Hájek expansion, the exact order-`m` second moment,
  and — the **headline** — the fixed-order central limit theorem
  `uStatisticOrder_clt_of_regular` (`OrderM/CLT.lean`): a regular order-`m` U-statistic
  is `√n`-asymptotically normal with the Hájek variance `∫ ψ² dP`. Its one genuinely
  probabilistic input, negligibility of the higher-order remainder, is discharged from
  a first-order-degeneracy `L² ≤ C/n` keystone (`OrderM/FirstDegenKernel.lean` →
  `OrderM/RemainderSecondMoment.lean` → `OrderM/RemainderNegligible.lean`).
- **Order-2 (a thin `m = 2` face).** `Basic.lean`/`Variance.lean` keep the natural
  pairwise-kernel API (`h : X → X → ℝ`, off-diagonal `uStatistic`, `DegenKernel`, `ζ`)
  that the HOIF estimators consume. The order-2 *variance* now routes through the
  order-`m` `ExactVariance` internally (via `pairKernel`); the order-2 CLT is recovered
  as the `m = 2` specialization `uStatistic_clt_of_symmetric_via_orderM`
  (`OrderM/OrderTwo.lean`).

### 12x.1. `Stat/UStatistic/Basic.lean` — order-2 Hoeffding decomposition

<!-- GEN:Causalean.Stat.UStatistic.Basic -->
| Decl | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Stat.uStatistic` | `(X → X → ℝ) → ℕ → Ω → ℝ` | The order-2 U-statistic with kernel `h` over the first `n` sample points: `(n(n−1))⁻¹ Σ_{(i,j) ∈ offDiag (range n)} h(Zᵢ, Zⱼ)`. The off-diagonal sum ranges over ordered pairs `i ≠ j`; for a symmetric kernel this is the usual `(n choose 2)⁻¹ Σ_{i<j}`. |
| `Stat.uMean` | `(X → X → ℝ) → MeasureTheory.Measure X → ℝ` | Population mean of the kernel: `θ = ∬ h dP dP`. |
| `Stat.uProj` | `(X → X → ℝ) → MeasureTheory.Measure X → X → ℝ` | First Hoeffding projection (centered): `h₁(x) = ∫ h(x, ·) dP − θ`. |
| `Stat.uDegen` | `(X → X → ℝ) → MeasureTheory.Measure X → X → X → ℝ` | Degenerate second-order kernel: `g(x, y) = h(x, y) − θ − h₁(x) − h₁(y)`. |
| `Stat.hoeffding_decomp` | `h x y = Causalean.Stat.uMean h P + Causalean.Stat.uProj h P x + Causalean.Stat.uProj h P y + Causalean.Stat.uDegen h P x y` | Hoeffding decomposition (pointwise identity). For a kernel `h`, population law `P`, and points `x` and `y`, the kernel value decomposes as `h(x, y) = θ + h₁(x) + h₁(y) + g(x, y)`, the population mean plus the two first-order Hoeffding projections plus the degenerate second-order residual. |
| `Stat.uProj_integral_eq_zero` | `MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => ∫ (y : X), h x y ∂P) P → ∫ (x : X), Causalean.Stat.uProj h P x ∂P = 0` | The first projection integrates to zero: `∫ h₁ dP = 0`. |
| `Stat.uProj_integrable` | `MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => ∫ (y : X), h x y ∂P) P → MeasureTheory.Integrable (Causalean.Stat.uProj h P) P` | The first projection is integrable whenever `x ↦ ∫ h(x, ·) dP` is. |
| `Stat.uDegen_integral_right_eq_zero` | `MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => ∫ (y : X), h x y ∂P) P → ∀ (x : X), MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun y => h x y) P → ∫ (y : X), Causalean.Stat.uDegen h P x y ∂P = 0` | Degeneracy of the second-order kernel. For every fixed `x`, `∫ g(x, ·) dP = 0`. This is the defining property that makes the U-statistic's quadratic remainder negligible at the `√n` scale. |

### 12x.8. `Stat/UStatistic/OrderM/FirstDegenKernel.lean` — first-order degenerate kernel

<!-- GEN:Causalean.Stat.UStatistic.OrderM.FirstDegenKernel -->
| Decl | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Stat.OrderFirstDegenKernel` | `MeasureTheory.Measure X → {m : ℕ} → [NeZero m] → ((Fin m → X) → ℝ) → Prop` | First-order degenerate order-`m` kernel. A kernel `g` on `m`-tuples over `X`, together with the population measure `P`, is first-order degenerate when `g` is measurable, its first Hoeffding projection vanishes in every coordinate — integrating `g` over the other $m-1$ coordinates against the product measure leaves zero, whichever coordinate and value are held fixed, and `g` is square-integrable under the product measure $P^{\otimes m}$. |
| `Stat.OrderFirstDegenKernel.integrable` | `Causalean.Stat.OrderFirstDegenKernel P g → MeasureTheory.Integrable g (MeasureTheory.Measure.pi fun x => P)` | A first-order degenerate square-integrable kernel is integrable under the product law. |
| `Stat.OrderFirstDegenKernel.integral_eq_zero` | `Causalean.Stat.OrderFirstDegenKernel P g → Causalean.Stat.uMeanOrder g P = 0` | Population mean of a first-order degenerate kernel is zero. If the order-`m` kernel `g` is first-order degenerate: measurable, square-integrable under the `m`-fold product law, and with zero mean after integrating out all but any single coordinate, then the population mean of `g` under the `m`-fold product law is zero. |
<!-- /GEN -->

| `Stat.IIDSample.rescaled_order_normalization_le` | `m ≤ n → ∀ {ζ : ℝ}, 0 ≤ ζ → ↑n * (Causalean.Stat.injectiveTupleCount m n)⁻¹ ^ 2 * (↑(m.choose 2) * ↑m ^ 2 * ↑n ^ (2 * m - 2) * ζ) ≤ ↑(m.choose 2) * ↑m ^ (2 * m + 2) * ζ / ↑n` | For a nonnegative second-moment bound and a sample size at least the kernel order, the falling-factorial normalization term is bounded by a constant divided by the sample size. |
| `Stat.IIDSample.integral_rescaled_order_sq_le` | `Causalean.Stat.OrderFirstDegenKernel P g → ∃ C, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ {n : ℕ}, m ≤ n → ∫ (ω : Ω), (√↑n * Causalean.Stat.uStatisticOrder S g n ω) ^ 2 ∂μ ≤ C / ↑n` | `L²` bound on the rescaled higher-order remainder. For an i.i.d. sample `S`, if the order-`m` kernel `g` is first-order degenerate, then there is a nonnegative constant `C`, depending only on the order `m` and the kernel's second moment `ζ_m = E[g²]`, such that the second moment of the `√n`-rescaled order-`m` U-statistic of `g` is at most `C/n` for every sample size `n ≥ m`. This is the keystone estimate; it packages cross-term vanishing, the Cauchy–Schwarz bound `\|E[g_t g_q]\| ≤ ζ_m`, the `O(n^{2m-2})` count of surviving tuple pairs, and the `n · (n^{(m)})⁻²` normalization. |

## 12wo. `Stat/PolynomialTail/` — Polynomial lower-tail inverse-moment asymptotics

Causal-agnostic real-analysis / measure-theory infrastructure for the small-value
(lower-tail) asymptotics of a bounded positive random variable.  This is the moment
calculus underlying *any* inverse-weighted estimand whose weight is floored at `1/λ` —
not tied to one paper.  It specializes to (and quantitatively refines) the qualitative
`Overlap`/positivity assumption in `Identification/`: taking `U = min(e(X), 1−e(X))`
recovers the variance/rate ingredients of IPW, AIPW, and Hájek estimators under thin
overlap, trimming/truncation bias, and weak-overlap minimax rates.  Fix a probability
measure `P` and a measurable `U : Ω → ℝ` with `0 < U ≤ 1` a.s.  The two-sided
polynomial lower-tail hypothesis `PolyTail P U κ t₀ cm cp` says
`cm·tᵏ ≤ P{U ≤ t} ≤ cp·tᵏ` on `(0,t₀]` (`0 < κ`, `0 < t₀ < 1`, `0 < cm < cp`).  The
library bounds the two truncated inverse moments (`λ`-truncation, `0 < λ ≤ t₀`)

    I P U λ = ∫ U/(max U λ)²   (= 1/U on {U≥λ}, U/λ² on {U<λ}),
    J P U λ = ∫ (max U λ)⁻¹    (= 1/U on {U≥λ}, 1/λ  on {U<λ}),

and the leftover trimming weight `wλ = 1 − U/(max U λ) ∈ [0,1]` (supported on `{U<λ}`).
The key trichotomy is in the tail exponent `κ`: `λ^{κ-1}` (κ<1), `log(1/λ)` (κ=1),
bounded (κ>1).  The lower bounds genuinely use **both** tail constants (the gap
`cm < cp` breaks any one-sided argument).  Method: Mathlib's layer-cake theorem
`MeasureTheory.Integrable.integral_eq_integral_Ioc_meas_le` reduces `J` to a
threshold integral of `P{U ≤ t⁻¹}`, evaluated against `∫ t^{-κ}` (`integral_rpow` /
`integral_inv`).  All declarations **sorry-free and axiom-clean**.

### 12wo.1. `Stat/PolynomialTail/Basic.lean` — setup, integrands, basic facts

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PolyTail P U κ t₀ cm cp` | `structure : Prop` | The polynomial lower-tail hypothesis: `cm·tᵏ ≤ P{U≤t} ≤ cp·tᵏ` on `(0,t₀]`, with `0<κ`, `0<t₀<1`, `0<cm<cp`. Fields `kappa_pos/t0_pos/t0_lt_one/cm_pos/cm_lt_cp/tail_lower/tail_upper`. |
| `PolyTail.cp_pos` | `0 < cp` | Upper constant positive. |
| `TailSetup P U` | `structure : Prop` | Structural hypotheses on `U`: `Measurable U`, `0 < U` a.s., `U ≤ 1` a.s. |
| `truncDen U λ ω` | `def := max (U ω) λ` | Truncated denominator. |

## 12'. `Stat/Concentration/` — Vendored concentration toolbox (Phase-4a)

Selectively vendored from
[auto-res/lean-rademacher](https://github.com/auto-res/lean-rademacher)
(commit `72d28921dc960f47691640fb973303a1be9d13ca`, MIT License). Audit
trail and porting policy live in
[Causalean/Stat/Concentration/UPSTREAM.md](../Causalean/Stat/Concentration/UPSTREAM.md).
Phase 4a covers definitions and the headline statements only; lower-level
proof chains are scaffolded with `sorry` and filled by Codex in a
separate pass.

#### 12'.0 `Stat/Concentration/Chebyshev.lean`

Plain single-measure Chebyshev in the form call sites want: a *variance bound* and a supplied mean give a real-valued probability bound on the deviation event. Distinct from `iid_sum_chebyshev` (§12'.f'-adjacent, in `Matrix/IidSums.lean`), which is the i.i.d.-*sum* form with an exact variance and an `ENNReal` conclusion.

<!-- GEN:Causalean.Stat.Concentration.Chebyshev -->
| Decl | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Stat.Concentration.probability_abs_sub_mean_gt_le` | `MeasureTheory.MemLp F 2 Q → 0 < a → ∫ (x : Ω), F x ∂Q = mean → ProbabilityTheory.variance F Q ≤ v → (Q {x \| a < \|F x - mean\|}).toReal ≤ v / a ^ 2` | For a finite measure `Q` and a statistic `F` on the underlying space, if `F` is square-integrable under `Q`, the deviation threshold `a` is positive, `F` has mean equal to `mean` under `Q`, and the variance of `F` under `Q` is at most the envelope `v`, then the probability that `F` deviates from `mean` by more than `a` in absolute value is at most `v/a²`. |
<!-- /GEN -->

#### 12'.a' `Stat/Concentration/ERMOracle.lean` — generic ERM oracle inequality

The method-agnostic learning-theory rate: empirical risk minimization over a countable
hypothesis class with bounded loss has excess risk controlled by the Rademacher complexity of
the loss class plus a McDiarmid tail. The engine that turns a complexity bound for a specific
method's class into a concrete excess-risk rate.

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `erm_excess_le_two_uniformDeviation` | `theorem` | **Deterministic ERM basic inequality:** an empirical minimizer beating a comparator on the sample has excess population risk `≤ 2·uniformDeviation`. **Proved.** |
| `erm_oracle_inequality` | `theorem` | **Oracle inequality:** `μⁿ{ 4·𝔯ₙ + 2ε < R(ĥ) − R(h⋆) } ≤ exp(−ε² t n)`, chaining the basic inequality with FoML's symmetrization + McDiarmid tail (`𝔯ₙ` = Rademacher complexity of the loss class). **Proved.** |
| `erm_oracle_inequality_separable` | `theorem` | Separable-class version (`SeparableSpace`/`FirstCountableTopology ι`, loss continuous in the parameter) — the form that applies to the uncountable-but-separable L²/L¹-ball linear classes (kernel, lasso). **Proved.** |

#### 12'.e4b `Stat/Concentration/HausslerPacking.lean`

Haussler-style finite-VC packing bounds for weighted Boolean Hamming metrics,
isolating the random-coordinate extraction core from the deterministic

| `weightedHammingSq_nonneg` | Nonnegative weights → `0 ≤ weightedHammingSq w a b` | Basic nonnegativity of the weighted Hamming pseudo-distance squared. |
| `card_subsample_family_le_succ_pow` | Restricted trace VC dimension at most `d` → restricted trace cardinality at most `(m + 1)^d` | Applies Sauer-Shelah and a binomial-sum bound to a sampled coordinate family. |
| `subsample_image_vcDim_le` | Original true-set family VC dimension at most `d` → every coordinate restriction has VC dimension at most `d` | Shows restriction along any coordinate map cannot increase VC dimension. |
| `finite_averaging_exists_separating_subsample` | Total weight at most `r²`, `ε²`-separation, `2 ≤ #P`, and `0 < ε ≤ r` → a separating restricted trace with `m ≤ 1 + (2*r²/ε²)*log #P` | Isolates the finite product-sum averaging step for the random-coordinate extraction; currently the remaining `sorry` in this module. |
| `exists_separating_subsample` | VC control, total weight at most `r²`, `ε²`-separation, `2 ≤ #P`, and `0 < ε ≤ r` → a separating restricted trace with `m ≤ 1 + (2*r²/ε²)*log #P` and restricted VC dimension at most `d` | Combines finite averaging with VC-dimension preservation for sampled coordinate families. |
| `self_log_solve` | `L ≤ d*log(2 + a*L)` with `d ≥ 1`, `a ≥ 2`, and `L ≥ 0` → an explicit `1 + 2*d*log(2*a*d)` bound | Scalar self-logarithm inequality used after Sauer-Shelah. |
| `vc_weightedHamming_packing_card_le` | VC control, total weight at most `r²`, and `ε²`-separation → `log #P ≤ 1 + 2*d*log(4*d*r²/ε²)` | Logarithmic Haussler ε-packing bound with no dependence on the ambient coordinate count, modulo the isolated extraction lemma. |
| `vc_weightedHamming_log_packing_le` | Same hypotheses → `log #P ≤ 1 + 2*d*log(4*d*r²/ε²)` | Alias for the clean logarithmic weighted VC packing bound. |

#### 12'.e4be `Stat/Concentration/Covering/EuclideanRadialPolynomial/` — moving-center radial classes

Finite-trace semialgebraic certificates for compactly supported Euclidean
radial monomials, including odd powers, atomic boundary mass, finite signed
arms, shared-center boxed polynomials, and bounded residual scores.  The
resulting polynomial `L²(Q)` covers are uniform over every probability law.

#### 12'.e4bf `Stat/Concentration/VarianceAdaptiveVCExpectedMaximal/` — variance-adaptive VC-type expected suprema

For a countable measurable real-valued class, this module combines empirical
L² covers, Dudley chaining, localization, and symmetrization.  Its main bound
retains the population L² radius in the leading term and needs no separate
measurability assumption for a continuum supremum.

<!-- GEN:Causalean.Stat.Concentration.VarianceAdaptiveVCExpectedMaximal.Basic -->
| Decl | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|

| `Stat.Concentration.HasPolynomialEmpiricalL2Cover.enlargeEnvelope` | `Causalean.Stat.Concentration.HasPolynomialEmpiricalL2Cover F U A v → U ≤ V → Causalean.Stat.Concentration.HasPolynomialEmpiricalL2Cover F V A v` | Enlarging the envelope of an empirical polynomial cover preserves its entropy witnesses. |

The replacement centers are chosen inside the restricted class. |

| `Stat.Concentration.vcExpectedMaximalRate` | `ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℕ → ℝ` | The variance-adaptive VC-type rate is the sum of a leading `σ √(v log(AU/σ)/n)` term and a second-order `v U log(AU/σ)/n` term, with a logarithm normalized to be at least one. |

#### 12'.e4c `Stat/Concentration/VCLocalizedCovering.lean`

Metric bridges connecting binary-factored real classes with the weighted
Boolean Hamming geometry used in localized finite-VC covering arguments.

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `empiricalDist_sq_eq_weightedHammingSq` | Binary factorization `F i (S j) = φ j (π i (S j))` → squared empirical L² distance equals weighted Hamming squared distance with weights `(φ j true − φ j false)²/n` | Converts empirical metric separation for a binary-factored real class into weighted Boolean trace separation on the same sample. |

#### 12'.e5 `Stat/Concentration/VCLocalizedRegime.lean`

Localized finite-VC Rademacher regime used by the sharp localized uniform
deviation layer.  The elementary sub-root and critical-radius algebra is proved
directly.  The remaining Massart finite-realization construction is isolated as
an explicit analytic sublemma rather than packaged as a hypothesis field.

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `BinaryFactoredVCClass` | Real-valued class `F` factors through a Boolean class whose sample growth family has VC dimension at most `d` | Packages the binary trace substrate used by VC covering arguments. |
| `BinaryTraceEntropyControl` | Either samplewise VC-dimension control or direct `(m + 1)^d` growth-cardinality control | Common entropy input for the localized star-hull theorem. |
| `LocalizedVCDudleyHypotheses` | Empirical radius and total boundedness fields | Deterministic hypothesis bundle for the sample-path localized Dudley step. |
| `localizedVCDudleyHypotheses_of_empiricalRadius` | Bounded binary-factored finite-VC class plus an explicit samplewise empirical-radius bridge → `LocalizedVCDudleyHypotheses` | Constructor for the localized Dudley hypothesis bundle. For population L² localization norms, the empirical-radius bridge remains a real extra obligation; boundedness alone does not give deterministic empirical-radius control on every sample. |
| `starHullZeroOut_empirical_rademacher_massart_vc` | Binary trace entropy + localized hypotheses → Massart finite-realization bound with rate `r * sqrt((2 d log(n+1)+2)/n)` | Isolates the remaining analytic finite-pattern Massart construction. |
| `absolute_dudley_vc_starHullZeroOut_linear_residual_shared` | Same localized star-hull bound with either VC-dimension or direct growth-cardinality trace control, assuming `K ≥ 1` | Shared residual used by the downstream VC localized bounds. |
| `vcLocalizedRademacherUpperBound` | Binary-factored finite-VC class + localized hypotheses → local Rademacher upper bound and critical-radius rate | Headline localized finite-VC Rademacher envelope. |
| `vcLocalizedEnvelope` | Finite-VC localized assumptions → `localized_uniform_deviation_sharp` envelope | Connects the finite-VC Rademacher regime to the localized uniform-deviation theorem. |

#### 12'.g `Stat/Concentration/SubExponential.lean`

Sub-exponential MGF framework mirroring Mathlib's sub-Gaussian design, in the
`(v, b)` parameterization (validity interval encoded as `b·|t| < 1`, so `b = 0`
recovers the sub-Gaussian/all-`t` case). All declarations **proved, sorry-free,
axiom-clean**.

| `HasSubexponentialMGF.neg` | `lemma` | Closure under negation (same `(v,b)`). |

| `HasSubexponentialMGF.const_mul` | `lemma` | Scaling `r·X` has parameters `(r²v, |r|b)`. |

#### 12'.i `Stat/Concentration/Bernstein.lean`

Bernstein's inequality routed through the constant-`v` sub-exponential framework.
**Fully proved and `sorry`-free** (all four declarations are axiom-clean:
`propext`/`Classical.choice`/`Quot.sound` only). The earlier power-series blocker
is avoided entirely: the sub-exponential packaging only needs the MGF bound on
the validity interval `c|t| < 1`, where `|tX| ≤ 1` a.e. lets the elementary
pointwise bound `exp u ≤ 1 + u + u²` integrate term-by-term.

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `exp_le_one_add_add_sq` | `lemma` | Pointwise `exp u ≤ 1 + u + u²` for `|u| ≤ 1`; a real corollary of `Real.norm_exp_sub_one_sub_id_le`. **Proved.** |
| `bounded_mgf_le_exp_sq` | `lemma` | For mean-zero `X`, `|X| ≤ c`, `E[X²] ≤ σ²`: `mgf X μ t ≤ exp(σ²t²)` when `c|t| ≤ 1`. Integrates the pointwise bound using `E[X]=0`, `E[X²]≤σ²`. **Proved.** |
| `bounded_hasSubexponentialMGF` | `lemma` | A bounded mean-zero variable is sub-exponential with parameters `(2σ², c)` (note `2σ²·t²/2 = σ²t²`). **Proved.** |
| `bernstein_ge` | `theorem` | One-sided Bernstein: `P(X̄ₙ − E[f] ≥ ε) ≤ exp(−n ε² / (2(2σ² + cε)))`. From `bounded_hasSubexponentialMGF` + independent-sum + Chernoff. **Proved.** |
| `bernstein_abs_ge` | `theorem` | Two-sided Bernstein: `P(|X̄ₙ − E[f]| ≥ ε) ≤ 2·exp(−n ε² / (2(2σ² + cε)))`. **Proved.** |

> **Constant note.** The variance enters with proxy `2σ²` and the scale is `c`
> (so the tail is `exp(−nε²/(2(2σ²+cε)))`). The sharper textbook constant
> `exp(−nε²/(2(σ²+cε/3)))` is *not* attainable through the constant-`v`
> sub-exponential structure — it needs a Bernstein-specific Chernoff optimisation
> on the denominator-form MGF — and was deliberately traded for this cleaner,
> looser constant. The `c|t| < 1` validity interval forces the scale `b ≥ c`, so
> `b = c` is optimal for this route.

#### 12'.j `Stat/Concentration/ConfidenceInterval.lean`

Inverts the two-sided Hoeffding and Bernstein tails (12'.f, 12'.i) into explicit
*finite-sample* confidence half-widths. For a confidence level `δ ∈ (0,1]` and
sample size `n`, each result gives a half-width `w(n,δ)` such that the population
mean `m = ∫ f ∂P` is covered by the random interval `[X̄ₙ − w, X̄ₙ + w]` with
probability `≥ 1 − δ`. Both a miss-probability form (`P(w ≤ |X̄ₙ − m|) ≤ δ`) and
its coverage complement are provided. Holds at every fixed `n`, unlike the
asymptotic Wald interval. **Fully proved and `sorry`-free.**

| Declaration | Signature | Description | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hoeffdingCIHalfWidth` | `(a b : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (δ : ℝ) : ℝ` | Hoeffding half-width `(b−a)·√(log(2/δ)/(2n))` for an `[a,b]`-valued statistic. | **Proved** (def) |
| `bernsteinCIHalfWidth` | `(c σ : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (δ : ℝ) : ℝ` | Variance-adaptive Bernstein half-width `2σ·√(log(2/δ)/n) + 2c·(log(2/δ)/n)`; leading term scales with `σ`. | **Proved** (def) |
| `hoeffding_ci_miss` | `… : μ.real {ω | hoeffdingCIHalfWidth a b n δ ≤ |X̄ₙ − m|} ≤ δ` | Miss bound: the mean falls outside the Hoeffding interval w.p. `≤ δ`. Inverts `hoeffding_abs_ge`. | **Proved** |
| `bernstein_ci_miss` | `… : μ.real {ω | bernsteinCIHalfWidth c σ n δ ≤ |X̄ₙ − m|} ≤ δ` | Miss bound for the variance-adaptive Bernstein interval; exact quadratic-slack inversion of `bernstein_abs_ge`. | **Proved** |
| `hoeffding_ci_cover` | `… : 1 − δ ≤ μ.real {ω | |X̄ₙ − m| < hoeffdingCIHalfWidth a b n δ}` | Coverage complement of `hoeffding_ci_miss`. | **Proved** |
| `bernstein_ci_cover` | `… : 1 − δ ≤ μ.real {ω | |X̄ₙ − m| < bernsteinCIHalfWidth c σ n δ}` | Coverage complement of `bernstein_ci_miss`. | **Proved** |

#### 12'.k `Stat/Concentration/EmpiricalBernstein.lean`

Sample-variance infrastructure plus an **elementary, fully rigorous** data-driven
("empirical") Bernstein confidence interval. The full Maurer–Pontil bound is out
of scope; instead the population variance `σ² = ∫(f−m)²` is bounded above by the
*observed* sample variance `V̂ₙ` plus a deterministic slack `τ` (via two Hoeffding
deviations — one for `f`, one for `f²` — at level `δ/2` each), and `σ ≤ √(V̂ₙ+τ)`
is fed into the Bernstein half-width using monotonicity in `σ`. Constants are
looser than Maurer–Pontil's (the second-moment Hoeffding step is wasteful) but
every step is elementary. **Fully proved and `sorry`-free** (axiom-clean:
`propext`/`Classical.choice`/`Quot.sound` only).

The explicit slack (with `M := max |a| |b|`, `d := √(log(4/δ)/(2n))`) is
`τ = M²·d + 2 M (b−a)·d`.

| Declaration | Signature | Description | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `IIDSample.sampleVariance` | `(S : IIDSample Ω X μ P) (f : X → ℝ) (n : ℕ) : Ω → ℝ` | Biased (`1/n`-normalised) empirical variance `(1/n) ∑_{i<n} (f(Zᵢ ω) − X̄ₙ(ω))²` (in namespace `Causalean.Stat` for dot-notation). | **Proved** (def) |
| `IIDSample.sampleVariance_nonneg` | `… (ω) : 0 ≤ S.sampleVariance f n ω` | The sample variance is nonnegative (a scaled sum of squares). | **Proved** |
| `IIDSample.measurable_sampleVariance` | `(hf : Measurable f) (n) : Measurable (S.sampleVariance f n)` | The sample variance is measurable in the sample point `ω`. | **Proved** |
| `IIDSample.sampleVariance_eq` | `… (ω) : S.sampleVariance f n ω = (n:ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ i ∈ range n, (f (Z i ω))^2 − (X̄ₙ ω)^2` | Computational form: empirical second moment minus squared empirical mean. | **Proved** |
| `empiricalVarianceSlack` | `(a b : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (δ : ℝ) : ℝ` | The deterministic slack `τ = M²·d + 2M(b−a)·d` (`M = max|a||b|`, `d = √(log(4/δ)/(2n))`). | **Proved** (def) |
| `empirical_variance_concentration` | `(hf) (hab : a<b) (hbound : f∈[a,b] a.e.) (n) (hn) (hδ0) (hδ1) : μ.real {ω | V̂ₙ + τ < σ²} ≤ δ` | Data-driven variance bound: w.p. `≥ 1−δ`, `σ² ≤ V̂ₙ + empiricalVarianceSlack a b n δ`. Union of two level-`δ/2` Hoeffding events (for `f` and `f²`) plus a null set for the a.e. `|X̄ₙ| ≤ M` bound. | **Proved** |
| `empiricalBernsteinCIHalfWidth` | `(S) (f) (a b c : ℝ) (n) (δ) : Ω → ℝ` | Data-driven half-width: `bernsteinCIHalfWidth` with oracle `σ` replaced by the observed `√(V̂ₙ(ω) + τ)`. | **Proved** (def) |
| `empirical_bernstein_ci_miss` | `(hf) (hab) (hbound_ab) (hc : 0≤c) (hbound : |f−m|≤c a.e.) (hposvar : 0<σ²) (n) (hn) (hδ0) (hδ1) : μ.real {ω | empiricalBernsteinCIHalfWidth S f a b c n δ ω ≤ |X̄ₙ − m|} ≤ 2δ` | Data-driven Bernstein CI miss bound: the mean falls outside the observed-variance interval w.p. `≤ 2δ`. Unions the oracle Bernstein miss (`σ=√σ²`) with the variance-bound failure, using monotonicity of the width in `σ` on the good event. | **Proved** |

## 12g. `Estimation/OrthogonalMoments/` — Abstract DML estimation and inference framework

Generic moment-functional layer that consolidates the DML asymptotic-linearity
machinery so any concrete instance (currently AIPW) reduces to instantiating
the abstract structure. Mirrors `doc/basic_concepts/po/estimation/dml_ate.tex`
generalised away from AIPW-specific algebra.

### 12g.1 `Estimation/OrthogonalMoments/MomentFunctional.lean`

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `GeneralMoment Ω μ Z P_Z H` | structure | Abstract bundle: moment functional `m : H → Z → ℝ → ℝ`, truth `η₀ : H`, target `θ₀ : ℝ`, perturbation set `H_ε ⊆ H`, bilinear seminorms `(ρ₁, ρ₂) : H → H → NNReal`, joint measurability of `m _ · _`, and `η₀ ∈ H_ε`. |
| `GeneralMoment.J₀` | field, `ℝ` | Jacobian `∂_θ ∫ m(η₀, z, θ) dP_Z |_{θ=θ₀}` of the population moment. Scalar form (vector-θ generalisation deferred). For AIPW (linear score `m = ψ − θ`), `J₀ = −1`. |
| `GeneralMoment.J₀_ne_zero` | field, `Prop` | Non-singularity witness; ensures `J₀_inv` is well-defined. |
| `GeneralMoment.J₀_inv` | `noncomputable def` | `J₀⁻¹`. **Proved.** |
| `GeneralMoment.J₀_mul_J₀_inv` | `lemma`, `@[simp]` | `J₀ * J₀_inv = 1`. **Proved.** |
| `MeanZero M` | `Prop` | `∫ z, M.m M.η₀ z M.θ₀ ∂P_Z = 0`. |
| `H_ε_PerturbClosed M` | `Prop` | `M.H_ε` is closed under convex combinations between `η₀` and `η ∈ H_ε`. |

##### `LinearMoment` (linear-score extension)

Extension of `GeneralMoment` carrying the decomposition `m η z θ = m_a η z * θ + m_b η z` (Chernozhukov 2018 Thm 3.1 "linear score" form). AIPW is the canonical instance with `m_a η z = -1` and `m_b η z = ψ_AIPW(η, z)`, giving `J₀ = -1`.

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `LinearMoment` | structure (extends `GeneralMoment`) | Adds `m_a`, `m_b`, measurability, decomposition `m_decomp`, and consistency `J₀_eq : J₀ = ∫ m_a η₀ z dP_Z`. |

### 12g.2 `Estimation/OrthogonalMoments/DirectionalDeriv.lean`

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `HasDirDeriv M` | structure | Pointwise directional derivative data: function `dM : H → Z → ℝ`, pointwise `Tendsto` witness for the difference quotient along the segment `η₀ → η`, and measurability of `dM η`. |

| Declaration | Statement | Description |

| `integratedMoment_diffQuotient_tendsto_zero` | `theorem` | DCT bridge: `NeymanOrthogonal` + `DiffQuotientEnvelope` ⇒ integrated difference quotient → 0 along `𝓝[≠] 0`. **Proved** (forward-compat; not on AIPW path). |

### 12g.5. `Estimation/OrthogonalMoments/DMLChernozhukov.lean`

Classical Chernozhukov-form DML theorem; conclusion uses IF `−J₀⁻¹ · m(η₀, ·, θ₀)` and asymptotic variance `J₀⁻¹ Σ J₀⁻ᵀ`. Matches Chernozhukov et al. 2018 Thm 3.1 / 3.2. The earlier zero-centered `dml_asymptoticLinear` (`Estimation/OrthogonalMoments/DML.lean`) was deleted on 2026-05-08 since AIPW migrated and no other instance used it.

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `dmlChernozhukovEstimator M sample split η_hat` | `noncomputable def` | One-step Chernozhukov estimator: `θ̂_n := θ₀ − J₀⁻¹ · Pₙ_B m(η̂, ·, θ₀)`. Reduces to `(1/|B|) Σ ψ(η̂, Z_i)` for AIPW (J₀ = −1). |
| `dml_chernozhukov_asymptoticLinear` | `theorem` | Asymptotic linearity of `dmlChernozhukovEstimator` at `M.θ₀` with IF `−J₀⁻¹ · m(η₀, ·, θ₀)`, indexed over `split.foldB`. **Proved by Codex** (G+B decomposition with the Chernozhukov-form score `m(η̂, ·, θ₀)` and a `−J₀⁻¹` constant-multiplication wrapper; bundled an inline `const_mul_isLittleOp_one` helper). **API refactored 2026-05-06:** dropped the `D : HasDirDeriv M`, `_hNO : NeymanOrthogonal M D`, and `_h_in_Hε : ∀ n ω, η_hat n ω ∈ M.H_ε` parameters; replaced the ∀-quantified `_hBR : BilinearRemainder M Crem` with the per-η̂_n bound `_hBR_at : ∀ n ω, |∫ z, M.m (η_hat n ω) z M.θ₀ ∂P_Z| ≤ Crem · ρ₁(η̂_n, η₀) · ρ₂(η̂_n, η₀)`. Net effect: instances supply only what they actually need (orthogonality is implicit in the per-η̂_n bound), removing the artificial ∀-over-`H_ε` hypothesis. **Further trimmed 2026-05-09:** dropped the unused `_hc_lt : c < 1`, `_h_indiv_rate_ρ₁`, `_h_indiv_rate_ρ₂` parameters (all discarded in the body — the abstract proof needs only the product rate); callers (`AIPWInstance`, `AutoDebias.DML`) keep them at their own level when needed locally. |

### 12g.5'. `Estimation/OrthogonalMoments/DMLCrossFit.lean`

K-fold cross-fitted version of `dml_chernozhukov_asymptoticLinear`. Same Chernozhukov form, K folds, score evaluated independently of nuisance training fold per Chernozhukov et al. 2018 §3.2. Concludes asymptotic linearity at the **full-sample** index `Finset.range n` (the K fold-k sub-aggregations are reweighted into a `(1/√n)`-normalised sum modulo `o_p(1)`).

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `dmlCrossFitEstimator M sample split η_hat` | `noncomputable def` | K-fold averaged Chernozhukov estimator: `θ̂ := M.θ₀ − J₀⁻¹ · K⁻¹ · Σ_k \|fold n k\|⁻¹ · Σ_{i ∈ fold n k} m(η̂^{(-k)}, Z_i, θ₀)`. |
| `foldNormalizedSum_isBigOp` | private lemma | `(1/√\|fold n k\|) Σ_{i ∈ fold n k} ψ(Z_i) = O_p(1)` whenever `ψ` is mean-zero and `L²(P_Z)`. Markov + the abstract `iid_centered_sum_sq_lintegral_le` with trivial training σ-algebra `m_A = ⊥` (independence is automatic via `ProbabilityTheory.indep_bot_left`); mean-zero collapses centered = uncentered. **Proved.** |
| `foldNormalizedSumOverN_isBigOp` | private lemma | `(1/√n) Σ_{i ∈ fold n k} ψ(Z_i) = O_p(1)`. Bound by `foldNormalizedSum_isBigOp` × `√(\|fold n k\|/n)` (the latter is bounded eventually via `split.cover` + `split.partition` giving `(fold n k).card ≤ n`). **Proved.** |
| `dml_crossFit_asymptoticLinear` | `theorem` | Asymptotic linearity of `dmlCrossFitEstimator` at `M.θ₀` with IF `−J₀⁻¹ · m(η₀, ·, θ₀)`, indexed over `fun n => Finset.range n`. Hypotheses: per-fold measurability/integrability (`_h_m_meas`, `_h_m_train`, `_h_m_train_uncurry`, `_h_m_int`, `_h_m_sq_int`), per-fold score-difference rate (`_h_score_diff_rate k`), per-(n,k,ω) bilinear remainder bound `_hBR_at`, individual ρ-rates, product rate, and `_hK_pos : 1 < K` (tightened from `0 < K` because the K-fold bias step needs `(K:ℝ)⁻¹ ∈ (0, 1)`; `K = 1` reduces to the one-shot estimator and is out of scope). Proof structure: `mean_zero` and `finite_var` by constant-rescaling of `MeanZero M` / `_hFV`; the `remainder` decomposes into `h_fold_centered` + `h_fold_bias` (per-fold, lifted from the OneShot proof in `DMLChernozhukov.lean` via `KFoldSplit.fold_centered_sum_isLittleOp_one` and an inline bias derivation analogous to OneShot `hB`) and `h_full_reweighting` (the cover/partition + ratio rescaling). The reweighting step uses `IsBigOp.const_mul_tendsto_zero` for the weight-discrepancy "ratio piece" and `IsBigOp.mul_isLittleOp_one_isLittleOp` for the "score piece"; finite K-fold sum closed via a small inline `IsLittleOp` finite-Finset additivity helper. **Proved by Codex (A5).** **API refactored 2026-05-09:** mirrors the OneShot 2026-05-06 refactor — dropped the `D : HasDirDeriv M`, `_hNO : NeymanOrthogonal M D`, `_h_in_Hε`, and ∀-quantified `_hBR : BilinearRemainder M Crem` parameters; replaced by the per-(n,k,ω) bound `_hBR_at`. |

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `aipwGeneralMoment S h_e_pointwise` | `noncomputable def` | AIPW realization of `GeneralMoment` with `ρ₁ η η' = ‖Δμ_T‖_{L²(P_X)} + ‖Δμ_F‖_{L²(P_X)}`, `ρ₂ η η' = ‖Δe‖_{L²(P_X)}`, `H_ε = ATE.H_ε ε`. |
| `aipwGeneralMoment.J₀`, `J₀_ne_zero` | fields | AIPW Jacobian `J₀ = −1` (linear score `m = ψ − θ`). |

| `aipw_bilinearRem` | `theorem` | `aipw_remainder_bound` reshaped into `BilinearRemainder` via `Fintype.sum_bool` distribution. **Proved.** |
| `aipw_dml_isAsymLinear` | `theorem` | Headline AIPW DML AL, retargeted to use `dml_chernozhukov_asymptoticLinear`. Conclusion: `IsAsymLinear (dmlChernozhukovEstimator (aipwGeneralMoment S _) _ _ _) S.θ₀ (fun z => −J₀_inv · aipwMomentFunctional S.η₀ z S.θ₀)`. **Refactored 2026-05-06:** dropped the ∀-quantified `h_L2 : ∀ η ∈ H_ε ε, …` hypothesis (and the `hε_pos` / `hε_le` extracts that only fed the now-removed `aipw_neymanOrthog` / `aipwHasDirDeriv` calls). Now takes per-η̂_n L²: `h_mu_diff_memLp : ∀ n ω a, MemLp (μ̂(n,ω,a) − μ_val a) 2 P_X` and `h_e_diff_memLp : ∀ n ω, MemLp (ê(n,ω) − e_val) 2 P_X`. Body builds the per-η̂_n bilinear remainder bound directly via `aipw_remainder_bound` (followed by `Fintype.sum_bool` to align with the `ρ₁ · ρ₂ = (‖Δμ_T‖ + ‖Δμ_F‖) · ‖Δe‖` shape) and feeds it as `_hBR_at` to the refactored abstract theorem. The Gâteaux-derivative `aipwHasDirDeriv` / `aipw_neymanOrthog` wrappers (and the underlying `Neyman.lean` / `NeymanAux/` machinery) are no longer on the AL critical path and were archived to `Estimation/ATE/Archived/` on 2026-05-06. **Proved.** |

### 12g.7. `Estimation/OrthogonalMoments/Riesz.lean`

Riesz representer pattern for linear-in-γ functionals (ATE, policy value, average derivative). Light skeleton; concrete instances live next to their estimators.

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `RieszRepresentation H_γ γ_target L P_X` | structure | A Riesz representer `α₀ : X → ℝ` with `representation : ∀ γ, L γ = ∫ x, α₀ x · γ x ∂P_X`, plus measurability and L¹ witnesses. |
| `rieszScore γ_target L proj_X Y_obs γ α θ z` | `noncomputable def` | The Riesz orthogonal score `m(z; θ, γ, α) := L γ + α(proj_X z) · (Y_obs z − γ_target γ (proj_X z)) − θ`. |
| `rieszScore_meanZero` | `theorem` | Under the regression-orthogonality assumption `∫ z, α₀(proj_X z)·(Y_obs z − γ_target γ₀ (proj_X z)) ∂P_Z = 0`, the population score at the truth `(γ₀, α₀, L γ₀)` integrates to zero. **Proved.** |
| `rieszScore_bilinearRem` | `theorem` | Bilinear remainder identity: `∫ z, m(z; L γ₀, γ, α) ∂P_Z − ∫ z, m(z; L γ₀, γ₀, α₀) ∂P_Z = − ∫ x, (α x − α₀ x)·(γ_target γ x − γ_target γ₀ x) ∂P_X` under pushforward `P_X = P_Z.map proj_X`, dual regression-orthogonality, integrability of the perturbed residual, and integrability of the four product terms. **Proved.** |

### 12g.8. `Estimation/OrthogonalMoments/Parametric.lean`

Parametric (no-nuisance) specialisation of `GeneralMoment` (`H = Unit`). With `H = Unit`, the abstract `dmlChernozhukovEstimator` collapses to the classical parametric one-step estimator and the rescaled remainder is identically zero. OLS, IV-2SLS, MLE instantiate this pattern.

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `parametricMoment m_par θ₀ J₀ hJ m_meas` | `noncomputable def` | Constructs `GeneralMoment Ω μ Z P_Z Unit` from a user-supplied moment `m_par : ℝ → Z → ℝ`, target `θ₀`, and Jacobian `J₀ ≠ 0`. Bilinear seminorms are zero (no nuisance to perturb). |
| `parametric_asymptoticLinear` | `theorem` | `IsAsymLinear (dmlChernozhukovEstimator (parametricMoment …) sample split (fun _ _ => ())) θ₀ (fun z => −J₀⁻¹ · m_par θ₀ z) sample split.foldB` from population mean-zero `∫ m_par(θ₀, ·) dP_Z = 0` and L²-finite `Integrable ((m_par θ₀)²) P_Z`. The remainder collapses identically: the parametric one-step estimator equals the influence-function partial sum exactly. **Proved.** |

### 12g.9. `Estimation/OrthogonalMoments/SecondStageOperator.lean`

Abstract second-stage regression operator and stability framework for the DR-Learner CATE estimator (Kennedy 2023). Operator-level / target-agnostic content: takes a real-valued pseudo-outcome `f : γ × Bool × ℝ → ℝ` and returns a real-valued estimate at a query point `x : γ`. No AIPW algebra, no causal content. Mirrors `def:est-cate-second-stage` and `def:est-cate-stability` in `doc/basic_concepts/po/estimation/dr_learner_cate.tex`.

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `SecondStageOperator Ω μ γ` | structure | Abstract bundle: `evalAt : ℕ → Ω → (γ × Bool × ℝ → ℝ) → γ → ℝ` taking sample size, randomness scope, pseudo-outcome, and query point; plus a minimal joint-measurability stub `meas_evalAt_const`. Linearity in input is left as a separate predicate `IsLinearInInput`. |
| `SecondStageOperator.IsLinearInInput op` | `Prop` | `evalAt n ω (f + g) x = evalAt n ω f x + evalAt n ω g x`. Linear smoothers satisfy this; tree mean estimators with random splits typically do not. |
| `SecondStageOperator.oracleEstimator op f` | `def` | Operator applied to a fixed "true" pseudo-outcome `f` (Kennedy's `\tilde\tau_n`). |
| `SecondStageOperator.oracleRiskScale op f target x n` | `noncomputable def`, `ℝ` | `R^*_n(x) := √(∫ ω, (op.evalAt n ω f x − target x)² ∂μ)`. Pointwise oracle risk scale. |
| `IsConditionalBias` | removed | The old placeholder `Prop` alias (`True`) was removed. Conditional-bias identification now enters through a caller-supplied `BiasIdent` predicate parameter on `Stable` and `oracle_expansion`. |
| `Stable op target d_n x BiasIdent` | `Prop` | Def 4 stability: for any `(fHat_n, f, bHat_n)` with `BiasIdent fHat_n f bHat_n`, `d_n →_p 0` implies the operator-level discrepancy `op.evalAt(fHat_n) − op.evalAt(f) − op.evalAt(bHat_n)` is `o_p(R^*_n(x))`. |
| `oracle_expansion` | `theorem` | Headline: under `Stable op target d_n x BiasIdent`, `Tendsto_inProb d_n 0`, and a `BiasIdent fHat_n f bHat_n` witness, the operator-level oracle expansion `op.evalAt(fHat_n) − op.evalAt(f) − op.evalAt(bHat_n) = o_p(R^*_n(x))` holds. **Proved by Codex** (one-line application of `Stable`). |

**Refactored 2026-05-09:** the placeholder `IsConditionalBias := True` was replaced by an explicit Prop predicate parameter `BiasIdent` that callers supply, restoring semantic content.

### 12g.10. `Estimation/OrthogonalMoments/LinearSmoother.lean`

Abstract weighted-Hölder bound for linear-smoother second-stage operators. Mirrors `prop:est-cate-linear-smoother-bound` in `doc/basic_concepts/po/estimation/dr_learner_cate.tex`.

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `LinearSmootherOp Ω μ γ` | structure (extends `SecondStageOperator`) | Adds `weights : ℕ → Ω → γ → (γ × Bool × ℝ) → ℝ`. The actual weighted-sum identity `evalAt n ω f x = Σ w · f(z_i)` is supplied as a separate predicate `IsLinearSmoother` rather than baked in. |
| `LinearSmootherOp.IsLinearSmoother op n ω x B w xs` | `Prop` | Predicate witnessing the weighted-sum identity `∀ f, op.evalAt n ω f x = Σ_{i ∈ B} w i · f (xs i)` for explicit weights `w : ι → ℝ` and data points `xs : ι → γ × Bool × ℝ`. |
| `WeightedNorm B w g p` | `noncomputable def`, `ℝ` | Weighted Lᵖ norm `(Σ_i ∈ B, |w i| / (Σ_j |w j|) · |g i|^p)^(1/p)`. Index type `ι` abstract; uses `Real.rpow`. |
| `WeightedNorm_nonneg` | `lemma` | Non-negativity of `WeightedNorm`. **Proved.** |
| `smoother_bias_holder` | `theorem` | `|op.evalAt n ω (fun z => g z.1) x| ≤ c_n · WeightedNorm B w (g ∘ xs.1) 1` under `IsLinearSmoother op n ω x B w xs` and `Σ |w| ≤ c_n`. **Proved by Codex** via triangle inequality + factor-out-`Σ|w|` rearrangement of the weighted-L¹ norm. |
| `smoother_bias_product_holder` | `theorem` | Hölder for `g = g₁·g₂`: `|op.evalAt n ω (fun z => g₁(z.1) · g₂(z.1)) x| ≤ c_n · ‖g₁ ∘ xs.1‖_{w,p} · ‖g₂ ∘ xs.1‖_{w,q}` under `IsLinearSmoother`, `Σ |w| ≤ c_n`, and `Real.HolderConjugate p q`. **Proved by Codex** via `Real.inner_le_Lp_mul_Lq_of_nonneg` applied to `f i := |w i|^{1/p} · |g₁ (xs i).1|`, `g i := |w i|^{1/q} · |g₂ (xs i).1|` with `1/p + 1/q = 1`. |

### 12g.11. `Estimation/OrthogonalMoments/AutoDebias/` — Automatic debiasing module

Reusable construction that converts any **linear-in-regression target** (or, more generally, any **regression-nuisance moment**) into a Neyman-orthogonal score by adding the Riesz-representer correction `α(X)·(Y − g(X))`. Mirrors `doc/basic_concepts/po/estimation/automatic_debiasing.tex`. The module contains an algebraic core (linear functional case), a general-moment layer, and a one-shot Auto-DML estimator with its asymptotic-linearity theorem.

#### 12g.11.a `Estimation/OrthogonalMoments/AutoDebias/Linear.lean` — Linear functional core

Defs 1, 3, 5 and Props 4, 6 of the tex.

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `LinRegFnSys` | structure | Linear regression-functional system: types `Z, X, H_γ` with measure/AddCommGroup/Module instances, `proj_X, Y_obs, γ_target` (linear in `H_γ`), observation-level linear-in-γ functional `m_lin : Z → H_γ → ℝ`, regression truth `g₀`, pushforward `P_X = P_Z.map proj_X`, and the integrated dual-orthogonality `regression_resid_orthog`. |
| `L_of_m S γ` | `noncomputable def` | Population linear functional `γ ↦ ∫ m_lin(z, γ) dP_Z`. |
| `L_of_m_add`, `L_of_m_smul` | `theorem`, `theorem` | Linearity of `L_of_m` in `γ` (under integrability). **Proved.** |
| `linRieszScore S γ α θ z` | `noncomputable def` | Alias of `rieszScore` from `Estimation.OrthogonalMoments.Riesz` specialised to a `LinRegFnSys`. |
| `linRieszScore_meanZero` | `theorem` | Population score at the truth `(g₀, α₀, L g₀)` integrates to zero (Prop 6, mean-zero). Wraps `rieszScore_meanZero` via `regression_resid_orthog`. **Proved.** |
| `linRieszScore_directional_g_zero` | `theorem` | Directional zero in the regression direction: `(∫ m_lin z ν_g dP_Z) − ∫ rep.α₀ · γ_target ν_g dP_X = 0` (Prop 6, part b). Direct from `rep.representation`. **Proved.** |
| `linRieszScore_directional_α_zero` | `theorem` | Directional zero in the representer direction: residual orthogonality of `ν_α` against `Y_obs − γ_target g₀` (Prop 6, part c). Direct call to `regression_resid_orthog`. **Proved.** |
| `linRieszLoss S α` | `noncomputable def` | Linear Riesz loss `∫ (γ_target α x)² dP_X − 2 · L_of_m S α` (Def 3). |
| `linRieszLoss_excess_eq_l2dist` | `theorem` | Prop 4, second half: `linRieszLoss α − linRieszLoss α₀_idx = ∫ (γ_target α − γ_target α₀_idx)² dP_X` when `rep.α₀ = γ_target α₀_idx` pointwise. Complete-the-square via `rep.representation`. **Proved.** |
| `linRieszLoss_FOC_iff_representer` | `theorem` | Prop 4, first half: `α₀_idx` is a directional minimizer of `linRieszLoss` along every line `α₀_idx + t • ν` iff `L(ν) = ∫ γ_target α₀_idx · γ_target ν dP_X` for every `ν`. Parabolic-identity FOC argument with quadratic-coefficient case split on `a = ∫ (γ_target ν)² dP_X`. **Proved.** |

Defs 8, 9, 10, 12, 13 and Prop 11 of the tex.

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `RegNuisanceMomentSys` | structure | Regression-nuisance moment system. Same data layer as `LinRegFnSys`; replaces the linear functional `m_lin` with a general moment `M : ℝ → H → ℝ` (kernel `m : H → Z → ℝ → ℝ`, `M_truth : M θ₀ g₀ = 0`, `m_population : M θ g = ∫ m g z θ dP_Z`) and a precomputed Gateaux derivative `D_g_M : H → ℝ` with linearity laws. |

Pure definition; intended target of future RieszNet-style analysis. |

#### 12g.11.c `Estimation/OrthogonalMoments/AutoDebias/DML.lean` — Auto-DML estimator and AL theorem

Def 6 and Thm 7 of the tex.

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `linAutoNuisance S` | `def` | Joint nuisance type `S.H_γ × (S.X → ℝ)` with componentwise `AddCommGroup` (`Prod.instAddCommGroup`) and `Module ℝ` (`Prod.instModule`). |
| `linAutoGeneralMoment μ S rep ε hε_nn h_score_meas` | `noncomputable def` | `GeneralMoment` instance over `linAutoNuisance S`. `m (γ, α) z θ := linRieszScore S γ α θ z`; `η₀ := (S.g₀, rep.α₀)`; `θ₀ := L_of_m S S.g₀`; `H_ε := { (γ, α) | ‖γ_target γ − γ_target g₀‖_{L²(P_X)} ≤ ε ∧ ‖α − α₀‖_{L²(P_X)} ≤ ε }`; `ρ₁`/`ρ₂` are the corresponding L² norms; `J₀ = −1`. The measurability witness `h_score_meas : ∀ η θ, Measurable (fun z => linRieszScore S η.1 η.2 θ z)` and non-negativity `hε_nn : 0 ≤ ε` are passed as parameters because `linAutoNuisance` does not internally constrain `α : X → ℝ` to be measurable. |

| `linAuto_bilinearRem` | `theorem` | Bilinear remainder bound: `\|∫ z, score η z θ₀ ∂P_Z\| ≤ C · ρ₁(η, η₀) · ρ₂(η, η₀)` for `η ∈ H_ε` with `linAuto_int_pred S rep η` and explicit `MemLp` witnesses for the two L²(P_X) differences. Proof factors via `rieszScore_bilinearRem` then applies Hölder-2 (`integral_mul_norm_le_Lp_mul_Lq`). **Proved.** |
| `linAutoDMLEstimator S rep ε hε_nn h_score_meas sample split η_hat` | `noncomputable def` | One-shot linear Auto-DML estimator (Def 6), built as `dmlChernozhukovEstimator (linAutoGeneralMoment μ S rep ε hε_nn h_score_meas) sample split η_hat`. Equivalently: `(1/\|B(n)\|) Σ_{i ∈ B(n)} [m_lin(Z_i; ĝ_n) + α̂_n(X_i)·(Y_i − ĝ_n(X_i))]`. |
| `linAutoDML_asymptoticLinear` | `theorem` | Thm 7 headline: `IsAsymLinear (linAutoDMLEstimator …) (L_of_m S S.g₀) (fun z => −J₀_inv · linRieszScore S S.g₀ rep.α₀ θ₀ z) sample split.foldB` under `MeanZero`, finite L² of the oracle score, per-η bilinear remainder, the standard fold-A measurability/integrability hypotheses, and the score-difference / individual / product rate hypotheses inherited from `dml_chernozhukov_asymptoticLinear`. Proof: direct composition. **Proved.** |

The module skips the ATE-equivalence remark from the tex (Remark 7) per design.

## 13'''. `Estimation/CATE/` — DR-Learner CATE estimation (Kennedy 2023)

Specific-system layer instantiating `BackdoorEstimationSystem` for the function-valued target `τ₀(x) = μ_val(true, x) − μ_val(false, x)`. Mirrors `doc/basic_concepts/po/estimation/dr_learner_cate.tex`. The DR-Learner is built on top of the same AIPW pseudo-outcome already used for ATE; the new content is (1) the function-valued target with `condDistrib`-style pointwise interpretation, (2) the DR conditional-bias identity (Prop 2 / `prop:est-cate-dr-bias-identity`, the milestone), and (3) the second-stage regression operator with stability hypothesis driving the oracle expansion (Theorem 5).

### 13'''.a `Estimation/CATE/Setup.lean`

| Declaration | Statement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `CATEEstimationSystem P γ` | structure (extends `BackdoorEstimationSystem`) | Empty extension — the CATE target `τ_val` is purely derived. All back-door substrate (consistency, exchangeability, overlap, integrability, `μ_val` / `e_val`, σ(X)-compatibility) is inherited. |

The DR conditional-bias identity. Pure σ(X)-conditional algebra; the closed-form cross-product remainder driving the double-robustness corollary (`rem:est-cate-double-robust`).
